2.1.s: devānāṃ vai ṣaḍ udgātāra āsan vāk ca manaś ca cakṣuś ca śrotraṃ cāpānaś ca prāṇaś ca |
2.1.d: देवानां वै षड् उद्गातार आसन् वाक् च मनश् च चक्षुश् च श्रोत्रं चापानश् च प्राणश् च ।
2.1.e: Of the gods there were six M%a<fflrs .• viz., speech and mind and sight and hearing and exhalation and breath.
2.1.m: The gods indeed had six udgātṛs: speech, mind, sight, hearing, the downward breath, and breath.

2.1.s: te 'dhriyanta tenodgātrā dīkṣāmahai yenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam iyāmeti |
2.1.d: ते ऽध्रियन्त तेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहै येनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् इयामेति ।
2.1.e: They resolved: " Let us consecrate ourselves with that udgdtar by whom, having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, we may go to the heavenly world."
2.1.m: They resolved: “Let us consecrate ourselves with that udgātṛ by whom, having struck away death, having struck away evil, we may go to the heavenly world.”

2.1.s: te 'bruvan vācodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti te vācodgātrādīkṣanta sa yad eva vācā vadati tad ātmana āgāyad atha ya itare kāmās tān devebhyaḥ |
2.1.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् वाचोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ते वाचोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त स यद् एव वाचा वदति तद् आत्मन आगायद् अथ य इतरे कामास् तान् देवेभ्यः ।
2.1.e: They said: " Let us consecrate ourselves with speech as udgdtar." They consecrated themselves with speech as udgdtar. What one speaks with speech, that it sang to itself; and what the other desires are, those [it sang] to the gods.
2.1.m: They said: “Let us consecrate ourselves with speech as the udgātṛ.” They consecrated themselves with speech as the udgātṛ. Whatever one speaks with speech, that he sang for himself, but whatever other desires there were, those [he sang] for the gods.

2.1.s: tām pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva vācā pāpaṃ vadati sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.1.d: ताम् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव वाचा पापं वदति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.1.e: Evil was created after it. What evil thing one speaks with speech, that is that evil.
2.1.m: Evil attached itself to it. Whatever evil one speaks with speech, that is that very evil.

2.1.s: te 'bruvan na vai no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt manasodgātrā dikṣāmahā iti |
2.1.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् न वै नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् मनसोद्गात्रा दिक्षामहा इति ।
2.1.e: They said: " Verily, this one hath not carried us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with the mind as udgdtar."
2.1.m: They said: “This one has indeed carried us beyond neither death nor evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with the mind as the udgātṛ.”

2.1.s: te manasodgātrādīkṣanta sa yad eva manasā dhyāyati tad ātmana āgāyad atha ya itare kāmās tān devebhyaḥ |
2.1.d: ते मनसोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त स यद् एव मनसा ध्यायति तद् आत्मन आगायद् अथ य इतरे कामास् तान् देवेभ्यः ।
2.1.e: They consecrated themselves with the mind as udgdtar. What one thinks with the mind, that it sang to itself; and what the other desires are, those [it sang] to the gods.
2.1.m: They consecrated themselves with the mind as the udgātṛ. Whatever one thinks with the mind, that he sang for himself, but whatever other desires there were, those [he sang] for the gods.

2.1.s: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva manasā pāpaṃ dhyāyati sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.1.d: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव मनसा पापं ध्यायति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.1.e: Evil was created after it. What evil thing one thinks with the mind, that is that evil.
2.1.m: Evil attached itself to it. Whatever evil one thinks with the mind, that is that very evil.

2.1.s: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt cakṣuṣodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.1.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् चक्षुषोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.1.e: They said: " Verily, this one hath not carried us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with sight as udgdtar.''''
2.1.m: They said: “This one has indeed carried us beyond neither death nor evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with sight as the udgātṛ.”

2.1.s: te cakṣuṣodgātrādīkṣanta sa yad eva cakṣuṣā paśyati tad ātmana āgāyad atha ya itare kāmās tān devebhyaḥ |
2.1.d: ते चक्षुषोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त स यद् एव चक्षुषा पश्यति तद् आत्मन आगायद् अथ य इतरे कामास् तान् देवेभ्यः ।
2.1.e: They consecrated themselves with sight as udgdtar. What one sees with sight, that it sang to itself; and what the other desires are, those [it sang] to the godis.
2.1.m: They consecrated themselves with sight as the udgātṛ. Whatever one sees with sight, that he sang for himself, but whatever other desires there were, those [he sang] for the gods.

2.1.s: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva cakṣuṣā pāpam paśyati |
2.1.d: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव चक्षुषा पापम् पश्यति ।
2.1.e: Evil was created after it. What evil thing one sees with sight [that is that evil].
2.1.m: Evil attached itself to it. Whatever evil one sees with sight, [that is that very evil].

2.1.s: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt śrotreṇodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.1.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् श्रोत्रेणोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.1.e: They said: "Verily, this one hath not carried us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with hearing as w<?Śa<ar."
2.1.m: They said: “This one has indeed carried us beyond neither death nor evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with hearing as the udgātṛ.”

2.1.s: te śrotreṇodgātrādīkṣanta sa yad eva śrotreṇa śṛṇoti tad ātmana āgāyad atha ya itare kāmās tān devebhyaḥ |
2.1.d: ते श्रोत्रेणोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त स यद् एव श्रोत्रेण शृणोति तद् आत्मन आगायद् अथ य इतरे कामास् तान् देवेभ्यः ।
2.1.e: They consecrated themselves with hearing as udgdtar. What one hears with hearing, that it sang to itself; and what the other desires are, those [it sang] to the gods.
2.1.m: They consecrated themselves with hearing as the udgātṛ. Whatever one hears with hearing, that he sang for himself, but whatever other desires there were, those [he sang] for the gods.

2.1.s: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva śrotreṇa pāpaṃ śṛṇoti sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.1.d: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव श्रोत्रेण पापं शृणोति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.1.e: Evil was created after it. What evil thing one hears with hearing, that is that evil.
2.1.m: Evil attached itself to it. Whatever evil one hears with hearing, that is that very evil.

2.1.s: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt apānenodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.1.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् अपानेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.1.e: They said: " Verily, this one hath not carried us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with exhalation as udgdtar."
2.1.m: They said: “This one has indeed carried us beyond neither death nor evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with the downward breath as the udgātṛ.”

2.1.s: te 'pānenodgātrādīkṣanta sa yad evāpānenāpāniti tad ātmana āgāyad atha ya itare kāmās tān devebhyaḥ |
2.1.d: ते ऽपानेनोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त स यद् एवापानेनापानिति तद् आत्मन आगायद् अथ य इतरे कामास् तान् देवेभ्यः ।
2.1.e: They consecrated themselves with exhalation as udgdtar. What one exhales with exhalation, that it sang to itself; and what the other desires are, those [it sang] to the gods.
2.1.m: They consecrated themselves with the downward breath as the udgātṛ. Whatever one breathes out with the downward breath, that he sang for himself, but whatever other desires there were, those [he sang] for the gods.

2.1.s: tam pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad evāpānena pāpaṃ gandham apāniti sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.1.d: तम् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एवापानेन पापं गन्धम् अपानिति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.1.e: Evil was created after it. What evil odor one exhales with exhalation, that is that evil,
2.1.m: Evil attached itself to it. Whatever bad odour one smells with the downward breath, that is that very evil.

2.1.s: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt prāṇenodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.1.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् प्राणेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.1.e: They said: " Verily, this one hath not carried us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with breath as udgdtar.'"
2.1.m: They said: “This one has indeed carried us beyond neither death nor evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with breath as the udgātṛ.”

2.1.s: te prāṇenodgātrādīkṣanta sa yad eva prāṇena prāṇiti tad ātmana āgāyad atha ya itare kāmās tān devebhyaḥ |
2.1.d: ते प्राणेनोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त स यद् एव प्राणेन प्राणिति तद् आत्मन आगायद् अथ य इतरे कामास् तान् देवेभ्यः ।
2.1.e: They consecrated themselves with breath as udgdtar. What one breathes with breath, that it sang to itself; and what the other desires are, those [it sang] to the gods.
2.1.m: They consecrated themselves with breath as the udgātṛ. Whatever one breathes with breath, that he sang for himself, but whatever other desires there were, those [he sang] for the gods.

2.1.s: tam pāpmā nānvasṛjyata na hy etena prāṇena pāpaṃ vadati na pāpaṃ dhyāyati na pāpam paśyati na pāpaṃ śṛṇoti na pāpaṃ gandham apāniti |
2.1.d: तम् पाप्मा नान्वसृज्यत न ह्य् एतेन प्राणेन पापं वदति न पापं ध्यायति न पापम् पश्यति न पापं शृणोति न पापं गन्धम् अपानिति ।
2.1.e: No evil was created after that. For with this breath one speaks no evil thing, thinks no evil thing, sees no evil thing, hears no evil thing, exhales no evil odor.
2.1.m: Evil did not attach itself to it. For with this breath one speaks no evil, thinks no evil, sees no evil, hears no evil, and smells no bad odour.

2.1.s: tenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam āyan apahatya haiva mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam eti ya evaṃ veda | prathame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.1.d: तेनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् अपहत्य हैव मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् एति य एवं वेद । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
2.1.e: By it having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, they went to the heavenly world. Having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, he who knows thus goes to the heavenly world.
2.1.m:
Having struck away death by it, having struck away evil, they went to the heavenly world.
Striking away death indeed, striking away evil, he goes to the heavenly world who knows thus.
First khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

2.2.s: sā yā sā vāg āsīt so 'gnir abhavat |
2.2.d: सा या सा वाग् आसीत् सो ऽग्निर् अभवत् ।
2.2.e: What this speech was, that became Agni.
2.2.m: Now that speech which was there became Agni.

2.2.s: atha yat tan mana āsīt sa candramā abhavat |
2.2.d: अथ यत् तन् मन आसीत् स चन्द्रमा अभवत् ।
2.2.e: And what this mind was, that became the moon.
2.2.m: Then that mind which was there became the Moon.

2.2.s: atha yat tac cakṣur āsīt sa ādityo 'bhavat |
2.2.d: अथ यत् तच् चक्षुर् आसीत् स आदित्यो ऽभवत् ।
2.2.e: And what this sight was, that became the sun.
2.2.m: Then that sight which was there became Āditya.

2.2.s: atha yat tac chrotram āsīt tā imā diśo 'bhavan tā u eva viśve devāḥ |
2.2.d: अथ यत् तच् छ्रोत्रम् आसीत् ता इमा दिशो ऽभवन् ता उ एव विश्वे देवाः ।
2.2.e: And what this hearing was, that became these quarters; and these are all the gods.
2.2.m:
Then that hearing which was there became these quarters of space;
they indeed are the All-gods.

2.2.s: atha yas so 'pāna āsīt sa bṛhaspatir abhavat yad asyai vāco bṛhatyai patis tasmād bṛhaspatiḥ |
2.2.d: अथ यस् सो ऽपान आसीत् स बृहस्पतिर् अभवत् यद् अस्यै वाचो बृहत्यै पतिस् तस्माद् बृहस्पतिः ।
2.2.e: And what this exhalation was, that became Brhaspati. Because he is the husband (lord, pati) of this great (brhatl) speech, therefore he is [called] Brhaspati.
2.2.m:
Then that downward breath which was there became Bṛhaspati;
because it is the lord (pati) of this great (bṛhatī) speech, therefore it is Bṛhaspati.

2.2.s: atha yas sa prāṇa āsīt sa prajāpatir abhavat sa eṣa putrī prajāvān udgītho yaḥ prāṇaḥ tasya svara eva prajāḥ prajāvān bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
2.2.d: अथ यस् स प्राण आसीत् स प्रजापतिर् अभवत् स एष पुत्री प्रजावान् उद्गीथो यः प्राणः तस्य स्वर एव प्रजाः प्रजावान् भवति य एवं वेद ।
2.2.e: And what this breath was, that became Prajapati. That same, viz. breath, is rich in sons, rich in offspring, the udgītha. Of it tone is the offspring. Rich in offspring becomes he who knows thus.
2.2.m:
Then that breath which was there became Prajāpati.
This breath is that udgītha, having sons and having offspring;
its notes are its offspring.
He becomes possessed of offspring who knows thus.

2.2.s: taṃ haitam eke pratyakṣam eva gāyanti prāṇā3 prāṇā3 prāṇā3 hum bhā ovā iti |
2.2.d: तं हैतम् एके प्रत्यक्षम् एव गायन्ति प्राणा3 प्राणा3 प्राणा3 हुम् भा ओवा इति ।
2.2.e: Some sing that [breath] openly: " Breath, breath, breath, hum, bhd, ovd."
2.2.m: Some indeed sing this visibly: ‘prāṇā3, prāṇā3, prāṇā3, hum bhā ovā’.

2.2.s: tad u hovāca śāṭyāyanis tata etam arhati pratyakṣaṃ gātum yad vāva vācā karoti tad etad evāsya kṛtam bhavatīti |
2.2.d: तद् उ होवाच शाट्यायनिस् तत एतम् अर्हति प्रत्यक्षं गातुम् यद् वाव वाचा करोति तद् एतद् एवास्य कृतम् भवतीति ।
2.2.e: And Śatyayani said regarding this: " Therefore it is possible to sing it directly. Verily, what he performs with speech, that same is performed of him."
2.2.m:
Regarding this, Śāṭyāyani said: 'On that account he is worthy to sing it visibly;
for whatever he does with speech, that very thing becomes accomplished for him.'

2.2.s: atha vā ata ṛksāmnor eva prajātiḥ sa yad dhiṅkaroty abhy eva tena krandati atha yat prastauty aiva tena plavate atha yad ādim ādatte reta eva tena siñcati atha yad udgāyati reta eva tena siktaṃ sambhāvayati atha yat pratiharati reta eva tena sambhūtam pravardhayati atha yad upadravati reta eva tena pravṛddhaṃ vikaroti atha yan nidhanam upaiti reta eva tena vikṛtam prajanayati saiṣa rksāmnoḥ prajātiḥ |
2.2.d: अथ वा अत ऋक्साम्नोर् एव प्रजातिः स यद् धिङ्करोत्य् अभ्य् एव तेन क्रन्दति अथ यत् प्रस्तौत्य् ऐव तेन प्लवते अथ यद् आदिम् आदत्ते रेत एव तेन सिञ्चति अथ यद् उद्गायति रेत एव तेन सिक्तं सम्भावयति अथ यत् प्रतिहरति रेत एव तेन सम्भूतम् प्रवर्धयति अथ यद् उपद्रवति रेत एव तेन प्रवृद्धं विकरोति अथ यन् निधनम् उपैति रेत एव तेन विकृतम् प्रजनयति सैष र्क्साम्नोः प्रजातिः ।
2.2.e: Now [about] the generation of the re and the sāman. In that he utters the hinkdra, thereby he cries to [her]. In that he utters the prastāva, thereby he mounts. In that he utters the ddi, thereby he emits seed. In that he utters the udgītha, thereby he causes the emitted seed to come to life. In that he utters the pratihāra, thereby he causes the seed, come to life, to grow forth. In that he utters the upadrava, he develops the seed, having grown forth. In that he enters upon the nidhana, thereby he causes the seed, being unfolded, to be born forth. That is the generation of the re and of the sdm,an.

2.2.s: sa ya evam etām ṛksāmnoḥ prajātiṃ veda pra hainam ṛksāmanī janayataḥ | prathame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | prathamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
2.2.d: स य एवम् एताम् ऋक्साम्नोः प्रजातिं वेद प्र हैनम् ऋक्सामनी जनयतः । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः । प्रथमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
2.2.e: He who thus knows this generation of the re and of the sdtnan, him the re and the sāman propagate.
2.2.m:
He who knows thus this procreation of ṛc and sāman, ṛc and sāman propagate him.
Second khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.
The first anuvāka is completed.

2.3.s: eṣa evedam agra āsīd ya eṣa tapati sa eṣa sarveṣām bhūtānāṃ tejo hara indriyaṃ vīryam ādāyordhva udakrāmat |
2.3.d: एष एवेदम् अग्र आसीद् य एष तपति स एष सर्वेषाम् भूतानां तेजो हर इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् आदायोर्ध्व उदक्रामत् ।
2.3.e: This [universe] in the beginning was he who burns here. This same, taking the splendor, the grasp, the vitality, the virility of all beings, went upward..
2.3.m:
He indeed who burns here was this [universe] in the beginning;
he, having taken the fiery brilliance, glow, faculty, and vigor of all beings, stepped upward.

2.3.s: so 'kāmayataikam evākṣaraṃ svādu mṛdu devānāṃ vanāmeti |
2.3.d: सो ऽकामयतैकम् एवाक्षरं स्वादु मृदु देवानां वनामेति ।
2.3.e: He desired: " May we win the one sweet soft syllable of the gods."
2.3.m: He desired: 'May I win the one syllable, sweet and gentle, of the gods.'

2.3.s: sa tapo 'tapyata sa tapas taptvaikam evākṣaram abhavat |
2.3.d: स तपो ऽतप्यत स तपस् तप्त्वैकम् एवाक्षरम् अभवत् ।
2.3.e: He performed penance. He having performed penance became the one syllable.
2.3.m:
He performed heat [of austerity];
having performed heat, he became the one syllable.

2.3.s: taṃ devāś ca rṣayaś copasamaipsan athaiṣo 'surān bhūtahano 'sṛjataitasya pāpmano 'nanvāgamāya |
2.3.d: तं देवाश् च र्षयश् चोपसमैप्सन् अथैषो ऽसुरान् भूतहनो ऽसृजतैतस्य पाप्मनो ऽनन्वागमाय ।
2.3.e: That gods and sages desired together to obtain. Then he created creature-slaying Asuras, in order to prevent evil from going after.
2.3.m:
The gods and ṛṣis desired to reach it;
then he created the asuras, slayers of beings, so that this evil should not pursue [him].

2.3.s: taṃ vācopasamaipsan te vācaṃ samārohan teṣāṃ vācam paryādatta tasmāt paryādattā vāk satyaṃ ca hy enayā vadaty anṛtaṃ ca |
2.3.d: तं वाचोपसमैप्सन् ते वाचं समारोहन् तेषां वाचम् पर्यादत्त तस्मात् पर्यादत्ता वाक् सत्यं च ह्य् एनया वदत्य् अनृतं च ।
2.3.e: That they desired together to obtain by speech. They ascended speech together. He took possession of their speech. Therefore speech is taken possession of; for [what is] true one speaks with it and [what is] untrue.

2.3.s: tam manasopasamaipsan te manas samārohan teṣām manaḥ paryādatta tasmāt paryādattam manas puṇyaṃ ca hy enena dhyāyati pāpaṃ ca |
2.3.d: तम् मनसोपसमैप्सन् ते मनस् समारोहन् तेषाम् मनः पर्यादत्त तस्मात् पर्यादत्तम् मनस् पुण्यं च ह्य् एनेन ध्यायति पापं च ।
2.3.e: That they desired together to obtain by mind. They ascended mind together. He took possession of their mind. Therefore mind is taken possession of; for [what is] good one thinks with it and [what is] evil.

2.3.s: taṃ cakṣuṣopasamaipsan te cakṣus samārohan tesāṃ cakṣuḥ paryādatta tasmāt paryāttaṃ cakṣuḥ darśanīyaṃ ca hy enena paśyaty adarśanīyaṃ ca |
2.3.d: तं चक्षुषोपसमैप्सन् ते चक्षुस् समारोहन् तेसां चक्षुः पर्यादत्त तस्मात् पर्यात्तं चक्षुः दर्शनीयं च ह्य् एनेन पश्यत्य् अदर्शनीयं च ।
2.3.e: That they desired together to obtain by sight. They ascended sight together. He took possession of their sight. Therefore sight is taken possession of; for [what is] seemly one sees with it and [what is] unseemly,

2.3.s: taṃ śrotreṇopasamaipsan te śrotraṃ samārohan teṣāṃ śrotram paryādatta tasmāt paryāttaṃ śrotram śravaṇīyaṃ cainena śṛṇoty aśravaṇīyaṃ ca |
2.3.d: तं श्रोत्रेणोपसमैप्सन् ते श्रोत्रं समारोहन् तेषां श्रोत्रम् पर्यादत्त तस्मात् पर्यात्तं श्रोत्रम् श्रवणीयं चैनेन शृणोत्य् अश्रवणीयं च ।
2.3.e: That they desired together to obtain by hearing. They ascended hearing together. He took possession of their hearing. Therefore hearing is taken possession of. For [what is] worth hearing one hears with it and [what is] not worth hearing.

2.3.s: tam apānenopasamaipsan te 'pānaṃ samārohan teṣām apānam paryādatta tasmāt paryātto 'pānaḥ surabhi ca hy enena jighrati durgandhi ca |
2.3.d: तम् अपानेनोपसमैप्सन् ते ऽपानं समारोहन् तेषाम् अपानम् पर्यादत्त तस्मात् पर्यात्तो ऽपानः सुरभि च ह्य् एनेन जिघ्रति दुर्गन्धि च ।
2.3.e: That they desired together to obtain by exhalation. They ascended exhalation together. He took possession of their exhalation. Therefore exhalation is taken possession of; for fragrance one smells with it and bad odor.
That they desired together to obtain by breath. That they obtained together by breath,
2.3.m:
They desired to reach it through breath;
they reached it through breath.

2.3.s: athāsurā bhūtahana ādravan mohayiṣyāma iti manyamānāḥ |
2.3.d: अथासुरा भूतहन आद्रवन् मोहयिष्याम इति मन्यमानाः ।
2.3.e: Then the creature-slaying Asuras ran unto [themj, thinking: " We will confound [them]." is. — I. 60. 8., is. = I. 60. ».
2.3.m: Then the asuras, slayers of beings, ran up, thinking: 'We will cause confusion.'

2.3.s: sa yathāśmānam ṛtvā loṣṭo vidhvaṃsetaivam evāsurā vyadhvaṃsanta sa eṣo 'śmākhaṇo yat prāṇaḥ |
2.3.d: स यथाश्मानम् ऋत्वा लोष्टो विध्वंसेतैवम् एवासुरा व्यध्वंसन्त स एषो ऽश्माखणो यत् प्राणः ।
2.3.m:
Just as a clod of earth having struck a stone would shatter, so indeed the asuras shattered;
that breath is this solid stone.

2.3.s: sa yathāśmānam ākhaṇam ṛtvā loṣṭo vidhvaṃsata evam eva sa vidhvaṃsate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam upavadati | dvitīye 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.3.d: स यथाश्मानम् आखणम् ऋत्वा लोष्टो विध्वंसत एवम् एव स विध्वंसते य एवं विद्वांसम् उपवदति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
2.3.m:
Just as a clod of earth having struck a solid stone shatters, so indeed shatters he who speaks ill against one who knows thus.
First khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.

2.4.s: sa eṣa vaśī dīptāgra udgītho yat prāṇaḥ eṣa hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vaśe kurute |
2.4.d: स एष वशी दीप्ताग्र उद्गीथो यत् प्राणः एष हीदं सर्वं वशे कुरुते ।
2.4.e: That same, viz. breath, is the controling flame-pointed udgitha. For it gets this all into control.
2.4.m:
That breath is this controlling udgītha with a blazing point;
for this brings all this under control.

2.4.s: vaśī bhavati vaśe svān kurute ya evaṃ veda asya hy asāv agre dīpyate3 amuṣya vā saḥ |
2.4.d: वशी भवति वशे स्वान् कुरुते य एवं वेद अस्य ह्य् असाव् अग्रे दीप्यते3 अमुष्य वा सः ।
2.4.e: He becomes controling, he gets his people into control who knows thus; for does yonder one flame at this one's point or this one at yonder one's?
2.4.m:
He becomes a controller and brings his own under control who knows thus;
for his [point] blazes yonder at the top, or that [blazes] of yonder one.

2.4.s: taṃ haitam udgīthaṃ śāṭyāyanir ācaṣṭe vaśī dīptāgra iti dīptāgrā ha vā asya kīrtir bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
2.4.d: तं हैतम् उद्गीथं शाट्यायनिर् आचष्टे वशी दीप्ताग्र इति दीप्ताग्रा ह वा अस्य कीर्तिर् भवति य एवं वेद ।
2.4.e: That same udgitha ^Śtyayani calls 'the controling one, the flame-pointed one.' Verily flame-pointed becomes his fame who knows thus.
2.4.m:
Śāṭyāyani proclaims this udgītha as 'controlling, with a blazing point';
blazing at the point indeed becomes the fame of him who knows thus.

2.4.s: ābhūtir iti kārīrādayaḥ prāṇaṃ vā anu prajāḥ paśava ābhavanti sa ya evam etam ābhūtir ity upāsta aiva prāṇena prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
2.4.d: आभूतिर् इति कारीरादयः प्राणं वा अनु प्रजाः पशव आभवन्ति स य एवम् एतम् आभूतिर् इत्य् उपास्त ऐव प्राणेन प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति ।
2.4.e: The Kariradis [call it] 'existence' (dbhuti). Verily, along with breath offspring and domestic animals exist. Whoso thus worships it as existence, with breath, with offspring, with domestic animals he exists.

2.4.s: sambhūtir iti sātyayajñayaḥ prāṇaṃ vā anu prajāḥ paśavas sambhavanti sa ya evam etaṃ sambhūtir ity upāste sam eva prāṇena prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
2.4.d: सम्भूतिर् इति सात्ययज्ञयः प्राणं वा अनु प्रजाः पशवस् सम्भवन्ति स य एवम् एतं सम्भूतिर् इत्य् उपास्ते सम् एव प्राणेन प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति ।
2.4.e: The SatyayajSis [call it] ' origination' (sambhuti). Verily, along with breath offspring and domestic animals originate. Whoso thus worships it as origination, with breath, with offspring, with domestic animals he originates.

2.4.s: prabhūtir iti śailanāḥ prāṇaṃ vā anu prajāḥ paśavaḥ prabhavanti sa ya evam etam prabhūtir ity upāste praiva prāṇena prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
2.4.d: प्रभूतिर् इति शैलनाः प्राणं वा अनु प्रजाः पशवः प्रभवन्ति स य एवम् एतम् प्रभूतिर् इत्य् उपास्ते प्रैव प्राणेन प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति ।
2.4.e: The Śailanas [call it] 'prevalence' (prabhuti). Verily, along with bi-eath offspring and domestic animals prevail. Whoso thus worships it as prevalence, with breath, with offspring, with domestic animals he prevails.

2.4.s: bhūtir iti bhāllabinaḥ prāṇaṃ vā anu prajāḥ paśavo bhavanti sa ya evam etam bhūtir ity upāste bhavaty eva prāṇena prajayā paśubhiḥ |
2.4.d: भूतिर् इति भाल्लबिनः प्राणं वा अनु प्रजाः पशवो भवन्ति स य एवम् एतम् भूतिर् इत्य् उपास्ते भवत्य् एव प्राणेन प्रजया पशुभिः ।
2.4.e: The Bhallabins [call it] 'coming into being' {bhiUi). Verily, along with breath offspring and domestic animals come into being. Whoso thus worships it as coming into being, with breath, with offspring, with domestic animals he comes into being.

2.4.s: aparodho 'naparuddha iti pārṣṇaś śailanaḥ eṣa hy anyam aparuṇaddhi naitam anyaḥ eṣa ha vāsya dviṣantam bhrātṛvyam aparuṇaddhi ya evaṃ veda | dvitīye 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.4.d: अपरोधो ऽनपरुद्ध इति पार्ष्णश् शैलनः एष ह्य् अन्यम् अपरुणद्धि नैतम् अन्यः एष ह वास्य द्विषन्तम् भ्रातृव्यम् अपरुणद्धि य एवं वेद । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
2.4.e: Parsna Śs^ilana "calls it] 'the unexcluded exclusion.' For it excludes another, but] another [does] not [exclude] it. Verily, it excludes the hateful rival of him who knows thus.

2.5.s: ekavīra ity āruṇeyaḥ eko hy evaiṣa vīro yat prāṇaḥ ā hāsyaiko vīro vīryavāñ jāyate ya evaṃ veda |
2.5.d: एकवीर इत्य् आरुणेयः एको ह्य् एवैष वीरो यत् प्राणः आ हास्यैको वीरो वीर्यवाञ् जायते य एवं वेद ।
2.5.e: Aruneya [calls it] ' sole hero.' For that, viz. breath, is sole hero. Of him a sole hero, rich in heroism, is born who knows thus. s. Śaikitaneya [calls it] ' having one son.' For that, viz. breath, is the only son.

2.5.s: ekaputra iti caikitāneyaḥ eko hy evaiṣa putro yat prāṇaḥ |
2.5.d: एकपुत्र इति चैकितानेयः एको ह्य् एवैष पुत्रो यत् प्राणः ।
2.5.m:
'Having one son,' says Caikitāneya;
for breath is the only son.

2.5.s: sa u eva dviputra iti dvau hi prāṇāpānau |
2.5.d: स उ एव द्विपुत्र इति द्वौ हि प्राणापानौ ।
2.5.e: It is also having two sons. For breath and exhalation are two.
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having two sons';
for the out-breath and the downward breath are two.

2.5.s: sa u eva triputra iti trayo hi prāṇo 'pāno vyānaḥ |
2.5.d: स उ एव त्रिपुत्र इति त्रयो हि प्राणो ऽपानो व्यानः ।
2.5.e: It is also having three sons. For breath, exhalation, and vydna are three.
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having three sons';
for the out-breath, downward breath, and diffused breath are three.

2.5.s: sa u eva catuṣputra iti catvāro hi prāṇo 'pāno vyānas samānaḥ |
2.5.d: स उ एव चतुष्पुत्र इति चत्वारो हि प्राणो ऽपानो व्यानस् समानः ।
2.5.e: It is also having four sons. E'er breath, exhalation, vydna, [and] samdna are four.
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having four sons';
for the out-breath, downward breath, diffused breath, and equalizing breath are four.

2.5.s: sa u eva pañcaputra iti pañca hi prāṇo 'pāno vyānas samāno 'vānaḥ |
2.5.d: स उ एव पञ्चपुत्र इति पञ्च हि प्राणो ऽपानो व्यानस् समानो ऽवानः ।
2.5.e: It is also having five sons. For breath, exhalation, vydna, samdna, [and] avdna are five.
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having five sons';
for the out-breath, downward breath, diffused breath, equalizing breath, and lower breath are five.

2.5.s: sa u eva ṣaṭputra iti ṣaḍ ḍhi prāṇo 'pāno vyānas samāno 'vāna udānaḥ |
2.5.d: स उ एव षट्पुत्र इति षड् ढि प्राणो ऽपानो व्यानस् समानो ऽवान उदानः ।
2.5.e: It is also having six sons. For breath, exhalation, vydna, samdna, avdna, [and] uddna are six.
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having six sons';
for the out-breath, downward breath, diffused breath, equalizing breath, lower breath, and upward breath are six.

2.5.s: sa u eva saptaputra iti sapta hīme śīrṣaṇyāḥ prāṇāḥ |
2.5.d: स उ एव सप्तपुत्र इति सप्त हीमे शीर्षण्याः प्राणाः ।
2.5.e: It is also having seven sons. For these breaths in the head are seven.
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having seven sons';
for these breaths in the head are seven.

2.5.s: sa u eva navaputra iti sapta hi śīrṣaṇyāḥ prāṇā dvāv avāñcau |
2.5.d: स उ एव नवपुत्र इति सप्त हि शीर्षण्याः प्राणा द्वाव् अवाञ्चौ ।
2.5.e: It is also having nine sons. For there are seven breaths in the head [and] two downward ones.
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having nine sons';
for the breaths in the head are seven, and two are downward.

2.5.s: sa u eva daśaputra iti sapta śīrṣaṇyāḥ prāṇā dvāv avāñcau nābhyāṃ daśamaḥ |
2.5.d: स उ एव दशपुत्र इति सप्त शीर्षण्याः प्राणा द्वाव् अवाञ्चौ नाभ्यां दशमः ।
2.5.e: It is also having ten sons. For there are seven breaths in thehead, two downward ones, [and] the tenth in the navel,
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having ten sons';
for the breaths in the head are seven, two are downward, and the tenth is at the navel.

2.5.s: sa u eva bahuputra iti etasya hīyaṃ sarvāḥ prajāḥ |
2.5.d: स उ एव बहुपुत्र इति एतस्य हीयं सर्वाः प्रजाः ।
2.5.e: It is also having many sons. For this [earth] is all its offspring,
2.5.m:
'He is indeed having many sons';
for all these offspring belong to this one.

2.5.s: etaṃ ha sma vai tad udgīthaṃ vidvāṃsaḥ pūrve brāhmaṇāḥ kāmāgāyina āhuḥ kati te putrān āgāsyāma iti | dvitīye 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.5.d: एतं ह स्म वै तद् उद्गीथं विद्वांसः पूर्वे ब्राह्मणाः कामागायिन आहुः कति ते पुत्रान् आगास्याम इति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
2.5.e: Verily, knowing thus this udgitha, the Brahmans of old when they sang a wish [to any one] used to say: " How many sons shall we sing unto thee?"
2.5.m:
Knowing this udgītha, the ancient Brahmins singing for desires used to say: 'How many sons shall we sing into being for you?'
Third khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyād ekam ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha iti vidvān ekam manasā dhyāyet eko hi prāṇaḥ eko hāsyājāyate |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयाद् एकम् म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इति विद्वान् एकम् मनसा ध्यायेत् एको हि प्राणः एको हास्याजायते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: "Sing one unto me," knowing that breath is the udgitha, he should think one with his mind. For breath is one. Truly, one is born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for one [son]”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on one.
For breath is one.
One [son] indeed is born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyād dvau ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvān dvau manasā dhyāyet dvau hi prāṇāpānau dvau haivāsyājāyete |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयाद् द्वौ म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वान् द्वौ मनसा ध्यायेत् द्वौ हि प्राणापानौ द्वौ हैवास्याजायेते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: " Sing two unto me," knowing that breath is the udg'Uha, he should think two with his mind. For breath and exhalation are two. Truly, two are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for two”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on two.
For out-breath and in-breath are two.
Two indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyāt trīn ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvāṃs trīn manasā dhyāyet trayo hi prāṇo 'pāno vyānaḥ trayo haivāsyājāyante |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयात् त्रीन् म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वांस् त्रीन् मनसा ध्यायेत् त्रयो हि प्राणो ऽपानो व्यानः त्रयो हैवास्याजायन्ते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: " Sing three unto me," knowing that breath is the udg'Uha, "he should think three with his mind. For breath, exhalation, [and] oydna are three. Truly, three are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for three”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on three.
For breath, out-breath, and diffused breath are three.
Three indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyāc caturo ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvāṃś caturo manasā dhyāyet catvāro hi prāṇo 'pāno vyānas samānaḥ catvāro haivāsyājāyante |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयाच् चतुरो म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वांश् चतुरो मनसा ध्यायेत् चत्वारो हि प्राणो ऽपानो व्यानस् समानः चत्वारो हैवास्याजायन्ते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: " Sing four unto me," knowing that breath is the udgUha, he should think four with his mind. For breath, exhalation, vydna, [and] samdna are four. Truly, four are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for four”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on four.
For breath, out-breath, diffused breath, and equalized breath are four.
Four indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyāt pañca ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvān pañca manasā dhyāyet pañca hi prāṇo 'pāno vyānas samāno 'vānaḥ pañca haivāsyājāyante |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयात् पञ्च म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वान् पञ्च मनसा ध्यायेत् पञ्च हि प्राणो ऽपानो व्यानस् समानो ऽवानः पञ्च हैवास्याजायन्ते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: "Sing five unto me," knowing that breath is the udg'Uha, he should think five with his mind. For breath, exhalation, vydna, samdna, [and] avdna are five. Truly five are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for five”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on five.
For breath, out-breath, diffused breath, equalized breath, and downward breath are five.
Five indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyāt ṣaṇ ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvān ṣaṇ manasā dhyāyet ṣaḍ ḍhi prāṇo 'pāno vyānas samāno 'vāna udānaḥ ṣaḍ ḍhaivāsyājāyante |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयात् षण् म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वान् षण् मनसा ध्यायेत् षड् ढि प्राणो ऽपानो व्यानस् समानो ऽवान उदानः षड् ढैवास्याजायन्ते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: " Sing six unto me," knowing that breath is the udgitha, he should think six with his mind. For breath, exhalation, vydna, samdna, avdna, uddna are six. Truly, six are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for six”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on six.
For breath, out-breath, diffused breath, equalized breath, downward breath, and upward breath are six.
Six indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyāt sapta ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvān sapta manasā dhyāyet sapta hīme śīrṣaṇyāḥ prāṇāḥ sapta haivāsyājāyante |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयात् सप्त म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वान् सप्त मनसा ध्यायेत् सप्त हीमे शीर्षण्याः प्राणाः सप्त हैवास्याजायन्ते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: " Sing seven unto me," knowing that breath is the udgitha, he should think seven with his mind. For these breaths in the head are seven. Truly, seven are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for seven”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on seven.
For these breaths in the head are seven.
Seven indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyān nava ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvān nava manasā dhyāyet sapta śīrṣaṇyāḥ prāṇā dvāv avāñcau nava haivāsyājāyante |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयान् नव म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वान् नव मनसा ध्यायेत् सप्त शीर्षण्याः प्राणा द्वाव् अवाञ्चौ नव हैवास्याजायन्ते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: " Sing nine unto me," knowing that breath is the udgitha, he should think nine with his mind. There are seven breaths in the head [and] two downward ones. Truly, nine are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for nine”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on nine.
Seven are the breaths in the head, two are downward.
Nine indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyād daśa ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvān daśa manasā dhyāyet sapta śīrṣaṇyāḥ prāṇā dvāv avāñcau nābhyāṃ daśamaḥ daśa haivāsyājāyante |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयाद् दश म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वान् दश मनसा ध्यायेत् सप्त शीर्षण्याः प्राणा द्वाव् अवाञ्चौ नाभ्यां दशमः दश हैवास्याजायन्ते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: " Sing ten unto me," knowing that breath is the udgitha, he should think ten with his mind. There are seven breaths in the head, two downward ones, [and] the tenth in the navel. Truly, ten are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for ten”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on ten.
Seven are the breaths in the head, two downward, the tenth is at the navel.
Ten indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: sa yadi brūyāt sahasram ma āgāyeti prāṇa udgītha ity eva vidvān sahasram manasā dhyāyet sahasraṃ haita ādityaraśmayaḥ te 'sya putrāḥ sahasraṃ haivāsyājāyante |
2.6.d: स यदि ब्रूयात् सहस्रम् म आगायेति प्राण उद्गीथ इत्य् एव विद्वान् सहस्रम् मनसा ध्यायेत् सहस्रं हैत आदित्यरश्मयः ते ऽस्य पुत्राः सहस्रं हैवास्याजायन्ते ।
2.6.e: If he should say: " Sing a thousand for me," knowing that breath is the udgitha, he should think a thousand with his mind. Truly, a thousand are the rays of the sun. They are its sons. Truly, a thousand are born unto him.
2.6.m:
If he should say: “Chant for me for a thousand”, knowing that breath is the udgītha, he should mentally focus on a thousand.
A thousand indeed are these rays of the sun;
they are his sons.
A thousand indeed are born to him.

2.6.s: evaṃ haivaitam udgītham para āṭṇāraḥ kakṣīvāṃs trasadasyur iti pūrve mahārājāś śrotriyās sahasraputram upaniṣeduḥ te ha sarva eva sahasraputrā āsuḥ |
2.6.d: एवं हैवैतम् उद्गीथम् पर आट्णारः कक्षीवांस् त्रसदस्युर् इति पूर्वे महाराजाश् श्रोत्रियास् सहस्रपुत्रम् उपनिषेदुः ते ह सर्व एव सहस्रपुत्रा आसुः ।
2.6.e: Para Atnara, Kaksivant, Trasadasyu, great kings of old, scholars in sacred lore, thus studied this same udgitha of a thousand sons. All of them had a thousand sons. He who knows thus, of him there come to be a thousand sons.
2.6.m:
Thus indeed Para Āṭṇāra, Kakṣīvant, and Trasadasyu—these ancient great kings learned in the Veda—sat near this udgītha of a thousand sons.
They all indeed had a thousand sons.

2.6.s: sa ya evaivaṃ veda sahasraṃ haivāsya putrā bhavanti | dvitīye 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | dvitīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
2.6.d: स य एवैवं वेद सहस्रं हैवास्य पुत्रा भवन्ति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः । द्वितीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
2.6.m:
He who knows thus—a thousand sons indeed come to be his.
Fourth khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.
The second anuvāka is completed.

2.7.s: śaryāto vai mānavaḥ prācyāṃ sthalyām ayajata tasmin ha bhūtāny udgīthe 'pitvam eṣire |
2.7.d: शर्यातो वै मानवः प्राच्यां स्थल्याम् अयजत तस्मिन् ह भूतान्य् उद्गीथे ऽपित्वम् एषिरे ।
2.7.e: 9*ryata Manava made a sacrifice on the eastern site. With him created beings sought a share in the udgītha.
2.7.m:
Śaryāta Mānava sacrificed on an eastern mound.
At that, the creatures desired a share in the udgītha.

2.7.s: taṃ devā bṛhaspatinodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti purastād āgacchann ayaṃ ta udgāyatv iti bambenājadviṣeṇa pitaro dakṣiṇato 'yaṃ ta udgāyatv ity uśanasā kāvyenāsurāḥ paścād ayaṃ ta udgāyatv ity ayāsyenāṅgirasena manuṣyā uttarato 'yaṃ ta udgāyatv iti |
2.7.d: तं देवा बृहस्पतिनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति पुरस्ताद् आगच्छन्न् अयं त उद्गायत्व् इति बम्बेनाजद्विषेण पितरो दक्षिणतो ऽयं त उद्गायत्व् इत्य् उशनसा काव्येनासुराः पश्चाद् अयं त उद्गायत्व् इत्य् अयास्येनाङ्गिरसेन मनुष्या उत्तरतो ऽयं त उद्गायत्व् इति ।
2.7.e: Unto him the gods came from the east (front) [saying]: " Let us consecrate ourselves with Brhaspati as udgdtar. Let this one sing the udgliha for thee." With Bamba Ajadvisa the Fathers [came] from the south (right)' [saying]: " Let this one sing the udgītha for thee." With Uganas Kavya the Asuras [came] from the west (rear) [saying]: " Let this one sing the udgītha for thee." With Ayasya Angirasa men [came] from the north (left) [saying]: " Let this one sing the udgītha for thee."
2.7.m:
The gods came from the east [saying], “Let us consecrate with Bṛhaspati as udgātṛ; let this one chant for you.”
The ancestors came from the south [saying], “With Bamba Ājadviṣa; let this one chant for you.”
The asuras came from the west [saying], “With Uśanas Kāvya; let this one chant for you.”
Men came from the north [saying], “With Ayāsya Āṅgirasa; let this one chant for you.”

2.7.s: sa hekṣāṃ cakre hantainān pṛcchāni kiyato vā eka īśe kiyata ekaḥ kiyata eka iti |
2.7.d: स हेक्षां चक्रे हन्तैनान् पृच्छानि कियतो वा एक ईशे कियत एकः कियत एक इति ।
2.7.e: He considered: " Come now, I will ask them how great the power of the one is, how great the power of the other is, how great the power of the other (third) is."
2.7.m: He reflected: “Come, let me ask them: Over how much does one rule? Over how much one? Over how much one?”

2.7.s: sa hovāca bṛhaspatiṃ yan me tvam udgāyeḥ kiṃ tatas syād iti |
2.7.d: स होवाच बृहस्पतिं यन् मे त्वम् उद्गायेः किं ततस् स्याद् इति ।
2.7.e: He said to Brhaspati: " If thou shouldst sing the udgītha for me, what would be the result of it?" &. He said: " Among the gods there would be fortune, among the gods dominion, and I should cause thee to go to the heavenly world."
2.7.m: He said to Bṛhaspati: “If you were to chant for me, what would result from it?”

2.7.s: sa hovāca deveṣv eva śrīs syād deveṣv īśā svargam u tvāṃ lokaṃ gamayeyam iti |
2.7.d: स होवाच देवेष्व् एव श्रीस् स्याद् देवेष्व् ईशा स्वर्गम् उ त्वां लोकं गमयेयम् इति ।
2.7.m: He said: “Prosperity would belong only to the gods; rule would belong to the gods; and you I would bring to the heavenly world.”

2.7.s: atha hovāca bambam ājadviṣam yan me tvam udgāyeḥ kiṃ tatas syād iti |
2.7.d: अथ होवाच बम्बम् आजद्विषम् यन् मे त्वम् उद्गायेः किं ततस् स्याद् इति ।
2.7.e: Then he said to Bamba Ajadvisa: " If thou shouldst sing the udgītha for me, what would be the result of it?"
2.7.m: Then he said to Bamba Ājadviṣa: “If you were to chant for me, what would result from it?”

2.7.s: sa hovāca pitṛṣv eva śrīs syāt pitṛṣv īśā svargam u tvāṃ lokaṃ gamayeyam iti |
2.7.d: स होवाच पितृष्व् एव श्रीस् स्यात् पितृष्व् ईशा स्वर्गम् उ त्वां लोकं गमयेयम् इति ।
2.7.e: He said: " Among the Fathers there would be fortune, among the Fathers dominion, and I should cause thee to go to the heavenly world."
2.7.m: He said: “Prosperity would belong only to the ancestors; rule would belong to the ancestors; and you I would bring to the heavenly world.”

2.7.s: atha hovācośanasaṃ kāvyaṃ yan me tvam udgāyeḥ kiṃ tatas syād iti |
2.7.d: अथ होवाचोशनसं काव्यं यन् मे त्वम् उद्गायेः किं ततस् स्याद् इति ।
2.7.e: Then he said to U9anas Kavya: "If thou shouldst sing the udgītha for me, what would be the result of it?"
2.7.m: Then he said to Uśanas Kāvya: “If you were to chant for me, what would result from it?”

2.7.s: sa hovācāsureṣv eva śrīs syād asureṣv īśā svargam u tvāṃ lokaṃ gamayeyam iti |
2.7.d: स होवाचासुरेष्व् एव श्रीस् स्याद् असुरेष्व् ईशा स्वर्गम् उ त्वां लोकं गमयेयम् इति ।
2.7.e: He said: " Among the Asuras there would be fortune, among the Asuras dominion, and I should cause thee to go to the heavenly world."
2.7.m: He said: “Prosperity would belong only to the asuras; rule would belong to the asuras; and you I would bring to the heavenly world.”

2.7.s: atha hovācāyāsyam āṅgirasaṃ yan me tvam udgāyeḥ kiṃ tatas syād iti |
2.7.d: अथ होवाचायास्यम् आङ्गिरसं यन् मे त्वम् उद्गायेः किं ततस् स्याद् इति ।
2.7.e: Then he said to Ayasya Aiigirasa: "If thou shouldst sing the udgUha forme, what would be the result of it?"
2.7.m: Then he said to Ayāsya Āṅgirasa: “If you were to chant for me, what would result from it?”

2.7.s: sa hovāca devān eva devaloke dadhyām manuṣyān manuṣyaloke pitṝn pitṛloke nudeyāsmāl lokād asurān svargam u tvāṃ lokaṃ gamayeyam iti | tṛtīte 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.7.d: स होवाच देवान् एव देवलोके दध्याम् मनुष्यान् मनुष्यलोके पितॄन् पितृलोके नुदेयास्माल् लोकाद् असुरान् स्वर्गम् उ त्वां लोकं गमयेयम् इति । तृतीते ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
2.7.e: He said: " I should place the gods in the world of the gods, men in the world of men, the Fathers in the world of the Fathers; I should push the Asuras away from this world; and I should cause thee to go to the heavenly world."
2.7.m:
He said: “The gods I would place in the world of the gods, men in the world of men, the ancestors in the world of the ancestors; the asuras I would drive away from this world; and you I would bring to the heavenly world.”
First khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka.

2.8.s: sa hovāca tvam me bhagava udgāya ya etasya sarvasya yaśo 'sīti |
2.8.d: स होवाच त्वम् मे भगव उद्गाय य एतस्य सर्वस्य यशो ऽसीति ।
2.8.e: He (9.) said: " Sing thou, reverend sir, the udgītha for me, who art the glory of this all."
2.8.m: He said: “Venerable sir, chant for me, you who [are] the glory of this all!”

2.8.s: tasya hāyāsya evojjagau tasmād udgātā vṛta uttarato niveśanaṃ lipseta etad dha nāruddhaṃ niveśanaṃ yad uttarataḥ |
2.8.d: तस्य हायास्य एवोज्जगौ तस्माद् उद्गाता वृत उत्तरतो निवेशनं लिप्सेत एतद् ध नारुद्धं निवेशनं यद् उत्तरतः ।
2.8.e: Of him Ayasya sang the udgītha. Therefore an udgdtar, when chosen, should desire to take his resting-place in the north (left). For that restingplace which is in the north is not obstructed,
2.8.m:
Ayāsya indeed chanted for him.
Therefore, an udgātṛ once chosen should seek a lodging to the north.
For that is an unobjectionable lodging which is to the north.

2.8.s: uttarata āgato 'yāsya āṅgirasaś śaryātasya mānavasyojjagau sa prāṇena devān devaloke 'dadhād apānena manuṣyān manuṣyaloke vyānena pitṝn pitṛloke hiṅkāreṇa vajreṇāsmāl lokād asurān anudata |
2.8.d: उत्तरत आगतो ऽयास्य आङ्गिरसश् शर्यातस्य मानवस्योज्जगौ स प्राणेन देवान् देवलोके ऽदधाद् अपानेन मनुष्यान् मनुष्यलोके व्यानेन पितॄन् पितृलोके हिङ्कारेण वज्रेणास्माल् लोकाद् असुरान् अनुदत ।
2.8.e: Having come from the north, Ayasya Angirasa sang the udgītha of ^Śryata Manava. By breath he placed the gods in the world of the gods, by exhalation men in the world of men, by the vydna the Fathers in the world of the Fathers, by the hinkdra [as] thunderbolt he pushed the Asuras away from this world.
2.8.m:
Ayāsya Āṅgirasa, having arrived from the north, chanted for Śaryāta Mānava.
With breath he placed the gods in the world of the gods, with out-breath men in the world of men, with diffused breath the ancestors in the world of the ancestors, and with the hiṅkāra as a thunderbolt he drove the asuras away from this world.

2.8.s: tān hovāca dūraṃ gacchateti sa dūro ha nāma lokaḥ taṃ ha jagmuḥ ta ete 'surā asambhāvyam parābhūtāḥ |
2.8.d: तान् होवाच दूरं गच्छतेति स दूरो ह नाम लोकः तं ह जग्मुः त एते ऽसुरा असम्भाव्यम् पराभूताः ।
2.8.e: He said to them: " Go ye afar." That is a world named ' afar.' They went to it. These same Asuras were irretrievably defeated,
2.8.m:
He said to them: “Go far away!”
Far away is indeed the name of that world;
to that they went.
These asuras were defeated beyond restoration.

2.8.s: chandobhir eva vācā śaryātam mānavaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayāṃ cakāra |
2.8.d: छन्दोभिर् एव वाचा शर्यातम् मानवं स्वर्गं लोकं गमयां चकार ।
2.8.e: By the metres, by speech, he caused paryata Manava to go to the heavenly world.
2.8.m: Through the metres, through speech alone, he made Śaryāta Mānava attain the heavenly world.

2.8.s: te hocur asurā eta taṃ vedāma yo no 'yam ittham adhatteti tata āgacchan tam etyāpaśyan |
2.8.d: ते होचुर् असुरा एत तं वेदाम यो नो ऽयम् इत्थम् अधत्तेति तत आगच्छन् तम् एत्यापश्यन् ।
2.8.e: These Asuras said: " Come, let us know him who placed us thus." Thereupon they came. Having come, they saw him.

2.8.s: te 'bruvann ayaṃ vā āsya iti yad abruvann ayaṃ vā āsya iti tasmād ayamāsyaḥ ayamāsyo ha vai nāmaiṣaḥ tam ayāsya iti parokṣam ācakṣate |
2.8.d: ते ऽब्रुवन्न् अयं वा आस्य इति यद् अब्रुवन्न् अयं वा आस्य इति तस्माद् अयमास्यः अयमास्यो ह वै नामैषः तम् अयास्य इति परोक्षम् आचक्षते ।
2.8.e: They said: " Verily he {ayam) is in the mouth (asya)." Because they said: " Verily he is in the mouth," therefore he is [called] Ayamasya. Ayamasya, verily, is his name. Him they call Ayasya in an occult way. "
2.8.m:
They said: “This one is in the mouth (ayam āsye).”
Because they said, “This one is in the mouth”, therefore he is Ayamāsya.
Ayamāsya indeed is his name;
him they cryptically call Ayāsya.

2.8.s: sa prāṇo vā ayāsyaḥ prāṇo ha vā enān sa nunude |
2.8.d: स प्राणो वा अयास्यः प्राणो ह वा एनान् स नुनुदे ।
2.8.e: This breath is Ayasya. Verily as breath he pushed them away.
2.8.m:
Ayāsya is breath;
it was breath indeed that drove them away.

2.8.s: sa ya evaṃ vidvān udgāyati prāṇenaiva devān devaloke dadhāty apānena manuṣyān manuṣyaloke vyānena pitṝn pitṛloke hiṅkāreṇaiva vajreṇāsmāl lokād dviṣantam bhrātṛvyaṃ nudate | tṛtīye 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.8.d: स य एवं विद्वान् उद्गायति प्राणेनैव देवान् देवलोके दधात्य् अपानेन मनुष्यान् मनुष्यलोके व्यानेन पितॄन् पितृलोके हिङ्कारेणैव वज्रेणास्माल् लोकाद् द्विषन्तम् भ्रातृव्यं नुदते । तृतीये ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
2.8.e: He who knowing thus sings the udgītha places with breath the gods in the world of the gods, with exhalation men in the world of men, with the vydna the Fathers in the world of the Fathers, with the hinkdra [as] thunderbolt he pushes his hateful rival away from this world.
2.8.m:
He who, knowing thus, chants—with breath he places the gods in the world of the gods, with out-breath men in the world of men, with diffused breath the ancestors in the world of the ancestors, and with the hiṅkāra as a thunderbolt he drives away the hateful rival from this world.
Second khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka.

2.9.s: taṃ ha brūyād dūraṃ gaccheti sa yam eva lokam asurā agacchaṃs taṃ haiva gacchati |
2.9.d: तं ह ब्रूयाद् दूरं गच्छेति स यम् एव लोकम् असुरा अगच्छंस् तं हैव गच्छति ।
2.9.e: He should say to him: " Go afar." What world the Asuras went unto, unto that same one he goes.
2.9.m:
He should say to him: “Go far away!”
To the very world to which the asuras went, he indeed goes.

2.9.s: chandobhir eva vācā yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati |
2.9.d: छन्दोभिर् एव वाचा यजमानं स्वर्गं लोकं गमयति ।
2.9.e: With the metres, with speech, he causes the sacrificer to go to the heavenly world.
2.9.m: Through the metres, through speech alone, he causes the sacrificer to reach the heavenly world.

2.9.s: tā etā vyāhṛtayaḥ prety eti vāg bhūr bhuvas svar ity |
2.9.d: ता एता व्याहृतयः प्रेत्य् एति वाग् भूर् भुवस् स्वर् इत्य् ।
2.9.e: These are the sacred utterances: pra, d, vac, bhus bhuvas svar, [ud].
2.9.m: These are the mystic utterances: “pra”, “iti”, “vāc”, “bhūr bhuvas svaḥ”, “ud”, “iti”.

2.9.s: tad yat preti tat prāṇas tad ayaṃ lokas tad imaṃ lokam asmiṃl loka ābhajati |
2.9.d: तद् यत् प्रेति तत् प्राणस् तद् अयं लोकस् तद् इमं लोकम् अस्मिंल् लोक आभजति ।
2.9.e: What Śpm is, that is breath, that is this world, that gives a share of this world in this world.
2.9.m: As for that “pra”, that is breath, that is this world, that shares this world in this world.

2.9.s: ety apānas tad asau lokas tad amuṃ lokam amuṣmiṃl loka ābhajati |
2.9.d: एत्य् अपानस् तद् असौ लोकस् तद् अमुं लोकम् अमुष्मिंल् लोक आभजति ।
2.9.e: Z, that is exhalation, that is yonder world, that gives a share of yonder world in yonder world.
2.9.m: “iti” is out-breath, that is that world, that shares that world in that world.

2.9.s: vāg iti tad brahma tad idam antarikṣam |
2.9.d: वाग् इति तद् ब्रह्म तद् इदम् अन्तरिक्षम् ।
2.9.e: Vdc, that is the brahman, that is this atmosphere.
2.9.m: “vāc”—that is brahman, that is this intermediate space.

2.9.s: bhūr bhuvas svar iti sā trayī vidyā |
2.9.d: भूर् भुवस् स्वर् इति सा त्रयी विद्या ।
2.9.e: Jihus bhuvas svar, that is the threefold knowledge.
2.9.m: “bhūr bhuvas svaḥ”—that is the threefold knowledge.

2.9.s: ud iti so 'sāv ādityaḥ tad yad ud ity ud iva śleṣayati |
2.9.d: उद् इति सो ऽसाव् आदित्यः तद् यद् उद् इत्य् उद् इव श्लेषयति ।
2.9.e: Ud, that is yonder sun. Inasmuch as it is ud, it causes to cling up (Py'pKs + ud), as it were.
2.9.m:
“ud”—that is yonder sun.
Now, as for “ud”, it attaches as it were upwards.

2.9.s: tad yad ekam evābhisampadyate tasmād ekavīraḥ eko ha tu san vīro vīryavān bhavati ā hāsyaiko vīro vīryavān jāyate ya evaṃ veda |
2.9.d: तद् यद् एकम् एवाभिसम्पद्यते तस्माद् एकवीरः एको ह तु सन् वीरो वीर्यवान् भवति आ हास्यैको वीरो वीर्यवान् जायते य एवं वेद ।
2.9.e: Inasmuch as it forms a unit, therefore it is sole hero. But being one it becomes a hero possessing heroism. To him a sole hero possessing heroism is born who knows thus.
2.9.m:
Because it attains only one, therefore it is the sole hero.
Being indeed one, he becomes a hero possessing heroism.
To him who knows thus, a single hero possessing heroism is born.

2.9.s: tad u hovāca śāṭyāyanir bahuputra eṣa udgītha ity evopāsitavyam bahavo hy eta ādityasya raśmayas te 'sya putrāḥ tasmād bahuputra eṣa udgītha ity evopāsitavyam iti | tṛtīye 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | tṛtīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
2.9.d: तद् उ होवाच शाट्यायनिर् बहुपुत्र एष उद्गीथ इत्य् एवोपासितव्यम् बहवो ह्य् एत आदित्यस्य रश्मयस् ते ऽस्य पुत्राः तस्माद् बहुपुत्र एष उद्गीथ इत्य् एवोपासितव्यम् इति । तृतीये ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः । तृतीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
2.9.e: And Śatyayani said this: " One should worship [saying]: 'Possessing many sons is this udgītha.^ For many are these rays of the sun. They are its sons. Therefore one should worship [saying]: 'Possessing many sons is this udgītha.''''''
2.9.m: And regarding this, Śāṭyāyani said: 'One should meditate on this udgītha simply as "rich in sons". For many are these rays of Āditya; they are his sons. Therefore one should meditate on this udgītha simply as "rich in sons".' / The third khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka. / The third anuvāka is concluded.

2.10.s: devāsurās samayatantety āhuḥ na ha vai tad devāsurās samyetire prajāpatiś ca ha vai tan mṛtyuś ca samyetāte |
2.10.d: देवासुरास् समयतन्तेत्य् आहुः न ह वै तद् देवासुरास् सम्येतिरे प्रजापतिश् च ह वै तन् मृत्युश् च सम्येताते ।
2.10.e: They say the gods and the Asuras strove together. Truly, the gods and the Asuras did not then strive together. Both Prajapati and Death then strove together.
2.10.m: They say: 'The gods and Asuras struggled together.' That was not the gods and Asuras struggling together; it was Prajāpati and Death who struggled together.

2.10.s: tasya ha prajāpater devāḥ priyāḥ putrā anta āsuḥ te 'dhriyanta tenodgātrā dīkṣāmahai yenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam iyāmeti |
2.10.d: तस्य ह प्रजापतेर् देवाः प्रियाः पुत्रा अन्त आसुः ते ऽध्रियन्त तेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहै येनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् इयामेति ।
2.10.e: Now the gods were near to this Prajapati, [being his] dear sons. They resolved; " Let us consecrate ourselves with that udgdtar by whom, having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, we may go to the heavenly world."
2.10.m: Now, the gods were Prajāpati's dear sons near him. They resolved: 'Let us consecrate ourselves with that udgātṛ through whom we may attain the heavenly world, having struck away death, having struck away evil.'

2.10.s: te 'bruvan vācodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.10.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् वाचोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.10.e: They said: " Let us consecrate ourselves with speech as udgdtar.''''
2.10.m: They said: 'Let us consecrate ourselves with speech as udgātṛ.'

2.10.s: te vācodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idaṃ vāg āgāyad yad idaṃ vācā vadati yad idaṃ vācā bhuñjate |
2.10.d: ते वाचोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदं वाग् आगायद् यद् इदं वाचा वदति यद् इदं वाचा भुञ्जते ।
2.10.e: They consecrated themselves with speech as udgdtar. Speech sang to them that which one speaks here with speech, which one enjoys here with speech.
2.10.m: They consecrated themselves with speech as udgātṛ. Speech sang out for them what one speaks with speech and what one enjoys with speech.

2.10.s: tām pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva vācā pāpaṃ vadati sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.10.d: ताम् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव वाचा पापं वदति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.10.e: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one speaks with speech, that is that evil.
2.10.m: Evil was created following upon it. That bad [speech] which one speaks with speech, just that is that evil.

2.10.s: te 'bruvan na vai no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt manasodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.10.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् न वै नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् मनसोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.10.e: They said: "Verily, this one hath not carried us beyond death nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with mind as udgdtar.''''
2.10.m: They said: 'This one did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with mind as udgātṛ.'

2.10.s: te manasodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idam mana āgāyad yad idam manasā dhyāyati yad idam manasā bhuñjate |
2.10.d: ते मनसोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदम् मन आगायद् यद् इदम् मनसा ध्यायति यद् इदम् मनसा भुञ्जते ।
2.10.e: They consecrated themselves with mind as udgdtar. Mind sang to them that which one thinks here with the mind, which one enjoys here with the mind.
2.10.m: They consecrated themselves with mind as udgātṛ. Mind sang out for them what one thinks with the mind and what one enjoys with the mind.

2.10.s: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva manasā pāpaṃ dhyāyati sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.10.d: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव मनसा पापं ध्यायति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.10.e: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one thinks with the mind, that is that evil.
2.10.m: Evil was created following upon it. That bad [thought] which one thinks with the mind, just that is that evil.

2.10.s: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt cakṣuṣodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.10.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् चक्षुषोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.10.e: They said: " Verily, this one, too, hath not carried us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with sight as udgdtar.^''
2.10.m: They said: 'This one certainly did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with sight as udgātṛ.'

2.10.s: te cakṣuṣodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idaṃ cakṣur āgāyad yad idaṃ cakṣuṣā paśyati yad idaṃ cakṣuṣā bhuñjate |
2.10.d: ते चक्षुषोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदं चक्षुर् आगायद् यद् इदं चक्षुषा पश्यति यद् इदं चक्षुषा भुञ्जते ।
2.10.e: They consecrated themselves with sight as udgdtar. Sight sang to them that which one sees here with sight, which one enjoys here with sight.
2.10.m: They consecrated themselves with sight as udgātṛ. Sight sang out for them what one sees with sight and what one enjoys with sight.

2.10.s: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva cakṣuṣā pāpam paśyati sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.10.d: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव चक्षुषा पापम् पश्यति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.10.e: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one sees with sight, that is that evil,
2.10.m: Evil was created following upon it. That bad [sight] which one sees with sight, just that is that evil.

2.10.s: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt śrotreṇodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.10.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् श्रोत्रेणोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.10.e: They said: " Verily, this one, too, hath not carried us beyond death nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with hearing as udgdtar.''''
2.10.m: They said: 'This one certainly did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with hearing as udgātṛ.'

2.10.s: te śrotreṇodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idaṃ śrotram āgāyad yad idaṃ śrotreṇa śṛṇoti yad idaṃ śrotreṇa bhuñjate |
2.10.d: ते श्रोत्रेणोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदं श्रोत्रम् आगायद् यद् इदं श्रोत्रेण शृणोति यद् इदं श्रोत्रेण भुञ्जते ।
2.10.e: They consecrated themselves with hearing as udgdtar. Hearing sang to them that which one hears here with hearing, which one enjoys here with hearing.
2.10.m: They consecrated themselves with hearing as udgātṛ. Hearing sang out for them what one hears with hearing and what one enjoys with hearing.

2.10.s: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva śrotreṇa pāpaṃ śṛṇoti sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.10.d: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव श्रोत्रेण पापं शृणोति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.10.e: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one hears with hearing, that is that evil.
2.10.m: Evil was created following upon it. That bad [sound] which one hears with hearing, just that is that evil.

2.10.s: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt prāṇenodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.10.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् प्राणेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.10.e: They said: "Verily, this one, too, hath not carried us beyond death nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with breath as udgdtar.''''
2.10.m: They said: 'This one certainly did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with breath as udgātṛ.'

2.10.s: te prāṇenodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idam prāṇa āgāyad yad idam prāṇena prāṇiti yad idam prāṇena bhuñjate |
2.10.d: ते प्राणेनोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदम् प्राण आगायद् यद् इदम् प्राणेन प्राणिति यद् इदम् प्राणेन भुञ्जते ।
2.10.e: They consecrated themselves with breath as udgdtar. Breath sang to them that which one breathes here with breath, which one enjoys here with breath.
2.10.m: They consecrated themselves with breath as udgātṛ. Breath sang out for them what one breathes with breath and what one enjoys with breath.

2.10.s: tam pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva prāṇena prāṇiti sa eva sa pāpmā |
2.10.d: तम् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव प्राणेन प्राणिति स एव स पाप्मा ।
2.10.e: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one breathes with breath, that is that evil.
2.10.m: Evil was created following upon it. That [evil] which one breathes with breath, just that is that evil.

2.10.s: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt anena mukhyena prāṇenodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
2.10.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् अनेन मुख्येन प्राणेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
2.10.e: They said: " Verily, this one, too, hath not carried us beyond death nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with this breath of the mouth as udgdtar.''''
2.10.m: They said: 'This one certainly did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with this breath in the mouth as udgātṛ.'

2.10.s: te 'nena mukhyena prāṇenodgātrādīkṣanta |
2.10.d: ते ऽनेन मुख्येन प्राणेनोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त ।
2.10.e: They consecrated themselves with this breath of the mouth as udgdtar.
2.10.m: They consecrated themselves with this breath in the mouth as udgātṛ.

2.10.s: so 'bravīn mṛtyur eṣa eṣāṃ sa udgātā yena mṛtyum atyeṣyantīti |
2.10.d: सो ऽब्रवीन् मृत्युर् एष एषां स उद्गाता येन मृत्युम् अत्येष्यन्तीति ।
2.10.e: Death said: " This is that udgdtar by whom they will go beyond death."
2.10.m: Death said: 'This is that udgātṛ of theirs through whom they will pass beyond death.'

2.10.s: na hy etena prāṇena pāpaṃ vadati na pāpaṃ dhyāyati na pāpam paśyati na pāpaṃ śṛṇoti na pāpaṃ gandham apāniti |
2.10.d: न ह्य् एतेन प्राणेन पापं वदति न पापं ध्यायति न पापम् पश्यति न पापं शृणोति न पापं गन्धम् अपानिति ।
2.10.e: For with this breath one speaks no evil thing, thinks no evil thing, sees no evil thing, hears no evil thing, exhales no evil odor.
2.10.m: For with this breath, one does not speak evil, does not think evil, does not see evil, does not hear evil, and does not inhale bad smell.

2.10.s: tenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam āyan apahatya haiva mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam eti ya evaṃ veda | caturthe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.10.d: तेनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् अपहत्य हैव मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् एति य एवं वेद । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
2.10.e: By him having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, they went to the heavenly world. Having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, he goes to the heavenly world who knows thus.
2.10.m: Having struck away death, having struck away evil with it, they went to the heavenly world. He strikes away death, strikes away evil, and goes to the heavenly world, who knows thus. / The first khaṇḍa in the fourth anuvāka.

2.11.s: sa yathā hatvā pramṛdyātīyād evam evaitam mṛtyum atyāyan |
2.11.d: स यथा हत्वा प्रमृद्यातीयाद् एवम् एवैतम् मृत्युम् अत्यायन् ।
2.11.e: As one would pass beyond [another], having smitten him, having crushed him, even so they passed beyond that death.
2.11.m: Just as one would pass beyond [an enemy] having slain and crushed him, so indeed did they pass beyond this death.

2.11.s: sa vācam prathamām atyavahat tām pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt so 'gnir abhavat |
2.11.d: स वाचम् प्रथमाम् अत्यवहत् ताम् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् सो ऽग्निर् अभवत् ।
2.11.e: Speech he carried beyond it first. He deposited it beyond death. It became fire.
2.11.m: It carried speech beyond first. It deposited it beyond death; that became Agni.

2.11.s: atha mano 'tyavahat tat pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt sa candramā abhavat |
2.11.d: अथ मनो ऽत्यवहत् तत् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् स चन्द्रमा अभवत् ।
2.11.e: Then he carried mind beyond it. He deposited it beyond death. It became the moon.
2.11.m: Then it carried mind beyond. It deposited it beyond death; that became the Moon.

2.11.s: atha cakṣur atyavahat tat pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt sa ādityo 'bhavat |
2.11.d: अथ चक्षुर् अत्यवहत् तत् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् स आदित्यो ऽभवत् ।
2.11.e: Then he carried sight beyond it. He deposited it beyond death. It became the sun.
2.11.m: Then it carried sight beyond. It deposited it beyond death; that became Āditya.

2.11.s: atha śrotram atyavahat tat pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt tā imā diśo 'bhavan tā u eva viśve devāḥ |
2.11.d: अथ श्रोत्रम् अत्यवहत् तत् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् ता इमा दिशो ऽभवन् ता उ एव विश्वे देवाः ।
2.11.e: Then he carried hearing beyond it. He deposited it beyond death. It became these quarters; they are also all the gods.
2.11.m: Then it carried hearing beyond. It deposited it beyond death; they became these directions; they are indeed the Viśve Devas.

2.11.s: atha prāṇam atyavahat tam pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt sa vāyur abhavat |
2.11.d: अथ प्राणम् अत्यवहत् तम् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् स वायुर् अभवत् ।
2.11.e: Then he carried breath beyond it. He deposited it beyond death. It became wind.
2.11.m: Then it carried breath beyond. It deposited it beyond death; that became Vāyu.

2.11.e: Then he sang food-eating for himself only.
2.11.m: Then for itself alone, it sang out food.

2.11.s: sa eṣa evāyāsyaḥ āsye dhīyate tasmād ayāsyaḥ yad v evāyam āsye ramate tasmād v evāyāsyaḥ |
2.11.d: स एष एवायास्यः आस्ये धीयते तस्माद् अयास्यः यद् व् एवायम् आस्ये रमते तस्माद् व् एवायास्यः ।
2.11.e: That same is Ayasya. He (ayam) is placed in the mouth [dsya); therefore he is [called] Ayasya. And as he rests in the mouth, therefore also he is [called] Ayasya.
2.11.m: That very one is Ayāsya: it is placed in the mouth (āsya), therefore it is Ayāsya; or because it delights (ramate) in the mouth, therefore it is Ayāsya.

2.11.s: sa eṣa evāṅgirasaḥ ato hīmāny aṅgāni rasaṃ labhante tasmād āṅgirasaḥ yad v evaiṣām aṅgānāṃ rasas tasmād v evāṅgirasaḥ |
2.11.d: स एष एवाङ्गिरसः अतो हीमान्य् अङ्गानि रसं लभन्ते तस्माद् आङ्गिरसः यद् व् एवैषाम् अङ्गानां रसस् तस्माद् व् एवाङ्गिरसः ।
2.11.e: That same is Angirasa. For from him these limbs (anga) take their sap (rasa); therefore he is [called] Angirasa. And because he is the sap of these limbs, therefore also he is Angirasa.
2.11.m: That very one is Āṅgirasa: for from it these limbs (aṅgāni) obtain essence (rasam), therefore it is Āṅgirasa; or because it is the essence of these limbs, therefore it is Āṅgirasa.

2.11.s: taṃ devā abruvan kevalaṃ vā ātmane 'nnādyam āgāsīḥ anu na etasminn annādya ābhaja etad asyānāmayatvam astīti |
2.11.d: तं देवा अब्रुवन् केवलं वा आत्मने ऽन्नाद्यम् आगासीः अनु न एतस्मिन्न् अन्नाद्य आभज एतद् अस्यानामयत्वम् अस्तीति ।
2.11.e: The gods said to him: " Only for thyself hast thou sung foodeating. Let us also have a share in this food-eating. That is his immunity from illness (?)."
2.11.m: The gods said to it: 'You have sung out food for yourself alone. Grant us a share in this food; thus may this [body] be free from disease.'

2.11.s: taṃ vai praviśateti sa vā ākāśān kuruṣveti sa imān prāṇān ākāśān akuruta |
2.11.d: तं वै प्रविशतेति स वा आकाशान् कुरुष्वेति स इमान् प्राणान् आकाशान् अकुरुत ।
2.11.e: "Verily enter that." "Then make spaces." He made these breaths spaces [for them]. \i. Fire, having become speech, entered that; [so did] the moon, having become mind; the sun, having become light; the quarters, having become hearing; the wind, having become breath,
2.11.m: [It said:] 'Enter into me, then.' [They said:] 'Then make spaces [for us].' It made these vital breaths into spaces.

2.11.s: taṃ vāg eva bhūtvāgniḥ prāviśan mano bhūtvā candramāś cakṣur bhūtvādityaś śrotram bhūtvā diśaḥ prāṇo bhūtvā vāyuḥ |
2.11.d: तं वाग् एव भूत्वाग्निः प्राविशन् मनो भूत्वा चन्द्रमाश् चक्षुर् भूत्वादित्यश् श्रोत्रम् भूत्वा दिशः प्राणो भूत्वा वायुः ।
2.11.e: Verily, this is the divine assembly, the divine congregation, the divine conference.
2.11.m: Becoming speech, Agni entered it; becoming mind, the Moon; becoming sight, Āditya; becoming hearing, the directions; becoming breath, Vāyu.

2.11.s: eṣā vai daivī pariṣad daivī sabhā daivī saṃsat |
2.11.d: एषा वै दैवी परिषद् दैवी सभा दैवी संसत् ।
2.11.m: This indeed is the divine assembly, the divine gathering, the divine council.

2.11.s: gacchati ha vā etāṃ daivīm pariṣadaṃ daivīṃ sabhāṃ daivīṃ saṃsadaṃ ya evaṃ veda | caturthe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.11.d: गच्छति ह वा एतां दैवीम् परिषदं दैवीं सभां दैवीं संसदं य एवं वेद । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
2.11.e: He goes to that divine assembly, divine congregation, divine conference, who knows thus.
2.11.m: He indeed goes to this divine assembly, divine gathering, divine council, who knows thus. / The second khaṇḍa in the fourth anuvāka.

2.12.s: yatro ha vai kva caitā devatā nispṛśanti na haiva tatra kaś cana pāpmā nyaṅgaḥ pariśiṣyate |
2.12.d: यत्रो ह वै क्व चैता देवता निस्पृशन्ति न हैव तत्र कश् चन पाप्मा न्यङ्गः परिशिष्यते ।
2.12.e: Verily, wheresoever these divinities touch, there no evil whatever, [not a] trace, is left.
2.12.m: Wherever indeed these deities touch, not the least trace of evil is left behind.

2.12.s: sa vidyān neha kaś cana pāpmā nyaṅgaḥ pariśekṣyate sarvam evaitā devatāḥ pāpmānaṃ nidhakṣyantīti tathā haiva bhavati |
2.12.d: स विद्यान् नेह कश् चन पाप्मा न्यङ्गः परिशेक्ष्यते सर्वम् एवैता देवताः पाप्मानं निधक्ष्यन्तीति तथा हैव भवति ।
2.12.e: He should know: "No evil whatever, [not a] trace, will be left here; these divinities will burn down all evil." Truly it happens thus.
2.12.m: He should know: 'No trace of evil will be left behind here; these deities will burn up all evil.' Thus indeed it happens.

2.12.s: ya u ha vā evaṃvidam ṛcchati yathaitā devatā ṛtvā nīyād evaṃ nyeti etāsu hy evainaṃ devatāsu prapannam etāsu vasantam upavadati |
2.12.d: य उ ह वा एवंविदम् ऋच्छति यथैता देवता ऋत्वा नीयाद् एवं न्येति एतासु ह्य् एवैनं देवतासु प्रपन्नम् एतासु वसन्तम् उपवदति ।
2.12.e: And whoso encounters one knowing thus, as one having encountered these divinities would perish, even so he perishes. For he speaks ill of him who has resorted to these divinities, who dwells in them.
2.12.m: And whoever offends one who knows thus, just as if one were to perish having collided with these deities, so does he perish. For he speaks ill of him who has taken refuge in these deities, who dwells in them.

2.12.s: tasya haitasya naiva kā canārtir asti ya evaṃ veda ya evainam upavadati sa ārtim ārcchati |
2.12.d: तस्य हैतस्य नैव का चनार्तिर् अस्ति य एवं वेद य एवैनम् उपवदति स आर्तिम् आर्च्छति ।
2.12.e: Verily, of one who knows thus there is no misfortune whatever; he who speaks ill of one knowing thus, he meets with misfortune.
2.12.m: There is no misfortune whatsoever for him who knows thus. Whoever speaks ill of him, he incurs misfortune.

2.12.s: sa ya enam ṛcchād eva tā devatā upasṛtya brūyād ayam mārat sa imām ārtiṃ nyetv iti tāṃ haivārtiṃ nyeti |
2.12.d: स य एनम् ऋच्छाद् एव ता देवता उपसृत्य ब्रूयाद् अयम् मारत् स इमाम् आर्तिं न्येत्व् इति तां हैवार्तिं न्येति ।
2.12.e: If one should harm him, he should say, approaching these divinities: " This one hath harmed me. Let him go down unto this misfortune." He goes down unto that misfortune.
2.12.m: Whoever should offend him, he should approach those deities and say: 'This one has offended me; let him perish in this misfortune.' Thus he perishes in that misfortune.

2.12.s: yāvadāvāsā u hāsyeme prāṇā asmiṃl loka etāvadāvāsā u hāsyaitā devatā amuṣmiṃl loke bhavanti |
2.12.d: यावदावासा उ हास्येमे प्राणा अस्मिंल् लोक एतावदावासा उ हास्यैता देवता अमुष्मिंल् लोके भवन्ति ।
2.12.e: And as many abodes as these breaths of him have in this world, so many abodes these divinities of him come to have in yonder world.
2.12.m: As many dwellings as these vital breaths of his have in this world, so many dwellings do these deities of his have in yonder world.

2.12.s: tasmād u haivaṃ vidvān naivāgṛhatāyai bibhīyān nālokatāyai etā me devatā asmiṃl loke gṛhān kariṣyanti etā amuṣmiṃl loke bhavanti tasmād u lokam pradāsyantīti |
2.12.d: तस्माद् उ हैवं विद्वान् नैवागृहतायै बिभीयान् नालोकतायै एता मे देवता अस्मिंल् लोके गृहान् करिष्यन्ति एता अमुष्मिंल् लोके भवन्ति तस्माद् उ लोकम् प्रदास्यन्तीति ।
2.12.e: Therefore one knowing thus should not be in fear of houselessness, nor of worldlessness [thinking]: "These divinities will make houses for me in this world. They come to be in yonder world; and therefore they will give me the world."
2.12.m: Therefore, one who knows thus should neither fear being without a house nor being without a world: 'These deities will make houses for me in this world; they are in yonder world, and therefore they will give me a world.'

2.12.s: tasmād u haivaṃ vidvān naivāgṛhatāyai bibhīyān nālokatāyai etā me devatā asmiṃl loke gṛhebhyo gṛhān kariṣyanti svebhya āyatanebhya iti haiva vidyād devatā amuṣmiṃl loke lokam pradāsyantīti |
2.12.d: तस्माद् उ हैवं विद्वान् नैवागृहतायै बिभीयान् नालोकतायै एता मे देवता अस्मिंल् लोके गृहेभ्यो गृहान् करिष्यन्ति स्वेभ्य आयतनेभ्य इति हैव विद्याद् देवता अमुष्मिंल् लोके लोकम् प्रदास्यन्तीति ।
2.12.e: And therefore one knowing thus should not be in fe,ar of houselessness, nor of worldlessness. "These divinities will make in this world houses for me from [their] houses, from abodes of their own," he should know; "these divinities will give a world in yonder world."
2.12.m: Therefore, one who knows thus should neither fear being without a house nor being without a world: 'These deities will make houses for me in this world for the sake of their own homes,' thus indeed should he know; '[these] deities will give a world in yonder world.'

2.12.s: tasmād u haivaṃ vidvān naivāgṛhatāyai bibhīyān nālokatāyai etā ma etad ubhayaṃ saṃnaṃsyantīti haiva vidyāt tathā haiva bhavati | caturthe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ caturtho 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
2.12.d: तस्माद् उ हैवं विद्वान् नैवागृहतायै बिभीयान् नालोकतायै एता म एतद् उभयं संनंस्यन्तीति हैव विद्यात् तथा हैव भवति । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः चतुर्थो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
2.12.e: And therefore one knowing thus should not be in fear of houselessness, nor of worldlessness. Let him know: " They will bring about both for me." Verily so it comes to pass.
2.12.m: Therefore, one who knows thus should fear neither being without a home nor being without a world. One should know: 'These [deities] will bring about both for me.' And so it indeed happens. / Third khaṇḍa in the fourth anuvāka. The fourth anuvāka is completed.

2.13.s: devā vai brahmaṇo vatsena vācam aduhran agnir ha vai brahmaṇo vatsaḥ |
2.13.d: देवा वै ब्रह्मणो वत्सेन वाचम् अदुह्रन् अग्निर् ह वै ब्रह्मणो वत्सः ।
2.13.e: Verily, the gods milked speech by means of the calf of the brahman. Verily, fire is the calf of the brahman.
2.13.m: The gods milked speech by means of the calf of brahman. Agni is indeed the calf of brahman.

2.13.s: sā yā sā vāg brahmaiva tat atha yo 'gnir mṛtyus saḥ |
2.13.d: सा या सा वाग् ब्रह्मैव तत् अथ यो ऽग्निर् मृत्युस् सः ।
2.13.e: This speech, that is the brahman; and fire, that is death. From this same speech—as one would milk a given cow by means of a calf, admitting [it to her]—even so the gods milked from speech all desires.
2.13.m: That which is speech is brahman itself. And that which is Agni is death.

2.13.s: tām etāṃ vācaṃ yathā dhenuṃ vatsenopasṛjya prattāṃ duhītaivam eva devā vācaṃ sarvān kāmān aduhran |
2.13.d: ताम् एतां वाचं यथा धेनुं वत्सेनोपसृज्य प्रत्तां दुहीतैवम् एव देवा वाचं सर्वान् कामान् अदुह्रन् ।
2.13.m: Just as one would milk that speech, having brought the calf near like a cow, when she has yielded [her milk], even so the gods milked all desires from speech.

2.13.s: duhe ha vai vācaṃ sarvān kāmān ya evaṃ veda sa haiṣo 'nānṛto vācaṃ devīm udindhe vada vada vadeti |
2.13.d: दुहे ह वै वाचं सर्वान् कामान् य एवं वेद स हैषो ऽनानृतो वाचं देवीम् उदिन्धे वद वद वदेति ।
2.13.e: Verily, he milks from speech all desires who knows thus. He, not being untruthful, kindles (?) divine speech [saying]: " Speak, speak, speak."
2.13.m: He indeed milks all desires from speech who knows thus. Unduped, he kindles the divine speech, saying: 'Speak, speak, speak!'

2.13.s: tad yad iha puruṣasya pāpaṃ kṛtam bhavati tad āviṣkaroti yad ihainad api rahasīva kurvan manyate 'tha hainad āvir eva karoti tasmād vāva pāpaṃ na kuryāt | pañcame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.13.d: तद् यद् इह पुरुषस्य पापं कृतम् भवति तद् आविष्करोति यद् इहैनद् अपि रहसीव कुर्वन् मन्यते ऽथ हैनद् आविर् एव करोति तस्माद् वाव पापं न कुर्यात् । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
2.13.e: What evil is done here by man, that it makes manifest. Although he thinks that he does it secretly, as it were, still it makes it manifest. Verily, therefore he should not do evil.
2.13.m: Whatever evil is done here by a man, that it brings to light. Even what one thinks he does here in secret, as it were, that it brings to light. Therefore, one should not do evil. / First khaṇḍa in the fifth anuvāka.

2.14.s: eṣa u ha vāva devānāṃ nediṣṭham upacaryo yad agniḥ |
2.14.d: एष उ ह वाव देवानां नेदिष्ठम् उपचर्यो यद् अग्निः ।
2.14.e: Verily, he of the gods is to be next served, viz. Agni.
2.14.m: This Agni is indeed to be served nearest of all the gods.

2.14.s: taṃ sādhūpacaret ya enam asmiṃl loke sādhūpacarati tam eṣo 'muṣmiṃl loke sādhūpacarati atha ya enam asmiṃl loke nādriyate tam eṣo 'muṣmiṃl loke nādriyate tasmād vā agniṃ sādhūpacaret |
2.14.d: तं साधूपचरेत् य एनम् अस्मिंल् लोके साधूपचरति तम् एषो ऽमुष्मिंल् लोके साधूपचरति अथ य एनम् अस्मिंल् लोके नाद्रियते तम् एषो ऽमुष्मिंल् लोके नाद्रियते तस्माद् वा अग्निं साधूपचरेत् ।
2.14.e: Him one should serve well. Whoso serves him well in this world, him he (A.) serves well in yonder world. And who does not care for him in this world, him he (A.) does not care for in yonder world. Verily, therefore one should serve Agni well.
2.14.m: One should serve him well. Whoever serves him well in this world, him this [Agni] serves well in yonder world. But whoever does not respect him in this world, him this [Agni] does not respect in yonder world. Therefore, one should serve Agni well.

2.14.s: taṃ naiva hastābhyāṃ spṛśen na pādābhyāṃ na daṇḍena |
2.14.d: तं नैव हस्ताभ्यां स्पृशेन् न पादाभ्यां न दण्डेन ।
2.14.e: Him one should not touch with the hands, nor with the feet, nor with a stick.
2.14.m: One should not touch him with one's hands, nor with one's feet, nor with a stick.

2.14.s: hastābhyāṃ spṛśati yad asyāntikam avanenikte atha yad abhiprasārayati tat pādābhyām |
2.14.d: हस्ताभ्यां स्पृशति यद् अस्यान्तिकम् अवनेनिक्ते अथ यद् अभिप्रसारयति तत् पादाभ्याम् ।
2.14.e: He touches him with the hands, when he washes himself in his neighborhood; and when he stretches himself out towards [him], then [he touches him] with the feet.
2.14.m: One touches him with one's hands when one washes oneself near him; and when one stretches out towards him, that is with the feet.

2.14.s: sa enam āspṛṣta īśvaro durdhāyāṃ dhātoḥ tasmād vā agniṃ sādhūpacarati sudhāyāṃ haivainaṃ dadhāti | pañcame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
2.14.d: स एनम् आस्पृष्त ईश्वरो दुर्धायां धातोः तस्माद् वा अग्निं साधूपचरति सुधायां हैवैनं दधाति । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
2.14.e: He, being touched, is liable to place him in discomfort. Therefore one serves Agni well. Truly, he places such a one in comfort.
2.14.m: He, having been touched, is capable of placing him in distress. Therefore, one serves Agni well; and he places him in well-being. / Second khaṇḍa in the fifth anuvāka.

2.15.s: eṣa u ha vāva devānām mahāśanatamo yad agniḥ |
2.15.d: एष उ ह वाव देवानाम् महाशनतमो यद् अग्निः ।
2.15.e: And verily he of the gods is the most voracious one, viz. Agni.
2.15.m: This Agni is indeed the greatest eater among the gods.

2.15.s: tan na vratyam adadāno 'śnīyāt yo vai mahāśane 'naśnaty aśnātīśvāro hainam abhiṣaṅktoḥ pūtim iva hāśnīyāt |
2.15.d: तन् न व्रत्यम् अददानो ऽश्नीयात् यो वै महाशने ऽनश्नत्य् अश्नातीश्वारो हैनम् अभिषङ्क्तोः पूतिम् इव हाश्नीयात् ।
2.15.m: Therefore, one should not eat without having given him his vow-portion. He who eats while the great eater is not eating, [the fire] is capable of seizing him; he would eat as if it were putrid.

2.15.s: atho ha prokte 'śane brūyāt samintsvāgnim iti sa yathā prokte 'śane śreyāṃsam pariveṣṭavai brūyāt tādṛk tat |
2.15.d: अथो ह प्रोक्ते ऽशने ब्रूयात् समिन्त्स्वाग्निम् इति स यथा प्रोक्ते ऽशने श्रेयांसम् परिवेष्टवै ब्रूयात् तादृक् तत् ।
2.15.e: Therefore he should not eat what belongs to a vow without having given [him]. Verily, if one eats while the voracious one does not eat, he is likely to fasten on him. Truly he would eat what is putrid, as it were. a. So then, when the meal is announced, he should say: " Kindle the fire." As, when the meal is announced, one would direct that one's superior be served [first], even so is that.
