2.15.m: And when the meal has been announced, he should say: 'Kindle Agni!' That is just as when a meal has been announced, one would tell an elder to serve [food].

2.15.s: etad u ha vāva sāma yad vāk yo vai cakṣus sāma śrotraṃ sāmety upāste na ha tena karoti |
2.15.d: एतद् उ ह वाव साम यद् वाक् यो वै चक्षुस् साम श्रोत्रं सामेत्य् उपास्ते न ह तेन करोति ।
2.15.e: And that is also the sāman, viz. speech. Verily, he who worships [saying]: "Sight is the sāman; hearing is the sāman,'''' he does not thereby perform it.
2.15.m: The sāman is indeed speech. He who worships [thinking]: 'The eye is the sāman, the ear is the sāman,' does not accomplish anything by that.

2.15.s: atha ya ādityas sāma candramās sāmety upāste na haiva tena karoti |
2.15.d: अथ य आदित्यस् साम चन्द्रमास् सामेत्य् उपास्ते न हैव तेन करोति ।
2.15.e: And he who worships [saying]: " The sun is the sāman; the moon is the sāman" he does not thereby perform it.
2.15.m: And he who worships [thinking]: 'The sun is the sāman, the moon is the sāman,' does not accomplish anything by that.

2.15.s: atha yo vāk sāmety upāste sa evānuṣṭhyā sāma veda vācā hi sāmnārtvijyaṃ kriyate |
2.15.d: अथ यो वाक् सामेत्य् उपास्ते स एवानुष्ठ्या साम वेद वाचा हि साम्नार्त्विज्यं क्रियते ।
2.15.e: Now he who worships [saying]: " Speech is the sāman" he at once knows the sdm,an. For with speech as the sāman the priestly office is performed.
2.15.m: But he who worships [thinking]: 'Speech is the sāman,' he alone knows the sāman according to its proper order. For by speech the priestly office is performed with the sāman.

2.15.s: sa yo vācas svaro jāyate so 'gnir vāg v eva vāk tad atraikadhā sāma bhavati |
2.15.d: स यो वाचस् स्वरो जायते सो ऽग्निर् वाग् व् एव वाक् तद् अत्रैकधा साम भवति ।
2.15.e: The tone which is born from speech, that is Agni, and speech is just speech. That becomes here one, the sāman.
2.15.m: The tone that arises from speech, that is Agni; but speech is indeed speech. Thus here the sāman becomes one.

2.15.s: sa ya evam etad ekadhā sāma bhavad vedaivaṃ haitad ekadhā sāma bhavatīty ekadheva śreṣṭhas svānām bhavati |
2.15.d: स य एवम् एतद् एकधा साम भवद् वेदैवं हैतद् एकधा साम भवतीत्य् एकधेव श्रेष्ठस् स्वानाम् भवति ।
2.15.e: He who thus knows that which becomes one, the sdm,an [saying]: "Verily that becomes one, the sāman" he becomes one, as it were, the best of his [people].
2.15.m: He who knows this sāman as becoming one, that this sāman thus becomes one, becomes singly the best among his own people.

2.15.s: tasmād u haivaṃvidam eva sāmnārtvijyaṃ kārayeta sa ha vāva sāma veda ya evaṃ veda | pañcame 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | pañcamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
2.15.d: तस्माद् उ हैवंविदम् एव साम्नार्त्विज्यं कारयेत स ह वाव साम वेद य एवं वेद । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः । पञ्चमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
2.15.e: And therefore one should cause one knowing thus to perform the priestly office with the sāman. Verily he knows the sāman who knows thus.
2.15.m: Therefore, one should have the priestly office performed with the sāman only by one who knows thus. He indeed knows the sāman who knows thus. / Third khaṇḍa in the fifth anuvāka. The fifth anuvāka is completed.

3.1.s: ekā ha vāva kṛtsnā devatārdhadevatā evānyāḥ ayam eva yo 'yam pavate |
3.1.d: एका ह वाव कृत्स्ना देवतार्धदेवता एवान्याः अयम् एव यो ऽयम् पवते ।
3.1.e: One entire deity there is; the others are half-deities. [It is] this one namely who cleanses here (the wind).
3.1.m: One deity alone is complete; the other deities are only half-deities: namely, this one who purifies here [the wind].

3.1.s: eṣa eva sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ grahāḥ |
3.1.d: एष एव सर्वेषां देवानां ग्रहाः ।
3.1.e: He [represents] the seizers of all the gods.
3.1.m: He alone is the cups of all the gods.

3.1.s: sa haiṣo 'staṃ nāma astam iti heha paścād grahān ācakṣate |
3.1.d: स हैषो ऽस्तं नाम अस्तम् इति हेह पश्चाद् ग्रहान् आचक्षते ।
3.1.e: He, indeed, is'setting' by name. ' Setting' they call here the seizers in the west.
3.1.m: He is indeed named 'home' (asta). For here behind, they call the grahas 'the home'.

3.1.s: sa yad ādityo 'stam agād iti grahān agād iti haitat tena so 'sarvaḥ sa etam evāpyeti |
3.1.d: स यद् आदित्यो ऽस्तम् अगाद् इति ग्रहान् अगाद् इति हैतत् तेन सो ऽसर्वः स एतम् एवाप्येति ।
3.1.e: In that the sun has gone to setting, it has gone to the seizers. Therefore it is not whole. It goes unto that [god].
3.1.m: When [people say]: 'The sun has set (astam agāt),' this means: 'He has gone to the grahas.' By that he is incomplete. He merges into this one alone.

3.1.s: astaṃ candramā eti tena so 'sarvaḥ sa etam evāpyeti |
3.1.d: अस्तं चन्द्रमा एति तेन सो ऽसर्वः स एतम् एवाप्येति ।
3.1.e: The moon sets. Therefore it is not whole. It goes unto that [god].
3.1.m: The moon sets. By that it is incomplete. It merges into this one alone.

3.1.s: astaṃ nakṣatrāṇi yanti tena tāny asarvāṇi tāny etam evāpiyanti |
3.1.d: अस्तं नक्षत्राणि यन्ति तेन तान्य् असर्वाणि तान्य् एतम् एवापियन्ति ।
3.1.e: The asterisms set. Therefore they are not whole. They go unto that [god].
3.1.m: The lunar mansions set. By that they are incomplete. They merge into this one alone.

3.1.s: anv agnir gacchati tena so 'sarvaḥ sa etam evāpyeti |
3.1.d: अन्व् अग्निर् गच्छति तेन सो ऽसर्वः स एतम् एवाप्येति ।
3.1.e: The fire goes out. Therefore it is not whole. It goes unto that [god],
3.1.m: Fire goes out. By that it is incomplete. It merges into this one alone.

3.1.s: ety ahaḥ eti rātriḥ tena te asarve te etam evāpītaḥ |
3.1.d: एत्य् अहः एति रात्रिः तेन ते असर्वे ते एतम् एवापीतः ।
3.1.e: Day goes; night goes. Therefore they are not whole. They go unto that [god].
3.1.m: Day departs; night departs. By that they are incomplete. They merge into this one alone.

3.1.s: muhyanti diśo na vai tā rātrim prajñāyante tena tā asarvāḥ tā etam evāpiyanti |
3.1.d: मुह्यन्ति दिशो न वै ता रात्रिम् प्रज्ञायन्ते तेन ता असर्वाः ता एतम् एवापियन्ति ।
3.1.e: The quarters are confounded; they are not known by night. Therefore they are not whole. They go unto that [god].
3.1.m: The directions become confused; they are not discerned at night. By that they are incomplete. They merge into this one alone.

3.1.s: varṣati ca parjanya uc ca gṛhṇāti tena so 'sarvaḥ sa etam evāpyeti |
3.1.d: वर्षति च पर्जन्य उच् च गृह्णाति तेन सो ऽसर्वः स एतम् एवाप्येति ।
3.1.e: Parjanya rains and holds up. Therefore he is not whole. He goes unto that [god],
3.1.m: Parjanya rains and holds back [the rain]. By that he is incomplete. He merges into this one alone.

3.1.s: kṣīyanta āpa evam oṣadhaya evaṃ vanaspatayaḥ tena tāny asarvāṇi tāny etam evāpiyanti |
3.1.d: क्षीयन्त आप एवम् ओषधय एवं वनस्पतयः तेन तान्य् असर्वाणि तान्य् एतम् एवापियन्ति ।
3.1.e: The waters are exhausted, even so the herbs, even so the foresttrees. Therefore they are not whole. They go unto that [god],
3.1.m: Waters dwindle, plants likewise, trees likewise. By that they are incomplete. They merge into this one alone.

3.1.s: tad yad etat sarvaṃ vāyuṃ evāpyeti tasmād vāyur eva sāma |
3.1.d: तद् यद् एतत् सर्वं वायुं एवाप्येति तस्माद् वायुर् एव साम ।
3.1.e: So, as this all goes unto wind, therefore is wind the sāman.
3.1.m: Since all this merges into Vāyu alone, therefore Vāyu alone is the sāman.

3.1.s: sa ha vai sāmavit sa sāma veda ya evaṃ veda |
3.1.d: स ह वै सामवित् स साम वेद य एवं वेद ।
3.1.e: He is sāman-'know'mg, he knows the [entire] sāman, who knows thus.
3.1.m: He indeed is a knower of the sāman, he knows the complete sāman, who knows thus.

3.1.s: athādhyātmam na vai svapan vācā vadati seyam eva prāṇam apyeti |
3.1.d: अथाध्यात्मम् न वै स्वपन् वाचा वदति सेयम् एव प्राणम् अप्येति ।
3.1.e: Now with regard to the self. One who sleeps speaks not with the voice. That same [voice] goes unto breath,
3.1.m: Now as pertaining to the self. One who is sleeping does not speak with speech. It merges into the breath alone.

3.1.s: na manasā dhyāyati tad idam eva prāṇam apyeti |
3.1.d: न मनसा ध्यायति तद् इदम् एव प्राणम् अप्येति ।
3.1.e: He thinks not with the mind. That same [mind] goes unto breath.
3.1.m: He does not think with the mind. It merges into the breath alone.

3.1.s: na cakṣuṣā paśyati tad idam eva prāṇam apyeti |
3.1.d: न चक्षुषा पश्यति तद् इदम् एव प्राणम् अप्येति ।
3.1.e: He sees not with sight. That same [sight] goes unto breath.
3.1.m: He does not see with the eye. It merges into the breath alone.

3.1.s: na śrotreṇa śṛṇoti tad idam eva prāṇam apyeti |
3.1.d: न श्रोत्रेण शृणोति तद् इदम् एव प्राणम् अप्येति ।
3.1.e: He hears not witli hearing. That same [hearing] goes unto breath.
3.1.m: He does not hear with the ear. It merges into the breath alone.

3.1.s: tad yad etat sarvam prāṇam evābhisameti tasmāt prāṇa eva sāma |
3.1.d: तद् यद् एतत् सर्वम् प्राणम् एवाभिसमेति तस्मात् प्राण एव साम ।
3.1.e: So, as this all goes together unto breath, therefore is breath the sāman.
3.1.m: Since all this gathers together into the breath alone, therefore breath alone is the sāman.

3.1.s: sa ha vai sāmavit sa kṛtsnaṃ sāma veda ya evaṃ veda |
3.1.d: स ह वै सामवित् स कृत्स्नं साम वेद य एवं वेद ।
3.1.e: He is sawaw-knowing, he knows the entire sāman, who knows thus.
3.1.m: He indeed is a knower of the sāman, he knows the complete sāman, who knows thus.

3.1.s: tad yad idam āhur na batādya vātīti haitat puruṣe 'ntar niramate sa pūrṇas svedamāna āste |
3.1.d: तद् यद् इदम् आहुर् न बताद्य वातीति हैतत् पुरुषे ऽन्तर् निरमते स पूर्णस् स्वेदमान आस्ते ।
3.1.e: Now when they say: "Lo! it doth not blow to-day," it is then resting within man; he sits full, sweating.
3.1.m: As to what they say: 'Ah, the wind is not blowing today,' it rests inside the person; he sits filled and sweating.

3.1.s: tad dha śaunakaṃ ca kāpeyam abhipratāriṇaṃ ca brāhmaṇaḥ pariveviṣyamāṇā upāvavrāja | prathame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.1.d: तद् ध शौनकं च कापेयम् अभिप्रतारिणं च ब्राह्मणः परिवेविष्यमाणा उपावव्राज । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
3.1.e: Now unto Śaunaka Kapeya and Abhipratarin [Kaksaseni], while they were being waited upon, a Brahman came.
3.1.m: Now a brahmin approached Śaunaka Kāpeya and Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni while they were being served. / First khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

3.2.s: tau ha bibhikṣe taṃ ha nādadrāte ko vā ko veti manyamānau |
3.2.d: तौ ह बिभिक्षे तं ह नादद्राते को वा को वेति मन्यमानौ ।
3.2.e: He begged [food] of them. They paid no attention to him, thinking: "Who or who is he?"
3.2.m: He begged food of the two. Thinking, 'Who is he, anyway?' the two did not pay attention to him.

3.2.s: tau hopajagau mahātmanaś caturo deva ekaḥ kas sa jagāra bhuvanasya gopāḥ taṃ kāpeya na vijānanty eke 'bhipratārin bahudhā niviṣṭam iti |
3.2.d: तौ होपजगौ महात्मनश् चतुरो देव एकः कस् स जगार भुवनस्य गोपाः तं कापेय न विजानन्त्य् एके ऽभिप्रतारिन् बहुधा निविष्टम् इति ।
3.2.e: He sang unto them: "One [god]—who is he?—swallowed up four magnanimous ones, being a keeper of ci'eation; liim, O Kapeya, some do not know; him, O Abhipratarin, settled down in many places."
3.2.m: He sang beside them: / 'Four great-souled ones has the one god swallowed—who is that protector of the world? / Him, O Kāpeya, some do not recognize, O Abhipratārin, who is entered into many places.'

3.2.s: sa hovācābhipratārīmaṃ vāva prapadya pratibrūhīti tvayā vā ayam pratyucya iti |
3.2.d: स होवाचाभिप्रतारीमं वाव प्रपद्य प्रतिब्रूहीति त्वया वा अयम् प्रत्युच्य इति ।
3.2.e: Said Abhipratarin: " Stepping forward, answer this man; by thee must this man be answered."
3.2.m: Abhipratārin said: 'Go up to this one and answer him; he must be answered by you.'

3.2.s: taṃ ha pratyuvāca ātmā devānām uta martyānāṃ hiraṇyadanto rapaso na sūnuḥ mahāntam asya mahimānam āhur anadyamāno yad adantam attī ti |
3.2.d: तं ह प्रत्युवाच आत्मा देवानाम् उत मर्त्यानां हिरण्यदन्तो रपसो न सूनुः महान्तम् अस्य महिमानम् आहुर् अनद्यमानो यद् अदन्तम् अत्ती ति ।
3.2.e: Him he answered: " The self of the gods and of mortals, with golden teeth, defective (?), not a son. Great they call his greatness, in that he, not being eaten, eats him who eats."
3.2.m: He answered him: / 'The self of the gods and of mortals, with golden teeth, not the son of disease, / they speak of his great majesty, that uneaten, he eats the eater.'

3.2.s: mahātmanaś caturo eka iti vāg vā agniḥ sa mahātmā devaḥ sa yatra svapiti tad vācam prāṇo girati |
3.2.d: महात्मनश् चतुरो एक इति वाग् वा अग्निः स महात्मा देवः स यत्र स्वपिति तद् वाचम् प्राणो गिरति ।
3.2.e: 'One [god] four magnanimous ones:' speech verily is fire; that is a magnanimous god. When one sleeps, then breath swallows up speech.
3.2.m: 'Four great-souled ones has the one god [swallowed]'—speech is Agni; he is a great-souled god; when one sleeps, breath swallows speech.

3.2.s: manaś candramās sa mahātmā devaḥ sa yatra svapiti tan manaḥ prāṇo girati |
3.2.d: मनश् चन्द्रमास् स महात्मा देवः स यत्र स्वपिति तन् मनः प्राणो गिरति ।
3.2.e: Mind [is] the moon; that is a magnanimous god. When one sleeps, then breath swallows up mind.
3.2.m: The mind is the moon; he is a great-souled god; when one sleeps, breath swallows the mind.

3.2.s: cakṣur ādityas sa mahātmā devaḥ sa yatra svapiti tac cakṣuḥ prāṇo girati |
3.2.d: चक्षुर् आदित्यस् स महात्मा देवः स यत्र स्वपिति तच् चक्षुः प्राणो गिरति ।
3.2.e: Sight [is] the sun; that is a magnanimous god. When one sleeps, then breath swallows up sight,
3.2.m: The eye is the sun; he is a great-souled god; when one sleeps, breath swallows the eye.

3.2.s: śrotraṃ diśas tā mahātmāno devāḥ sa yatra svapiti tac chrotram prāṇo girati |
3.2.d: श्रोत्रं दिशस् ता महात्मानो देवाः स यत्र स्वपिति तच् छ्रोत्रम् प्राणो गिरति ।
3.2.e: Hearing [is] the quarters; those are magnanimous gods. When one sleeps, then breath swallows up hearing.
3.2.m: The ear is the directions; they are great-souled gods; when one sleeps, breath swallows the ear.

3.2.s: tad yan mahātmanaś caturo deva eka ity etad dha tat |
3.2.d: तद् यन् महात्मनश् चतुरो देव एक इत्य् एतद् ध तत् ।
3.2.e: So, when [it is said]: 'One god four magnanimous ones,' this is what that means.
3.2.m: So when it says, 'Four great-souled ones has the one god [swallowed],' that is this.

3.2.s: kas sa jagāreti prajāpatir vai kaḥ sa haitaj jagāra |
3.2.d: कस् स जगारेति प्रजापतिर् वै कः स हैतज् जगार ।
3.2.e: 'Who (ka) is he who swallowed up:' Ka is Prajapati. He swallowed this up.
3.2.m: 'Who is that who swallowed them?' Ka is Prajāpati; he swallowed them.

3.2.s: bhuvanasya gopā iti sa u vāva bhuvanasya gopāḥ |
3.2.d: भुवनस्य गोपा इति स उ वाव भुवनस्य गोपाः ।
3.2.e: 'A keeper of creation:' he, indeed, is a keeper of creation.
3.2.m: 'The protector of the world'—he indeed is the protector of the world.

3.2.s: taṃ kāpeya na vijānanty eka iti na hy etam eke vijānanti |
3.2.d: तं कापेय न विजानन्त्य् एक इति न ह्य् एतम् एके विजानन्ति ।
3.2.e: 'Him, O Kapeya, some do not know:' for some do not know him.
3.2.m: 'Him, O Kāpeya, some do not recognize'—for some do not recognize him.

3.2.s: abhipratārin bahudhā niviṣṭam iti bahudhā hy evaiṣa niviṣṭo yat prāṇaḥ |
3.2.d: अभिप्रतारिन् बहुधा निविष्टम् इति बहुधा ह्य् एवैष निविष्टो यत् प्राणः ।
3.2.e: ' Him, O Abhiprattirin, settled down in many places:' for this breath has settled down in many places.
3.2.m: 'O Abhipratārin, who is entered into many places'—for he is entered into many places, namely breath.

3.2.s: ātmā devānām uta martyānām iti ātmā hy eṣa devānām uta martyānām |
3.2.d: आत्मा देवानाम् उत मर्त्यानाम् इति आत्मा ह्य् एष देवानाम् उत मर्त्यानाम् ।
3.2.e: 'The self of the gods and of mortals:' for he is the self of the gods and of mortals,
3.2.m: 'The self of the gods and of mortals'—for he is the self of the gods and of mortals.

3.2.s: hiraṇyadanto rapaso na sūnur iti na hy eṣa sūnuḥ sūnurūpo hy eṣa san na sūnuḥ |
3.2.d: हिरण्यदन्तो रपसो न सूनुर् इति न ह्य् एष सूनुः सूनुरूपो ह्य् एष सन् न सूनुः ।
3.2.e: ' With golden teeth, defective, not a son:' for he is not a son; for he, having the form of a son, is not a son.

3.2.s: mahāntam asya mahimānam āhur iti mahāntaṃ hy etasya mahimānam āhuḥ |
3.2.d: महान्तम् अस्य महिमानम् आहुर् इति महान्तं ह्य् एतस्य महिमानम् आहुः ।
3.2.e: 'Great they call his greatness:' for they call his greatness great.
3.2.m:
"Great they call his greatness":
for great indeed they call his greatness.

3.2.s: anadyamāno yad adantam attīti anadyamāno hy eṣo 'dantam atti | prathame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.2.d: अनद्यमानो यद् अदन्तम् अत्तीति अनद्यमानो ह्य् एषो ऽदन्तम् अत्ति । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
3.2.e: 'In that he, not being eaten, eats him who eats:' for he, not being eaten, eats him who eats.
3.2.m:
"Eaten by none, he eats him that eats":
for being eaten by none, he eats him that eats.
[This is] the second khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

3.3.s: tasyaiṣa śrīr ātmā samudrūḍho yad asāv ādityaḥ tasmād gāyatrasya stotre ṇāvānyān nec chriyā avachidyā iti |
3.3.d: तस्यैष श्रीर् आत्मा समुद्रूढो यद् असाव् आदित्यः तस्माद् गायत्रस्य स्तोत्रे णावान्यान् नेच् छ्रिया अवछिद्या इति ।
3.3.e: Of it he is the fortune, the self completely risen (?), viz. yonder sun. Therefore one should not take breath in (during) the stotra of the ydyatra [-sāman'] [saying]: "May I not be cut off from fortune."
3.3.m:
His prosperous self, risen high, is that sun up there.
Therefore, in the chant of the gāyatra, let him not breathe out, thinking: "Lest I be cut off from prosperity."

3.3.s: sa eṣa evoktham yat purastād avāniti tad etad ukthasya śiro yad dakṣiṇatas sa dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣo yad uttaratas sa uttaraḥ pakṣo yat paścāt puccham |
3.3.d: स एष एवोक्थम् यत् पुरस्ताद् अवानिति तद् एतद् उक्थस्य शिरो यद् दक्षिणतस् स दक्षिणः पक्षो यद् उत्तरतस् स उत्तरः पक्षो यत् पश्चात् पुच्छम् ।
3.3.e: That same is the uktha. When one takes breath eastward, that is the head of the uktha/ when southward, that is the right side (wing); when northward, that is the left side (wing); when westward, that is the tail.
3.3.m:
This very one is the uktha.
That which breathes forward in front, that is the head of the uktha; that which is to the right is the right wing; that which is to the left is the left wing; that which is behind is the tail.

3.3.s: ayam eva prāṇa ukthasyātmā sa ya evam etam ukthasyātmānam ātman pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda sa hāmuṣmiṃl loke sāṅgas satanus sambhavati |
3.3.d: अयम् एव प्राण उक्थस्यात्मा स य एवम् एतम् उक्थस्यात्मानम् आत्मन् प्रतिष्ठितं वेद स हामुष्मिंल् लोके साङ्गस् सतनुस् सम्भवति ।
3.3.e: This breath is the self of the uktha. Who thus knows this self of the uktha firmly established in the self, truly he comes into being in yonder world with limbs, with a body, [whole].
3.3.m:
This breath alone is the self of the uktha.
He who knows this self of the uktha thus established in the self, comes into being in yonder world with [all his] limbs, with his body, [complete].

3.3.s: śaśvad dha vā amuṣmiṃl loke yad idam puruṣasyāṇḍau śiśnaṃ karṇau nāsike yat kiṃ cānasthikaṃ na sambhavati |
3.3.d: शश्वद् ध वा अमुष्मिंल् लोके यद् इदम् पुरुषस्याण्डौ शिश्नं कर्णौ नासिके यत् किं चानस्थिकं न सम्भवति ।
3.3.e: Verily, that is certainly in yonder world, viz. a man's two testicles, the penis, the two ears, the two nostrils: whatever does not come into being boneless,
3.3.m: For indeed, constantly in yonder world, what is in this man the testicles, penis, ears, nostrils, and whatever is boneless, does not come into being.

3.3.s: atha ya evam etam ukthasyātmānam ātman pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda sa haivāmuṣmiṃl loke sāṅgas satanus sarvas sambhavati |
3.3.d: अथ य एवम् एतम् उक्थस्यात्मानम् आत्मन् प्रतिष्ठितं वेद स हैवामुष्मिंल् लोके साङ्गस् सतनुस् सर्वस् सम्भवति ।
3.3.e: Now whoso thus knows this self of the uktha firmly established in the self, truly he comes into being in yonder world with limbs, with a body, whole.
3.3.m: Now he who knows this self of the uktha thus established in the self, comes into being in yonder world with [all his] limbs, with his body, complete.

3.3.s: tad etad vaiśvāmitram uktham tad annaṃ vai viśvam prāṇo mitram |
3.3.d: तद् एतद् वैश्वामित्रम् उक्थम् तद् अन्नं वै विश्वम् प्राणो मित्रम् ।
3.3.e: That same is the uktha belonging to Vigvamitra. Verily, food is all (vipva), breath is a friend (mitra).
3.3.m:
This is that Vaiśvāmitra uktha.
Food is indeed all (viśva); breath is friend (mitra).

3.3.s: tad dha viśvāmitraś śrameṇa tapasā vratacaryeṇendrasya priyaṃ dhāmopajagāma |
3.3.d: तद् ध विश्वामित्रश् श्रमेण तपसा व्रतचर्येणेन्द्रस्य प्रियं धामोपजगाम ।
3.3.e: Now Vi9vamitra through exertion, through penance, through the performance of vows, went unto the dear abode of Indra. e. And he proclaimed to him that which has come to men here.
3.3.m: Through weariness, ascetic heat, and observance of vows, Viśvāmitra approached Indra's beloved domain.

3.3.s: tasmā u haitat provāca yad idam manuṣyān āgatam |
3.3.d: तस्मा उ हैतत् प्रोवाच यद् इदम् मनुष्यान् आगतम् ।
3.3.e: Now he went for instruction [to him] [saying]: " Light is this uktha."
3.3.m: To him he proclaimed that which has reached men here.

3.3.s: tad dha sa upaniṣasāda jyotir etad uktham iti |
3.3.d: तद् ध स उपनिषसाद ज्योतिर् एतद् उक्थम् इति ।
3.3.m: He [Viśvāmitra] approached him [saying], "This uktha is light."

3.3.s: jyotir iti dve akṣare prāṇa iti dve annam iti dve tad etad anna eva pratiṣṭhitam |
3.3.d: ज्योतिर् इति द्वे अक्षरे प्राण इति द्वे अन्नम् इति द्वे तद् एतद् अन्न एव प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
3.3.e: ' Light' has two syllables,' breath' has two, ' food' has two. That same is firmly established in food.
3.3.m:
"Light" (jyotis) has two syllables; "breath" (prāṇa) has two; "food" (anna) has two.
Thus it is established in food alone.

3.3.s: atha hainaṃ jamadagnir upaniṣasādāyur etad uktham iti |
3.3.d: अथ हैनं जमदग्निर् उपनिषसादायुर् एतद् उक्थम् इति ।
3.3.e: Then Jamadagni went for instruction to him [saying]: "Life is this uktha."
3.3.m: Then Jamadagni approached him [saying], "This uktha is lifespan (āyus)."

3.3.s: āyur iti dve akṣare prāṇa iti dve annam iti dve tad etad anna eva pratiṣṭhitam |
3.3.d: आयुर् इति द्वे अक्षरे प्राण इति द्वे अन्नम् इति द्वे तद् एतद् अन्न एव प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
3.3.e: ' Life' has two syllables, ' breath' two, ' food ' two. That same is firmly established in food.
3.3.m:
"Lifespan" (āyus) has two syllables; "breath" (prāṇa) has two; "food" (anna) has two.
Thus it is established in food alone.

3.3.s: atha hainaṃ vasiṣṭha upaniṣasāda gaur etad uktham iti tad etad annam eva annaṃ hi gauḥ |
3.3.d: अथ हैनं वसिष्ठ उपनिषसाद गौर् एतद् उक्थम् इति तद् एतद् अन्नम् एव अन्नं हि गौः ।
3.3.e: Then Vasistha went for instruction to him [saying]: " The cow is this uktha." That same is just food. For the cow is food.

3.3.s: tad āhur yad asya prāṇasya puruṣaś śarīram atha kenānye prānāś śarīravanto bhavantīti |
3.3.d: तद् आहुर् यद् अस्य प्राणस्य पुरुषश् शरीरम् अथ केनान्ये प्रानाश् शरीरवन्तो भवन्तीति ।
3.3.e: This they say: " If man be the body of this breath, how then do the other breaths .(senses) come to have bodies?"
3.3.m: They say: "If the man is the body of this breath, then by what do the other breaths possess a body?"

3.3.s: sa brūyād yad vācā vadati tad vācaś śarīraṃ yan manasā dhyāyati tan manasaś śarīraṃ yac cakṣuṣā paśyati tac cakṣuṣaś śarīraṃ yac chrotreṇa śṛṇoti tac chrotrasya śarīram evam u hānye prāṇāś śarīravanto bhavantīti | prathame 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.3.d: स ब्रूयाद् यद् वाचा वदति तद् वाचश् शरीरं यन् मनसा ध्यायति तन् मनसश् शरीरं यच् चक्षुषा पश्यति तच् चक्षुषश् शरीरं यच् छ्रोत्रेण शृणोति तच् छ्रोत्रस्य शरीरम् एवम् उ हान्ये प्राणाश् शरीरवन्तो भवन्तीति । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
3.3.e: Let him say: " What he speaks with speech, that is the body of speech. What he thinks with the mind, that is the body of the mind. What he sees with sight, that is the body of sight. What he hears with hearing, that is the body of hearing. Thus the other breaths (senses) also come to have bodies."
3.3.m:
He should say: "What one speaks with speech, that is the body of speech; what one meditates with mind, that is the body of mind; what one sees with the eye, that is the body of the eye; what one hears with the ear, that is the body of the ear.
Thus indeed do the other breaths possess a body."
[This is] the third khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

3.4.s: tad etad ukthaṃ saptavidham śasyate stotriyo 'nurūpo dhāyyā pragāthas sūktaṃ nivit paridhānīyā |
3.4.d: तद् एतद् उक्थं सप्तविधम् शस्यते स्तोत्रियो ऽनुरूपो धाय्या प्रगाथस् सूक्तं निवित् परिधानीया ।
3.4.e: That same uktha is sevenfold. Chanted is the stotriya (strophe), the anurupa (antistrophe), the dhdyyd (kindling verse), the pragdtha (tristich), the sukta (hymn), the 7iivid (notification), [and] the paridhdnlyd (closing verse).
3.4.m:
Now this uktha is sevenfold:
there are recited the stotriya, the anurūpa, the dhāyyā, the pragātha, the sūkta, the nivid, and the paridhānīyā.

3.4.s: iyam eva stotriyo 'gnir anurūpo vāyur dhāyyāntarikṣam pragātho dyaus sūktam ādityo nivit tasmād bahvṛcā udite nividam adhīyante ādityo hi nivit diśaḥ paridhānīyety adhidevatam |
3.4.d: इयम् एव स्तोत्रियो ऽग्निर् अनुरूपो वायुर् धाय्यान्तरिक्षम् प्रगाथो द्यौस् सूक्तम् आदित्यो निवित् तस्माद् बह्वृचा उदिते निविदम् अधीयन्ते आदित्यो हि निवित् दिशः परिधानीयेत्य् अधिदेवतम् ।
3.4.e: This [earth] is the stotriya; Agni the anurupa; VSyu the dhdyyd; the atmosphere the pragdtha; the sky the sukta; the sun the nivid— therefore the Rig-veda scholars study the nivid when [the sun] has risen; for the sun is the tiivid—the quarters the paridhdnlyd. Thus with regard to the divinities.
3.4.m:
This [earth] is the stotriya; Agni is the anurūpa; Vāyu is the dhāyyā; the intermediate space is the pragātha; heaven is the sūkta; the sun is the nivid—
therefore the Ṛgvedins recite the nivid when [the sun] has risen;
for the sun is the nivid—
the directions are the paridhānīyā. Thus pertaining to the deities.

3.4.s: athādhyātmam ātmaiva stotriyaḥ prajānurūpaḥ prāṇo dhāyyā manaḥ pragāthaś śiras sūktaṃ cakṣur nivic chrotram paridhānīyā |
3.4.d: अथाध्यात्मम् आत्मैव स्तोत्रियः प्रजानुरूपः प्राणो धाय्या मनः प्रगाथश् शिरस् सूक्तं चक्षुर् निविच् छ्रोत्रम् परिधानीया ।
3.4.e: Now with regard to the self. The self itself is the stotriya; offspring the anurupa; breath the dhdyyd; mind the pragdtha; the head the sukta; sight the/n'yeV^,- heaving the paridhdniyd.
3.4.m:
Now pertaining to the self:
The self alone is the stotriya; offspring is the anurūpa; breath is the dhāyyā; mind is the pragātha; the head is the sūkta; the eye is the nivid; the ear is the paridhānīyā.

3.4.s: tad dhaitad eke triṣṭubhā paridadhaty anuṣṭubhaike triṣṭubhā tv eva paridadhyāt |
3.4.d: तद् धैतद् एके त्रिष्टुभा परिदधत्य् अनुष्टुभैके त्रिष्टुभा त्व् एव परिदध्यात् ।
3.4.e: Now some recite its paridhdnlyd with a tristubh, others with an anustubh. But let him recite the paridhdnlyd with a tristubh.
3.4.m:
Some conclude it with a triṣṭubh, some with an anuṣṭubh.
One should indeed conclude it with a triṣṭubh.

3.4.s: tad dhaitad eka etā vyāhṛtīr abhivyāhṛtya śaṃsanti mahān mahyā samadhatta devo devyā samadhatta brahma brāhmaṇyā samadhatta tad yat samadhatta samadhatteti |
3.4.d: तद् धैतद् एक एता व्याहृतीर् अभिव्याहृत्य शंसन्ति महान् मह्या समधत्त देवो देव्या समधत्त ब्रह्म ब्राह्मण्या समधत्त तद् यत् समधत्त समधत्तेति ।
3.4.e: That same some chant having uttered these sacred utterances: " He, the great one, united with her, the great one; the god united with the goddess; the brahman united with the brdhmanl. In that he united, he united."
3.4.m:
Some recite [the uktha] after uttering these mystic utterances: "The great joined with the great [female]; the god joined with the goddess; the brahman joined with the brāhmaṇī."
Because [they say], "He joined, he joined."

3.4.s: tasmād idānīm puruṣasya śarīrāṇi pratisaṃhitāni puruṣo hy etad uktham |
3.4.d: तस्माद् इदानीम् पुरुषस्य शरीराणि प्रतिसंहितानि पुरुषो ह्य् एतद् उक्थम् ।
3.4.e: Therefore the bodies of men are now united respectively. For man is this uktha.
3.4.m:
Therefore now the bodies of a man are joined together;
for the man is this uktha.

3.4.s: mahān mahyā samadhatteti agnir vai mahān iyam eva mahī |
3.4.d: महान् मह्या समधत्तेति अग्निर् वै महान् इयम् एव मही ।
3.4.e: ' He, the great one, united with her, the great one.' Verily Agni is he, the great one, this [earth] is she, the great one.
3.4.m:
"The great joined with the great [female]":
Agni is the great; this [earth] is the great [female].

3.4.s: devo devyā samadhatteti vāyur vai devo 'ntarikṣaṃ devī |
3.4.d: देवो देव्या समधत्तेति वायुर् वै देवो ऽन्तरिक्षं देवी ।
3.4.e: 'The god united with the goddess.' Verily Vayu is the god, the atmosphere is the goddess.
3.4.m:
"The god joined with the goddess":
Vāyu is the god; the intermediate space is the goddess.

3.4.s: brahma brāhmaṇyā samadhatteti ādityo vai brahma dyaur brāhmaṇī |
3.4.d: ब्रह्म ब्राह्मण्या समधत्तेति आदित्यो वै ब्रह्म द्यौर् ब्राह्मणी ।
3.4.e: ' The brahman united with the brdhmanV Verily the sun is the brahman, the sky is the brdhmanl.
3.4.m:
"The brahman joined with the brāhmaṇī":
the sun is the brahman; heaven is the brāhmaṇī.

3.4.s: tāsāṃ vā etāsāṃ devatānāṃ dvayor-dvayor devatayor nava-navākṣarāṇi sampadyante etad ime lokās triṇavā bhavanti |
3.4.d: तासां वा एतासां देवतानां द्वयोर्-द्वयोर् देवतयोर् नव-नवाक्षराणि सम्पद्यन्ते एतद् इमे लोकास् त्रिणवा भवन्ति ।
3.4.e: Of these divinities each two divinities make up nine syllables respectively. Thus these worlds come to be thrice nine.
3.4.m:
Of these deities, two deities together make nine syllables;
thus these worlds are ninefold-thrice (triṇava).

3.4.s: tad brahma vai trivṛt tad brahmābhivyāhṛtya śaṃsanti eṣa u eva stomas so 'nucaraḥ |
3.4.d: तद् ब्रह्म वै त्रिवृत् तद् ब्रह्माभिव्याहृत्य शंसन्ति एष उ एव स्तोमस् सो ऽनुचरः ।
3.4.e: Verily that brahman is threefold. Having uttered the sacred utterances they chant unto this brahman. And this is also the stoma, this the anucura (sequel).
3.4.m:
The brahman is threefold (trivṛt).
Having uttered that brahman, they recite.
This very stoma is that follower.

3.4.s: yad imam āhur ekastoma ity ayam eva yo 'yam pavate eṣo 'dhidevatam prāṇo 'dhyātmam tasya śarīram anucaraḥ |
3.4.d: यद् इमम् आहुर् एकस्तोम इत्य् अयम् एव यो ऽयम् पवते एषो ऽधिदेवतम् प्राणो ऽध्यात्मम् तस्य शरीरम् अनुचरः ।
3.4.e: When they call him 'possessing one stomal that is he who cleanses here. That [he is] with regard to the divinities; breath [he is] with regard to the self. The anucara is its body.
3.4.m:
What they call this one single-stoma (ekastoma) is this one who purifies here [the wind].
This is pertaining to the deities.
Breath is pertaining to the self.
His body is the follower.

3.4.s: tad yathā ha vai maṇau maṇisūtraṃ samprotaṃ syād | prathame 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.4.d: तद् यथा ह वै मणौ मणिसूत्रं सम्प्रोतं स्याद् । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
3.4.e: As the thread of a jewel would be twined in with the jewel,—
3.4.m:
Just as a thread would be strung through a jewel—
[This is] the fourth khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

3.5.s: evaṃ haitasmin sarvam idaṃ samprotaṃ gandharvāpsarasaḥ paśavo manuṣyāḥ |
3.5.d: एवं हैतस्मिन् सर्वम् इदं सम्प्रोतं गन्धर्वाप्सरसः पशवो मनुष्याः ।
3.5.e: — Even so this all is twined in with it, viz. Gandharvas, Apsarases, domestic animals, [and] men.
3.5.m: —so upon this all this is strung: the gandharvas and apsarases, animals, and men.

3.5.s: tad dha muñjas sāmaśravasaḥ prayayau tasmai ha śvājanir vaiśyaḥ preyāya |
3.5.d: तद् ध मुञ्जस् सामश्रवसः प्रययौ तस्मै ह श्वाजनिर् वैश्यः प्रेयाय ।
3.5.e: Now Munja Srima5ravasa went forth, Śviijani, a Vaigya, went before him.
3.5.m:
Now Muñja Sāmaśravasa set out on a journey.
Towards him Śvājani, a vaiśya, came forward.

3.5.s: tasya hāntarikṣāt patitvā navanītapiṇḍa urasi nipapāta taṃ hādāyānudadhau |
3.5.d: तस्य हान्तरिक्षात् पतित्वा नवनीतपिण्ड उरसि निपपात तं हादायानुदधौ ।
3.5.e: Falling from the atmosphere, a lump of fresh butter fell down on his breast. He, taking it, put it in addition [in the fire (?)].
3.5.m:
Having fallen from the intermediate space, a lump of butter dropped upon his chest.
Taking it, he ran after [Muñja].

3.5.s: tato haiva stomaṃ dadarśāntarikṣe vitatam bahu śobhamānam tasyo ha yuktiṃ dadarśa |
3.5.d: ततो हैव स्तोमं ददर्शान्तरिक्षे विततम् बहु शोभमानम् तस्यो ह युक्तिं ददर्श ।
3.5.e: Thereupon he saw the stoma spi-ead out in the atmosphere, greatly shining; he also saw its application (?).
3.5.m:
Then indeed he saw the stoma stretched out in the intermediate space, shining greatly;
and he saw its application.

3.5.s: bahiṣpavamānam āsadya ṭītra viyi prāṇya iti kūryāt ṭītra gṛhitra apānya iti vācā didṛkṣetaivākṣibhyaṃ śuśrūṣetaiva karṇābhyām svayam idam manoyuktam |
3.5.d: बहिष्पवमानम् आसद्य टीत्र वियि प्राण्य इति कूर्यात् टीत्र गृहित्र अपान्य इति वाचा दिदृक्षेतैवाक्षिभ्यं शुश्रूषेतैव कर्णाभ्याम् स्वयम् इदम् मनोयुक्तम् ।
3.5.e: Having set himself about the bahispavamdna, he should say fitra viyi prdnya; tUra grhitra apdnya, with speech. He should wish to see with the eyes, he should wish_ to hear with the ears. This is of itself yoked to mind. Now when an arrow is too pointed, verily it then does not hurt. Verily thus he would not attain it. Let him breathe out [saying] simply j>a. As one would attract a deer by means of a mirror, even thus he attracts it (?) by means of this divinity. He (?) performs yoked, and he is yoked also.

3.5.s: tad yatra vā iṣur atyagro bhavati na vai sa tato hinasti tad u vā etaṃ nopāpnuyāt pa ity evāpānyāt tad yathā bimbena mṛgam ānayed evam evainam etayā devatayānayati sa yuktaḥ karoti eṣa evāpi yuktaḥ | prathame 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | prathamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
3.5.d: तद् यत्र वा इषुर् अत्यग्रो भवति न वै स ततो हिनस्ति तद् उ वा एतं नोपाप्नुयात् प इत्य् एवापान्यात् तद् यथा बिम्बेन मृगम् आनयेद् एवम् एवैनम् एतया देवतयानयति स युक्तः करोति एष एवापि युक्तः । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः । प्रथमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
3.5.m:
Where an arrow is overly sharp, it does not harm from there, nor would it reach this [target].
He should breathe out just with "pa".
Just as one would lead a deer with a reflection/decoy, even so one leads him with this deity.
He acts when yoked;
and this one also is yoked.
[This is] the fifth khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.
The first anuvāka is completed.

3.6.s: yo 'sau sāmnaḥ prattiṃ veda pra hāsmai dīyate |
3.6.d: यो ऽसौ साम्नः प्रत्तिं वेद प्र हास्मै दीयते ।
3.6.e: That one yonder who knows the delivery of the sāman, verily unto him it is delivered,
3.6.m: Whoever knows that gift-giving (pratti) of the sāman, to him [wealth] is given forth.

3.6.s: dadā iti ha vā ayam agnir dīpyate tatheti vāyuḥ pavate hanteti candramā om ity ādityaḥ |
3.6.d: ददा इति ह वा अयम् अग्निर् दीप्यते तथेति वायुः पवते हन्तेति चन्द्रमा ओम् इत्य् आदित्यः ।
3.6.e: [Uttering] dadd, this fire here shines; [uttering] tathd, the wind cleanses (blows); hanta the moon [utters], om the sun.
3.6.m: "Give!" (dadā) this Agni blazes forth; "So be it!" (tathā) Vāyu blows; "Come!" (hanta) the Moon; "Om!" the sun.

3.6.s: eṣā ha vai sāmnaḥ prattiḥ etāṃ ha vai sāmnaḥ prattiṃ sudakṣiṇaḥ kṣaimir vidāṃ cakāra |
3.6.d: एषा ह वै साम्नः प्रत्तिः एतां ह वै साम्नः प्रत्तिं सुदक्षिणः क्षैमिर् विदां चकार ।
3.6.e: Verily this is the delivery of the sāman. Verily this delivery of the sāman Sudaksiua Ksfiimi knew.
3.6.m:
This indeed is the gift-giving of the sāman.
Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi knew this gift-giving of the sāman.

3.6.s: tāṃ haitāṃ hotur vājye gāyen maitrāvaruṇasya vā tāṃ dadā3 tathā3 hantā3 him bhā ovā iti pra ha vā asmai dīyate |
3.6.d: तां हैतां होतुर् वाज्ये गायेन् मैत्रावरुणस्य वा तां ददा3 तथा3 हन्ता3 हिम् भा ओवा इति प्र ह वा अस्मै दीयते ।
3.6.e: One should sing that same in the «/»/«-chant hanta, him bhd ovd. Verily it is delivered unto him.
3.6.m:
One should sing that in the hotṛ's or the maitrāvaruṇa's vājya [śastra], [chanting] it: "dadā3 tathā3 hantā3 him bhā ovā".
To him indeed [wealth] is given forth.

3.6.s: 'py anyān bahūn uparyupari ya evam etāṃ sāmnaḥ prattiṃ veda |
3.6.d: ऽप्य् अन्यान् बहून् उपर्युपरि य एवम् एतां साम्नः प्रत्तिं वेद ।
3.6.e: He is much superior to even many others who thus knows this delivery of the sāman.
3.6.m: He [surpasses] even many others, higher and higher—he who thus knows this gift-giving of the sāman.

3.6.s: ya u ha vā abandhur bandhumat sāma veda yatra hāpy enaṃ na vidur yatra roṣanti yatra parīva cakṣate tad dhāpi śraiṣṭhyam ādhipatyam annādyam purodhām paryeti |
3.6.d: य उ ह वा अबन्धुर् बन्धुमत् साम वेद यत्र हाप्य् एनं न विदुर् यत्र रोषन्ति यत्र परीव चक्षते तद् धापि श्रैष्ठ्यम् आधिपत्यम् अन्नाद्यम् पुरोधाम् पर्येति ।
3.6.e: And whoso being without relatives knows the sdmany:\cS\ in relatives, even where they do not know him, where they are angry at him, where they overlook liim, as it were, he thus compasses excellence, supremacy, food-eating, [and] the office of &purohita.
3.6.m: And he who knows the sāman having relatives though having no relative—even where they do not know him, where they are angry with him, where they speak ill of him—even there he attains pre-eminence, overlordship, abundance of food, and priesthood.

3.6.s: agnir ha vā abandhur bandhumat sāma kasmād vā hy enaṃ dārvoḥ kasmād vā paryāvṛtya manthanti sa śraiṣṭhyāyādhipatyāyānnādyāya purodhāyai jāyate |
3.6.d: अग्निर् ह वा अबन्धुर् बन्धुमत् साम कस्माद् वा ह्य् एनं दार्वोः कस्माद् वा पर्यावृत्य मन्थन्ति स श्रैष्ठ्यायाधिपत्यायान्नाद्याय पुरोधायै जायते ।
3.6.e: Verily Agni, being without relatives, is the sāman rich in relatives. For in whatever way they churn him, from the wood, or by turning, he is born for excellence, for supremacy, for food-eating, [and] for the office of a purohita.
3.6.m:
Agni indeed is the sāman having relatives though having no relative.
For why, turning it round and round, do they churn him from two pieces of wood? He is born for pre-eminence, overlordship, abundance of food, and priesthood.

3.6.s: sa yatra ha vā apy evaṃvidaṃ na vidur yatra roṣanti yatra parīva cakṣate tad dhāpi śraiṣṭhyam ādhipatyam annādyam purodhām paryeti | dvitīye 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.6.d: स यत्र ह वा अप्य् एवंविदं न विदुर् यत्र रोषन्ति यत्र परीव चक्षते तद् धापि श्रैष्ठ्यम् आधिपत्यम् अन्नाद्यम् पुरोधाम् पर्येति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
3.6.e: Verily even where they do not know one knowing thus, where they are angry at him, where they so to speak overlook him, he thus compasses excellence, supremacy, food-eating, [and] the office of & purohita.
3.6.m:
And when they do not recognise such a knower, when they are angry, when they censure him, even then he attains pre-eminence, lordship, eating of food, and the office of domestic priest.
First khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.

3.7.e: And [that happens] of itself where they know him.
3.7.m: Naturally so where they do recognise him.

3.7.s: sudakṣiṇo ha vai kṣaimiḥ prācīnaśālir jābālau te ha sabrahmacāriṇa āsuḥ |
3.7.d: सुदक्षिणो ह वै क्षैमिः प्राचीनशालिर् जाबालौ ते ह सब्रह्मचारिण आसुः ।
3.7.e: Sudaksina Ksaimi, Pracinagali, the two Jabalas—they were fellow-students.
3.7.m: Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi, Prācīnaśāli, and the two Jābālas were fellow-students of sacred knowledge.

3.7.s: te heme bahu japyasya cānyasya cānūcire prācīnaśāliś ca jābālau ca |
3.7.d: ते हेमे बहु जप्यस्य चान्यस्य चानूचिरे प्राचीनशालिश् च जाबालौ च ।
3.7.e: These, viz. Pracinagali and the two Jabalas, recited much of what is to be muttered and of other [prayers].
3.7.m: Now these—Prācīnaśāli and the two Jābālas—had studied much of what is to be muttered and of other things.

3.7.s: atha ha sma sudakṣiṇaḥ kṣaimir yad eva yajñasyāñjo yat suviditaṃ tad dha smaiva pṛcchati |
3.7.d: अथ ह स्म सुदक्षिणः क्षैमिर् यद् एव यज्ञस्याञ्जो यत् सुविदितं तद् ध स्मैव पृच्छति ।
3.7.e: Then Sudaksina Ksaimi used to ask [them] concerning that which is easy of the sacrifice, concerning that which is well known,
3.7.m: Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi, on the other hand, used to inquire only into what was the direct path of the sacrifice, what was well understood.

3.7.s: ta u ha vā apoditā vyākrośamānāś ceruś śūdro duranūcāna iti ha sma sudakṣiṇaṃ kṣaimim ākrośanti prācīnaśāliś ca jābālau ca |
3.7.d: त उ ह वा अपोदिता व्याक्रोशमानाश् चेरुश् शूद्रो दुरनूचान इति ह स्म सुदक्षिणं क्षैमिम् आक्रोशन्ति प्राचीनशालिश् च जाबालौ च ।
3.7.e: And they, being distracted, kept crying out: " Śudra, ignoramus!" Thus they, viz. Priiclnagali and the two Jabalas, used to cry out against Sudaksina Ksaimi.
3.7.m: Being slighted, they went about reviling him. "A Śūdra, an incompetent scholar!" Prācīnaśāli and the two Jābālas thus kept reviling Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi.

3.7.s: sa ha smāha sudakṣiṇaḥ kṣaimir yatra bhūyiṣṭhāḥ kurupañcālās samāgatā bhavitāras tan na eṣa saṃvādo nānupadṛṣṭe śūdrā iva saṃvadiṣyāmaha iti |
3.7.d: स ह स्माह सुदक्षिणः क्षैमिर् यत्र भूयिष्ठाः कुरुपञ्चालास् समागता भवितारस् तन् न एष संवादो नानुपदृष्टे शूद्रा इव संवदिष्यामह इति ।
3.7.e: Then Sudaksina Ksaimi used to say: "Where most of the Kurupaiiealas shall be assembled together, there shall be this disputation of ours; we will not dispute without witnesses, like Śtiiiras."
3.7.m: Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi said: "Where the most Kuru-Pañcālas are assembled, there our debate shall take place. We will not debate like Śūdras out of sight."

3.7.s: tā u ha vai jābālau didīkṣāte śukraś ca gośruś ca tayor ha prācīnaśālir vṛta udgātā |
3.7.d: ता उ ह वै जाबालौ दिदीक्षाते शुक्रश् च गोश्रुश् च तयोर् ह प्राचीनशालिर् वृत उद्गाता ।
3.7.e: Now the two Jabalas, Śukra and Gogru, consecrated themselves. Of them Pracinagali [was] chosen udgdtar.
3.7.m:
Then the two Jābālas, Śukra and Gośru, underwent consecration [for a sacrifice].
Prācīnaśāli was chosen as their udgātṛ.

3.7.s: sa tad dha sudakṣiṇo 'nububudhe jābālau hādīkṣiṣātām iti sa ha saṃgrahītāram uvācānayasvāre jābālau hādīkṣiṣātāṃ tad gamiṣyāva iti | dvitīye 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.7.d: स तद् ध सुदक्षिणो ऽनुबुबुधे जाबालौ हादीक्षिषाताम् इति स ह संग्रहीतारम् उवाचानयस्वारे जाबालौ हादीक्षिषातां तद् गमिष्याव इति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
3.7.e: Then Sudaksina became aware: " The two Jabalas have consecrated themselves." He said to his driver: '' Sirrah, conduct [me thither]. The two Jabalas have consecrated themselves. Thither we will go."
3.7.m:
Sudakṣiṇa perceived this: "The two Jābālas have undergone consecration."
He said to his charioteer: "Bring [the chariot] near, friend; the two Jābālas have undergone consecration; thither we two will go."
Second khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.

3.8.s: tasya ha jñātikā aśrumukhā ivāsur anyatarāṃ vā ayam upāgād iti |
3.8.d: तस्य ह ज्ञातिका अश्रुमुखा इवासुर् अन्यतरां वा अयम् उपागाद् इति ।
3.8.e: Now his relatives were tear-faced, as it were [saying]: " This one hath gone unto one or the other."
3.8.m: His kinsmen were as if tearful, thinking: "He has undertaken one or the other [perilous contest]."

3.8.s: atha ha sma vai yaḥ purā brahmavādyaṃ vadaty anyatarām upāgād iti ha smainam manyante atho ha smainam mṛtam ivaivopāsate |
3.8.d: अथ ह स्म वै यः पुरा ब्रह्मवाद्यं वदत्य् अन्यतराम् उपागाद् इति ह स्मैनम् मन्यन्ते अथो ह स्मैनम् मृतम् इवैवोपासते ।
3.8.e: Now whenever one formerly engaged in a theological disputation, they used to think of him: " He hath gone unto one or the other;" and they used to wait on him as on one dead.
3.8.m:
For in ancient times, when anyone engaged in a theological disputation, they thought: "He has undertaken one or the other [survival or destruction]."
And they treated him as if he were already dead.

3.8.s: taṃ ha saṃgrahītovācātha yad bhagavas te tābhyāṃ na kuśalaṃ kathettham āttheti |
3.8.d: तं ह संग्रहीतोवाचाथ यद् भगवस् ते ताभ्यां न कुशलं कथेत्थम् आत्थेति ।
3.8.e: The driver said to him: " Since, sir, thou art not on good terms with these two, why dost thou speak thus?"
3.8.m: The charioteer said to him: "Sir, since you are not on good terms with them, why do you speak thus?"

3.8.s: om iti hovāca gantavyam ma ācāryas suyamān amanyateti |
3.8.d: ओम् इति होवाच गन्तव्यम् म आचार्यस् सुयमान् अमन्यतेति ।
3.8.e: "Yes," he said, "I must go; the teacher thought [them] easily governed."
3.8.m: "Om," he said, "I must go; my teacher considered me easy to guide."

3.8.s: sa ha ratham āsthāya pradhāvayāṃ cakāra taṃ ha sma pratīkṣante |
3.8.d: स ह रथम् आस्थाय प्रधावयां चकार तं ह स्म प्रतीक्षन्ते ।
3.8.e: He, mounting the chariot, drove off. They catch sight of him.
3.8.m:
Mounting the chariot, he drove forward.
They looked toward him:

3.8.s: kaṃ jānīteti sudakṣiṇa iti na vai nūnaṃ sa idam abhyaveyād iti sa eveti |
3.8.d: कं जानीतेति सुदक्षिण इति न वै नूनं स इदम् अभ्यवेयाद् इति स एवेति ।
3.8.e: "Do you know who this is?" "Sudaksina." " May he not come down hither now." " [It is] just he."
3.8.m:
"Whom do you recognise?"
"Sudakṣiṇa."
"Surely he would not come down here!"
"It is he indeed."

3.8.s: sa ha sopānād evāntarvedy avasthāyovācāṅga nv itthaṃ gṛhapatā3 iti taṃ ha nānūdatiṣṭhāsat sa hovācānūtthātā ma edhi kṛṣṇājino 'sīti tad ime kurupañcālā avidur anūtthātaiva ta iti hocuḥ |
3.8.d: स ह सोपानाद् एवान्तर्वेद्य् अवस्थायोवाचाङ्ग न्व् इत्थं गृहपता3 इति तं ह नानूदतिष्ठासत् स होवाचानूत्थाता म एधि कृष्णाजिनो ऽसीति तद् इमे कुरुपञ्चाला अविदुर् अनूत्थातैव त इति होचुः ।
3.8.e: He, descending from the steps within the sacred enclosure, said: " Verily now is it thus, O householder?" He did not wish to attend upon him. He said: "Be thou attending upon me; thou art [dressed] in the skin of a black antelope." These Kurupancalas knew this. "He is thy attendant," they said.
3.8.m:
Remaining in his shoes, he stood inside the sacrificial altar ground and said: "Well now, householder!"
He would not stand up for him.
He said: "Rise up for me! You are wearing a black antelope skin."
These Kuru-Pañcālas realised that, and said: "Rise up indeed for him!"

3.8.s: taṃ ha kanīyān bhrātovācānūttiṣṭha bhagava udgātāram iti taṃ hānūttasthau |
3.8.d: तं ह कनीयान् भ्रातोवाचानूत्तिष्ठ भगव उद्गातारम् इति तं हानूत्तस्थौ ।
3.8.e: His younger brother said to him: " Sir, attend upon the udgdtar." He attended upon him.
3.8.m:
The younger brother said to him: "Sir, rise up for the udgātṛ."
He rose up for him.

3.8.s: sa hovāca trir vai gṛhapate puruṣo jāyate pitur evāgre 'dhi jāyate 'tha mātur atha yajñāt |
3.8.d: स होवाच त्रिर् वै गृहपते पुरुषो जायते पितुर् एवाग्रे ऽधि जायते ऽथ मातुर् अथ यज्ञात् ।
3.8.e: He said: " Verily thrice, O householder, man is born. From his father he is born first, then from his mother, then from the sacrifice.
3.8.m:
He said: "A person, O householder, is born three times.
First he is born from the father, then from the mother, then from the sacrifice.

3.8.s: trir v eva mriyata iti sa yad dha vā enam etat pitā yonyāṃ reto bhūtaṃ siñcati | dvitīye 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.8.d: त्रिर् व् एव म्रियत इति स यद् ध वा एनम् एतत् पिता योन्यां रेतो भूतं सिञ्चति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
3.8.e: And thrice he likewise dieth. When his father emitteth him as seed thus into the womb,—
3.8.m:
And three times indeed he dies.
When the father pours him into the womb as semen—
Third khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.

3.9.e: 2. andham iva viii "— Then he dies for the first time.
3.9.m: —then he dies for the first time.

3.9.s: andham iva vai tamo yoniḥ lohitastoko vā vai sa tad ābhavaty apāṃ vā stokaḥ kiṃ hi sa tad ābhavati |
3.9.d: अन्धम् इव वै तमो योनिः लोहितस्तोको वा वै स तद् आभवत्य् अपां वा स्तोकः किं हि स तद् आभवति ।
3.9.e: Blind darkness, as it were, is the womb. He thus becomes either a drop of blood or a di'op of water. What, pray, does he thus become?
3.9.m:
Blind darkness, indeed, is the womb.
A drop of blood or a drop of water he becomes then.
For what does he become then?

3.9.s: sa yas tāṃ devatāṃ veda yāṃ ca sa tato 'nusambhavati yā cainaṃ tam mṛtyum ativahati sa udgātā mṛtyum ativahatīti |
3.9.d: स यस् तां देवतां वेद यां च स ततो ऽनुसम्भवति या चैनं तम् मृत्युम् अतिवहति स उद्गाता मृत्युम् अतिवहतीति ।
3.9.e: He who knows that divinity after which he thence comes into being and which carries him beyond this death—he as udgdtar carries beyond death.
3.9.m: He who knows that deity from whom he is born thereafter, and who carries him across that death, that udgātṛ carries [the sacrificer] across death."

3.9.s: atha ya enam etad dīkṣayanti tad dvitīyam mriyate vapanti keśaśmaśrūṇi nikṛntanti nakhān pratyañjanty aṅgāni pratyacaty aṅgulīḥ apavṛto 'paveṣṭita āste na juhoti na yajate na yoṣitaṃ carati amānuṣīṃ vācaṃ vadati mṛtasya vāvaiṣa tadā rūpam bhavati |
3.9.d: अथ य एनम् एतद् दीक्षयन्ति तद् द्वितीयम् म्रियते वपन्ति केशश्मश्रूणि निकृन्तन्ति नखान् प्रत्यञ्जन्त्य् अङ्गानि प्रत्यचत्य् अङ्गुलीः अपवृतो ऽपवेष्टित आस्ते न जुहोति न यजते न योषितं चरति अमानुषीं वाचं वदति मृतस्य वावैष तदा रूपम् भवति ।
3.9.e: And when they thus consecrate him, then he dies for the second time. They cut [his] hair and [his] beard. They trim [his] nails. They anoint his several limbs. He bends his fingers. He sits uncovered, stripped oft (?). He does not offer oblations, he does not sacrifice, he does not approach a woman, he speaks non-human speech. Verily he then has the form of one dead. 6. = a.

3.9.s: sa yas tāṃ devatāṃ veda yāṃ ca sa tato 'nusambhavati yā cainaṃ tam mṛtyum ativahati sa udgātā mṛtyum ativahatīti |
3.9.d: स यस् तां देवतां वेद यां च स ततो ऽनुसम्भवति या चैनं तम् मृत्युम् अतिवहति स उद्गाता मृत्युम् अतिवहतीति ।
3.9.m: He who knows that deity from whom he is born thereafter, and who carries him across that death, that udgātṛ carries [the sacrificer] across death."

3.9.s: atha ya enam etad asmāl lokāt pretaṃ cityām ādadhati tad tṛtīyam mriyate |
3.9.d: अथ य एनम् एतद् अस्माल् लोकात् प्रेतं चित्याम् आदधति तद् तृतीयम् म्रियते ।
3.9.e: And when they lay him, having departed from this world, upon the funeral-pyre, then he dies for the third time. i. = s."
3.9.m: "Then, when they place him, departed from this world, upon the funeral pyre, then he dies for the third time.

3.9.s: sa yas tāṃ devatāṃ veda yāṃ ca sa tato 'nusambhavati yā cainaṃ tam mṛtyum ativahati sa udgātā mṛtyum ativahatīti |
3.9.d: स यस् तां देवतां वेद यां च स ततो ऽनुसम्भवति या चैनं तम् मृत्युम् अतिवहति स उद्गाता मृत्युम् अतिवहतीति ।
3.9.m: He who knows that deity from whom he is born thereafter, and who carries him across that death, that udgātṛ carries [the sacrificer] across death."

3.9.s: etāvad dhaivoktvā ratham āsthāya pradhāvayāṃ cakāra |
3.9.d: एतावद् धैवोक्त्वा रथम् आस्थाय प्रधावयां चकार ।
3.9.e: Having said this much, mounting the chariot, he drove off.
3.9.m: Having said only this much, mounting the chariot, he drove forward.

3.9.s: taṃ ha jābālam pratyetaṃ kanīyān bhrātovāca kām bhavañ chūdrako vācam avādīti hastinā gādham aiṣīr iti |
3.9.d: तं ह जाबालम् प्रत्येतं कनीयान् भ्रातोवाच काम् भवञ् छूद्रको वाचम् अवादीति हस्तिना गाधम् ऐषीर् इति ।
3.9.e: To this Jabala, having come back, [his] younger brother said: " Sir, what words hath the Śudra spoken? Thou hast sought a shallow with an elephant." He (the older Jabala) set that forth to him who [had said]: " How hath he spoken, sir?": " He who knows the carrying-over of the three deaths by means of the sāman, he as udgdtar carries beyond death."
3.9.m:
When Jābāla returned, the younger brother said to him: "Sir, what words did the little Śūdra speak?"
"You sought a ford by means of an elephant."

3.9.s: pra haivainaṃ tac chaśaṃsa yaḥ katham avocad bhagava iti yas trayāṇām mṛtyūnāṃ sāmnātivāhaṃ veda sa udgātā mṛtyum ativahatīti | dvitīye 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.9.d: प्र हैवैनं तच् छशंस यः कथम् अवोचद् भगव इति यस् त्रयाणाम् मृत्यूनां साम्नातिवाहं वेद स उद्गाता मृत्युम् अतिवहतीति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
3.9.m:
He openly praised him for it: "How did he speak, sir?"
"'He who knows the carrying across the three deaths by means of the sāman, that udgātṛ carries [the sacrificer] across death.'"
Fourth khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.

3.10.s: taṃ vāva bhagavas te pitodgātāram amanyateti hovāca tad u ha prācīnaśālā vidur ya eṣām ayaṃ vṛta udgātāsa tasmin ha nānuviduḥ |
3.10.d: तं वाव भगवस् ते पितोद्गातारम् अमन्यतेति होवाच तद् उ ह प्राचीनशाला विदुर् य एषाम् अयं वृत उद्गातास तस्मिन् ह नानुविदुः ।
3.10.e: He said: " Sir, verily, thy father thought him an udgdtar; and the Pracina9alas know it, who of them was the chosen udgdtar here." To him they did not assent (?).

3.10.s: te hocur anudhāvata kāṇḍviyam iti taṃ hānusasruḥ te ha kāṇḍviyam udgātāraṃ cakrire brahmāṇam prācīnaśālim |
3.10.d: ते होचुर् अनुधावत काण्ड्वियम् इति तं हानुसस्रुः ते ह काण्ड्वियम् उद्गातारं चक्रिरे ब्रह्माणम् प्राचीनशालिम् ।
3.10.e: They said: "Run after Kandviya." They ran after him. They made Kandviya the udgdtar, [and] Praoina5ali the 5raAwian-priest.
3.10.m:
They said: "Run after Kāṇḍviya!"
They ran after him.
They made Kāṇḍviya the udgātṛ, and Prācīnaśāli the brahman priest.

3.10.s: taṃ hābhyavekṣyovācaivam eṣa brāhmaṇo moghāya vādāya nāglāyat sa nāṇu sāmno 'nvicchatīti ati haivainaṃ tac cakre |
3.10.d: तं हाभ्यवेक्ष्योवाचैवम् एष ब्राह्मणो मोघाय वादाय नाग्लायत् स नाणु साम्नो ऽन्विच्छतीति अति हैवैनं तच् चक्रे ।
3.10.e: He looking down at him said: " Thus this Brahman was not averse to idle talk. He doth not strive after the subtle of the sāman." He did this beyond him (?).
3.10.m:
Looking down upon him, he said: "Thus this brāhmaṇa did not tire of idle talk.
He does not seek the fine [truth] of the sāman."
Thus he surpassed him.

3.10.s: sa yad dha vā enam etat pitā yonyāṃ reto bhūtaṃ siñcaty ādityo hainaṃ tad yonyāṃ reto bhūtaṃ siñcati sa hāsya tatra mṛtyor īśe |
3.10.d: स यद् ध वा एनम् एतत् पिता योन्यां रेतो भूतं सिञ्चत्य् आदित्यो हैनं तद् योन्यां रेतो भूतं सिञ्चति स हास्य तत्र मृत्योर् ईशे ।
3.10.e: When the father thus emits him as seed into the womb, then the sun thus emits him as seed in the womb. He there lords over this death.
3.10.m:
Now, when the father pours him into the womb as semen, Āditya pours him into the womb as semen.
He rules over his death there.

3.10.s: atho yad evainam etat pitā yonyāṃ reto bhūtaṃ siñcati tad dha vāva sa tato 'nusambhavati prāṇaṃ ca yadā hy eva retas siktam prāṇa āviśaty atha tat sambhavati |
3.10.d: अथो यद् एवैनम् एतत् पिता योन्यां रेतो भूतं सिञ्चति तद् ध वाव स ततो ऽनुसम्भवति प्राणं च यदा ह्य् एव रेतस् सिक्तम् प्राण आविशत्य् अथ तत् सम्भवति ।
3.10.m:
And when the father pours him into the womb as semen, then he is born from that and from breath;
for when breath enters the poured semen, then it comes into being.

3.10.s: atho yad evainam etad dīkṣayanty agnir haivainaṃ tad yonyāṃ reto bhūtaṃ siñcati sa haivāsya tatra mṛtyor īśe |
3.10.d: अथो यद् एवैनम् एतद् दीक्षयन्त्य् अग्निर् हैवैनं तद् योन्यां रेतो भूतं सिञ्चति स हैवास्य तत्र मृत्योर् ईशे ।
3.10.e: And when the father thus emits him as seed into the womb, verily he thence comes into existence after that [seed] and after breath. For when breath enters the emitted seed, then it comes into being, e. And when they thus consecrate him, it is Agni who thus emits him as seed into the womb. He there lords over this death,
3.10.m:
And when they consecrate him, Agni indeed pours him into the womb as semen.
He rules over his death there.

3.10.s: atho yām evaitāṃ vaisarjanīyām āhutim adhvaryur juhoti tām eva sa tato 'nusambhavati chandāṃsi caiva |
3.10.d: अथो याम् एवैतां वैसर्जनीयाम् आहुतिम् अध्वर्युर् जुहोति ताम् एव स ततो ऽनुसम्भवति छन्दांसि चैव ।
3.10.e: Now what vdisarjana-oEev'mg the adhvaryu offers, after that he thence comes into existence and after the metres.
3.10.m: And whichever vaisarjanīya oblation the adhvaryu offers, he is born from that and from the metres.

3.10.s: atha ya enam etad asmāl lokāt pretaṃ cityām ādadhati candramā haivainaṃ tad yonyāṃ reto bhūtāṃ siñcati sa u haivāsya tatra mṛtyor īśe |
3.10.d: अथ य एनम् एतद् अस्माल् लोकात् प्रेतं चित्याम् आदधति चन्द्रमा हैवैनं तद् योन्यां रेतो भूतां सिञ्चति स उ हैवास्य तत्र मृत्योर् ईशे ।
3.10.e: And when they thus lay him, having departed from this world, on the funeral pyre, it is the moon who thus emits him as seed into the womb. He there lords over this death.
3.10.m:
And when they place him, departed from this world, upon the funeral pyre, the Moon indeed pours him into the womb as semen.
And he rules over his death there.

3.10.s: atho yad evainam etad asmāl lokāt pretaṃ cityām ādadhaty atho yā evaitā avokṣaṇīyā āpas tā eva sa tato 'nusambhavati prāṇam v eva prāṇo hy āpaḥ |
3.10.d: अथो यद् एवैनम् एतद् अस्माल् लोकात् प्रेतं चित्याम् आदधत्य् अथो या एवैता अवोक्षणीया आपस् ता एव स ततो ऽनुसम्भवति प्राणम् व् एव प्राणो ह्य् आपः ।
3.10.e: Now when they put him, having departed from this world, on the funeral pyre, now what the waters for sprinkling are, after those he thence comes into existence and after breath also. For breath is the waters.
3.10.m:
And when they place him, departed from this world, upon the funeral pyre, and whatever sprinkling waters these are, he is born from them and from breath;
for breath is the waters.

3.10.s: taṃ ha vā evaṃvid udgātā yajamānam om ity etenākṣareṇādityam mṛtyum ativahati vāg ity agniṃ hum iti vāyum bhā iti candramasam |
3.10.d: तं ह वा एवंविद् उद्गाता यजमानम् ओम् इत्य् एतेनाक्षरेणादित्यम् मृत्युम् अतिवहति वाग् इत्य् अग्निं हुम् इति वायुम् भा इति चन्द्रमसम् ।
3.10.e: Him sacrificing an udgdtar who knows thus carries beyond the sun, [i. e. beyond] death, by means of this syllable, viz. om; [saying] vac [he carries him] beyond Agni; [saying] hum, beyond Vayu; [saying] bhd, beyond the moon.
3.10.m: Such a knowing udgātṛ carries that sacrificer across the death that is Āditya with the syllable 'om', across Agni with 'speech', across Vāyu with 'hum', and across the Moon with 'bhā'.

3.10.s: tān vā etān mṛtyūn sāmnodgātātmānaṃ ca yajamānaṃ cātivahaty om ity etenākṣareṇa prāṇenāmunādityena |
3.10.d: तान् वा एतान् मृत्यून् साम्नोद्गातात्मानं च यजमानं चातिवहत्य् ओम् इत्य् एतेनाक्षरेण प्राणेनामुनादित्येन ।
3.10.e: Verily beyond these same deaths an udgdtar carries himself and the sacrificer, by means of this syllable, viz. om, by means of breath, by means of yonder sun.
3.10.m: Across these deaths the udgātṛ carries himself and the sacrificer by means of the sāman, by this syllable 'om', by breath, and by that Āditya.

3.10.s: tasyaiṣa śloka utaiṣāṃ jyeṣṭha uta vā kaniṣṭha utaiṣām putra uta vā pitaiṣām eko ha devo manasi praviṣṭaḥ pūrvo ha jajñe sa u garbhe 'ntar iti |
3.10.d: तस्यैष श्लोक उतैषां ज्येष्ठ उत वा कनिष्ठ उतैषाम् पुत्र उत वा पितैषाम् एको ह देवो मनसि प्रविष्टः पूर्वो ह जज्ञे स उ गर्भे ऽन्तर् इति ।
3.10.e: About this there is this Śloka: " Is he the oldest of them or the youngest? Is he their son, or their father? Truly one god is entered in the mind; he was born of old and he is within the womb."
3.10.m:
Regarding this there is this verse:
"Both their eldest and their youngest, both their son and their father— / the one god entered into the mind; he was born first, and he is within the womb."

3.10.s: tad yad eṣo 'bhyukta imam eva puruṣaṃ yo 'yam āchanno 'ntar om ity etenaivākṣareṇa prāṇenaivāmunaivādityena | dvitīye 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ dvitīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
3.10.d: तद् यद् एषो ऽभ्युक्त इमम् एव पुरुषं यो ऽयम् आछन्नो ऽन्तर् ओम् इत्य् एतेनैवाक्षरेण प्राणेनैवामुनैवादित्येन । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः द्वितीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
3.10.e: In that he is spoken of, this same man who is concealed within, by just that syllable om, by breath, by yonder sun [ ].
3.10.m:
As to what was referred to in verse, it is this very person who is covered within, by this very syllable om, by breath, by that sun.
Fifth khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.
The second anuvāka is concluded.

3.11.s: trir ha vai puruṣo mriyate trir jāyate |
3.11.d: त्रिर् ह वै पुरुषो म्रियते त्रिर् जायते ।
3.11.e: Verily, thrice man dies, thrice he is born.
3.11.m: Three times indeed a man dies, three times he is born.

3.11.s: sa haitad eva prathamam mriyate yad retas siktaṃ sambhūtam bhavati sa prāṇam evābhisambhavati āśām abhijāyate |
3.11.d: स हैतद् एव प्रथमम् म्रियते यद् रेतस् सिक्तं सम्भूतम् भवति स प्राणम् एवाभिसम्भवति आशाम् अभिजायते ।
3.11.e: Then he dies for the first time, when the seed, emitted, comes into being. He is converted into breath; he is born into space.

3.11.s: athaitad dvitīyam mriyate yad dīkṣate sa chandāṃsy evābhisambhavati dakṣiṇām abhijāyate |
3.11.d: अथैतद् द्वितीयम् म्रियते यद् दीक्षते स छन्दांस्य् एवाभिसम्भवति दक्षिणाम् अभिजायते ।
3.11.e: Then he dies for the second time, when he consecrates himself. He is converted into the metres; lie is born unto the sacrificial gift.

3.11.s: athaitat tṛtīyam mriyate yan mriyate sa śraddhām evābhisambhavati lokam abhijāyate |
3.11.d: अथैतत् तृतीयम् म्रियते यन् म्रियते स श्रद्धाम् एवाभिसम्भवति लोकम् अभिजायते ।
3.11.e: Then he dies for the third time, when he dies. He is converted into faith; he is born into [his] world.

3.11.s: tad etat tryāvṛd gāyatraṃ gāyati tasya prathamayāvṛtemam eva lokaṃ jayati yad u cāsmiṃl loke tad etena cainam prāṇena samardhayati yam abhisambhavaty etāṃ cāsmā āśām prayacchati yām abhijāyate |
3.11.d: तद् एतत् त्र्यावृद् गायत्रं गायति तस्य प्रथमयावृतेमम् एव लोकं जयति यद् उ चास्मिंल् लोके तद् एतेन चैनम् प्राणेन समर्धयति यम् अभिसम्भवत्य् एतां चास्मा आशाम् प्रयच्छति याम् अभिजायते ।
3.11.e: Therefore he sings the gāyatra [-chant] in three turns (dvrt). By its first turn he conquers this world, and what there is in this world. Thus he causes him to thrive with that breath into which he is converted, and he gives him that space unto which he is born.

3.11.s: atha dvitīyayāvṛtedam evāntarikṣaṃ jayati yad u cāntarikṣe tad etaiś cainaṃ chandobhis samardhayati yāny abhisambhavati etāṃ cāsmai dakṣiṇām prayacchati yām abhijāyate |
3.11.d: अथ द्वितीययावृतेदम् एवान्तरिक्षं जयति यद् उ चान्तरिक्षे तद् एतैश् चैनं छन्दोभिस् समर्धयति यान्य् अभिसम्भवति एतां चास्मै दक्षिणाम् प्रयच्छति याम् अभिजायते ।
3.11.e: And by its second turn he conquers this atmosphere, and what there is in the atmosphere. Thus he causes him to thrive with those metres into which he is converted, and he gives him that sacrificial gift unto which he is born.

3.11.s: atha tṛtīyayāvṛtāmum eva lokam jayati yad u cāmuṣmiṃl loke tad etayā cainaṃ śraddhayā samardhayati yayaivainam etac chraddhayāgnāv abhyādadhati sam ayam ito bhaviṣyatīti etaṃ cāsmai lokam prayacchati yam abhijāyate | tṛtīye 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.11.d: अथ तृतीययावृतामुम् एव लोकम् जयति यद् उ चामुष्मिंल् लोके तद् एतया चैनं श्रद्धया समर्धयति ययैवैनम् एतच् छ्रद्धयाग्नाव् अभ्यादधति सम् अयम् इतो भविष्यतीति एतं चास्मै लोकम् प्रयच्छति यम् अभिजायते । तृतीये ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
3.11.e: And with the third turn he conquers yonder world, and what there is in yonder world. Thus he causes him to thrive with that faith with which faith they lay him into the fire [saying]: "This one, from here, will come to life;" and he gives him that world unto which he is born.
3.11.m:
Then with the third turn, he wins that world and whatever is in that world;
thereby he enriches him with that faith with which they place him into the fire [thinking], 'He will exist whole from here,'
and bestows upon him that world into which he is born.
First khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka.

3.12.s: etad vai tisṛbhir āvṛdbhir imāṃś ca lokāñ jayaty etaiś cainam bhūtais samardhayati yāny abhisambhavati |
3.12.d: एतद् वै तिसृभिर् आवृद्भिर् इमांश् च लोकाञ् जयत्य् एतैश् चैनम् भूतैस् समर्धयति यान्य् अभिसम्भवति ।
3.12.e: Verily, thus with three turns he conquers these worlds, and he causes him to thrive with those things into which he is converted.
3.12.m: Indeed, by these three turns he wins these worlds and enriches him with these beings into which he enters.

3.12.s: atha vā ato hiṅkārasyaiva taṃ ha svarge loke santam mṛtyur anvety aśanayā |
3.12.d: अथ वा अतो हिङ्कारस्यैव तं ह स्वर्गे लोके सन्तम् मृत्युर् अन्वेत्य् अशनया ।
3.12.e: Now from here concerning the hinkdra. After him, being in the heavenly world, death goes, hunger.
3.12.m:
Now then concerning the hiṅkāra alone:
when he is in the heavenly world, hunger, which is death, pursues him.

3.12.s: śrīr vā eṣā prajāpatis sāmno yad dhiṅkāraḥ tam id udgātā śriyā prajāpatinā hiṅkāreṇa mṛtyum apasedhati |
3.12.d: श्रीर् वा एषा प्रजापतिस् साम्नो यद् धिङ्कारः तम् इद् उद्गाता श्रिया प्रजापतिना हिङ्कारेण मृत्युम् अपसेधति ।
3.12.e: The hinkdra is the fortune, Prajapati of the sāman. That death the udgdtar drives away by means of fortune, of Prajapati, of the hinkdra.
3.12.m:
The hiṅkāra is prosperity, it is Prajāpati of the sāman.
With prosperity, with Prajāpati, with the hiṅkāra, the udgātṛ keeps off death from him.

3.12.s: hum mety āha mātra nu gā yatraitad yajamāna iti haitat |
3.12.d: हुम् मेत्य् आह मात्र नु गा यत्रैतद् यजमान इति हैतत् ।
3.12.e: He says hum md: that is, " Do not now go thither, where the sacrificer now is." As, driven by a better one, a worse one trembles before hitn, even so death, evil, trembles before him.
3.12.m: He says: 'hum mā'—this means: 'Do not go there now, where this sacrificer is.'

3.12.s: sa yathā śreyasā siddhaḥ pāpīyān prativijata evaṃ haivāsmān mṛtyuḥ pāpmā prativijate |
3.12.d: स यथा श्रेयसा सिद्धः पापीयान् प्रतिविजत एवं हैवास्मान् मृत्युः पाप्मा प्रतिविजते ।
3.12.m: Just as a worse person chased away by a better one shrinks back, so does evil death shrink back from him.

3.12.s: yan mety āha candramā vai mā māsaḥ eṣa ha vai mā māsaḥ tasmān mety āha bhā iti haitat parokṣeṇeva yasmād v eva mety āha yad v eva mety āhaitāni trīṇi tasmān mety brūyāt | tṛtīye 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.12.d: यन् मेत्य् आह चन्द्रमा वै मा मासः एष ह वै मा मासः तस्मान् मेत्य् आह भा इति हैतत् परोक्षेणेव यस्माद् व् एव मेत्य् आह यद् व् एव मेत्य् आहैतानि त्रीणि तस्मान् मेत्य् ब्रूयात् । तृतीये ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
3.12.e: As for his saying md, md is the m^oon, the month. Verily, this month is md. Therefore he says md; that is bhd, in an occult way, as it were. As to why he says md—in that he says md, there are these three [meanings]. Therefore he should say md.
3.12.m:
When he says 'mā': the moon indeed is 'mā', the month [māsa].
This month indeed is 'mā'.
Therefore he says 'mā'.
This is indirectly as 'bhā' [light].
And because he says 'mā', and because he says 'mā'—these three [meanings].
Therefore he should say 'mā'.
Second khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka.

3.13.s: hum bhā iti brahmavarcasakāmasya bhatīva hi brahmavarcasam |
3.13.d: हुम् भा इति ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य भतीव हि ब्रह्मवर्चसम् ।
3.13.e: Hum bhd are [the utterances] of him who desires lustre in sacred lore. For lustre in sacred lore shines (Śma), as it were.
3.13.m:
'hum bhā'—for one who desires spiritual lustre;
for spiritual lustre shines [bhāti], as it were.

3.13.s: hum bo iti paśukāmasya bo iti ha paśavo vāśyante |
3.13.d: हुम् बो इति पशुकामस्य बो इति ह पशवो वाश्यन्ते ।
3.13.e: Mum bo a.re [the utterances] of him who desires cattle. For cattle low bo.
3.13.m:
'hum bo'—for one who desires cattle;
for cattle low as 'bo'.

3.13.s: hum bag iti śrīkāmasya bag iti ha śriyam paṇāyanti |
3.13.d: हुम् बग् इति श्रीकामस्य बग् इति ह श्रियम् पणायन्ति ।
3.13.e: Hum bag are [the utterances] of him who desires fortune. For saying bag they, extol fortune.
3.13.m:
'hum bag'—for one who desires prosperity;
for people praise prosperity as 'bag'.

3.13.s: hum bhā ovā ity etad evopagītam |
3.13.d: हुम् भा ओवा इत्य् एतद् एवोपगीतम् ।
3.13.e: Ham bhd ovd, that is sung in response. " Let him sing turning about unto something great, as it were," Naka used to say; " he becomes the owner of a great village, the owner of a great resting place." That is as if, having caused to run against a post, with another or another one should go about [it],
3.13.m: 'hum bhā ovā'—this is the accompanying singing.

3.13.s: mahad ivābhiparivartayan gāyed iti ha smāha nāko mahāgrāmo mahāniveśo bhavatīti sa yathā sthāṇum arpayitvetareṇa vetareṇa vā pariyāyāt tādṛk tat |
3.13.d: महद् इवाभिपरिवर्तयन् गायेद् इति ह स्माह नाको महाग्रामो महानिवेशो भवतीति स यथा स्थाणुम् अर्पयित्वेतरेण वेतरेण वा परियायात् तादृक् तत् ।
3.13.e: [But] Śatyayani said regarding this: " For what purpose should he cause to ran against a post? Now that is sung in response. Let him pay no attention to that."
3.13.m:
'One should sing bringing it around as if large,' said Nāka, 'one becomes of a great community, of a great settlement.'
That is just as if one, having fixed a post, should go around on this side or that side.

3.13.s: tad u hovāca śāṭyāyaniḥ kasmai kāmāya sthāṇum arpayet athopagītam evaitat naivaitad ādriyeteti |
3.13.d: तद् उ होवाच शाट्यायनिः कस्मै कामाय स्थाणुम् अर्पयेत् अथोपगीतम् एवैतत् नैवैतद् आद्रियेतेति ।

3.13.s: nu hiṅkārānāṃ atha vā ato nidhanam eva ovā iti dve akṣare anto vai sāmno nidhanam antas svargo lokānām anto bradhnasya viṣṭapam |
3.13.d: नु हिङ्कारानां अथ वा अतो निधनम् एव ओवा इति द्वे अक्षरे अन्तो वै साम्नो निधनम् अन्तस् स्वर्गो लोकानाम् अन्तो ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपम् ।
3.13.e: So much about the hinkdras. Henceforth regarding the nidhana. Ovd is two syllables. Verily the nidhana is the end of the sāman, heaven is the end of the worlds, the summit is the end of the ruddj one.
3.13.m:
So much for the hiṅkāras.
Now then concerning the finale [nidhana] alone:
'ovā'—these are two syllables.
The finale is the end of the sāman, heaven is the end of the worlds, the highest region of the sun is the end.

3.13.s: tam etad udgātā yajamānam om ity etenākṣareṇānte svarge loke dadhāti |
3.13.d: तम् एतद् उद्गाता यजमानम् ओम् इत्य् एतेनाक्षरेणान्ते स्वर्गे लोके दधाति ।
3.13.e: Thus the udgdtar places the sacrificer by means of this syllable om in the end in the heavenly world.
3.13.m: By this syllable om, the udgātṛ places that sacrificer at the end, in the heavenly world.

3.13.s: ya u ha vā apakṣo vṛkṣāgraṃ gacchaty ava vai sa tataḥ padyate atha yad vai pakṣī vṛkṣāgre yad asidhārāyāṃ yat kṣuradhārāyām āste na vai sa tato 'vapadyate pakṣābhyāṃ hi saṃyata āste |
3.13.d: य उ ह वा अपक्षो वृक्षाग्रं गच्छत्य् अव वै स ततः पद्यते अथ यद् वै पक्षी वृक्षाग्रे यद् असिधारायां यत् क्षुरधारायाम् आस्ते न वै स ततो ऽवपद्यते पक्षाभ्यां हि संयत आस्ते ।
3.13.e: Verily he who without wings goes up to the top of a tree, he falls down froln it. But if one having wings sits on the top of a tree, or on the edge of a sword, or on the edge of a razor, verily he does not fall down from it. For he sits supported by his wings.

3.13.s: tam etad udgātā yajamānam om ity etenākṣareṇa svarapakṣaṃ kṛtvānte svarge loke dadhāti sa yathā pakṣy abibhyad āsītaivam eva svarge loke 'bibhyad āste 'thācarati |
3.13.d: तम् एतद् उद्गाता यजमानम् ओम् इत्य् एतेनाक्षरेण स्वरपक्षं कृत्वान्ते स्वर्गे लोके दधाति स यथा पक्ष्य् अबिभ्यद् आसीतैवम् एव स्वर्गे लोके ऽबिभ्यद् आस्ते ऽथाचरति ।
3.13.e: Thus the udgdtar, making him, the sacrificer, by means of that syllable om, possess sound as wings, puts him in the end in the heavenly world. As one with wings would sit without fear, even so he sits without fear in the heavenly world, [andj likewise moves about.
3.13.m:
By this syllable om, having given him wings of sound [svara], the udgātṛ places that sacrificer at the end, in the heavenly world.
Just as a winged [bird] would sit without fear, even so he sits without fear in the heavenly world, and then moves about.

3.13.s: te ha vā ete akṣare devalokaś caiva manuṣyalokaś ca ādityaś ca ha vā ete akṣare candramāś ca |
3.13.d: ते ह वा एते अक्षरे देवलोकश् चैव मनुष्यलोकश् च आदित्यश् च ह वा एते अक्षरे चन्द्रमाश् च ।
3.13.e: These same two syllables are the world of the gods and the world of man. The sun these two syllables are, and the moon.
3.13.m:
These two syllables are the world of the gods and the world of human beings;
and these two syllables are the sun and the moon.

3.13.s: āditya eva devalokaś candramā manuṣyalokaḥ om ity ādityo vāg iti candramāḥ |
3.13.d: आदित्य एव देवलोकश् चन्द्रमा मनुष्यलोकः ओम् इत्य् आदित्यो वाग् इति चन्द्रमाः ।
3.13.e: The sun is the world of the gods, [and] the moon is the world of man. The sun is om, the moon is vac.
3.13.m:
The sun is the world of the gods; the moon is the world of human beings.
Om is the sun; 'vāc' is the moon.

3.13.s: tam etad udgātā yajamānam om ity etenākṣareṇādityaṃ devalokaṃ gamayati | tṛtīye 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.13.d: तम् एतद् उद्गाता यजमानम् ओम् इत्य् एतेनाक्षरेणादित्यं देवलोकं गमयति । तृतीये ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
3.13.e: Thus the udgdtar causes him, the sacrificer, to go to the heavenly world by means of this syllable
3.13.m:
By this syllable om, the udgātṛ makes that sacrificer reach the sun, the world of the gods.
Third khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka.

3.14.s: taṃ hāgatam pṛcchati kas tvam asīti sa yo ha nāmnā vā gotreṇa vā prabrūte taṃ hāha yas te 'yam mayy ātmābhūd eṣa te sa iti |
3.14.d: तं हागतम् पृच्छति कस् त्वम् असीति स यो ह नाम्ना वा गोत्रेण वा प्रब्रूते तं हाह यस् ते ऽयम् मय्य् आत्माभूद् एष ते स इति ।
3.14.e: Him, having come, he asks: "Who art thou?" When he announces himself, either by his [personal] name or by his family [name], he says to him: "This self of thee that hath been in me, that same is thine."
3.14.m:
He asks him when he has arrived: 'Who are you?'
If he announces himself by name or by clan [gotra], he says to him: 'This self of yours which was in me, that is yours.'

3.14.s: tasmin hātman pratipat tam ṛtavas sampadāryapad gṛhītam apakarṣanti tasya hāhorātre lokam āpnutaḥ |
3.14.d: तस्मिन् हात्मन् प्रतिपत् तम् ऋतवस् सम्पदार्यपद् गृहीतम् अपकर्षन्ति तस्य हाहोरात्रे लोकम् आप्नुतः ।
3.14.e: In this self is the beginning {?pratipat). Him seized the seasons drag away; of him day and night obtain the world.

3.14.s: tasmā u haitena prabruvīta ko 'ham asmi suvas tvam sa tvāṃ svargyaṃ svar agām iti |
3.14.d: तस्मा उ हैतेन प्रब्रुवीत को ऽहम् अस्मि सुवस् त्वम् स त्वां स्वर्ग्यं स्वर् अगाम् इति ।
3.14.e: To him be should answer thus: "Who (ka) am I, heaven [art] thou. As such I have gone to thee, the heavenly heaven."
3.14.m:
To him he should declare with this: 'Who am I? You are heaven.
Such as I am, I have come to you, the heavenly light [svar].'

3.14.s: ko ha vai prajāpatir atha haivaṃvid eva suvargaḥ sa hi suvar gacchati |
3.14.d: को ह वै प्रजापतिर् अथ हैवंविद् एव सुवर्गः स हि सुवर् गच्छति ।
3.14.e: "Verily Prajapati is who {ka), and he who knows thus is heaven-going; for he goes to heaven,
3.14.m:
Who [Ka] indeed is Prajāpati; and one who knows thus is heavenly;
for he goes to heaven.

3.14.s: taṃ hāha yas tvam asi so 'ham asmi yo 'ham asmi sa tvam asy ehīti |
3.14.d: तं हाह यस् त्वम् असि सो ऽहम् अस्मि यो ऽहम् अस्मि स त्वम् अस्य् एहीति ।
3.14.e: He says to him: "Who thou art, that one am I; who I am, that one art thou; come!"
3.14.m: He says to him: 'Who you are, that am I; who I am, that are you. Come!'

3.14.s: sa etam eva sukṛtarasam praviśati yad u ha vā asmiṃl loke manuṣyā yajante yat sādhu kurvanti tad eṣām ūrdhvam annādyam utsīdati tad amuṃ candramasam manuṣyalokam praviśati |
3.14.d: स एतम् एव सुकृतरसम् प्रविशति यद् उ ह वा अस्मिंल् लोके मनुष्या यजन्ते यत् साधु कुर्वन्ति तद् एषाम् ऊर्ध्वम् अन्नाद्यम् उत्सीदति तद् अमुं चन्द्रमसम् मनुष्यलोकम् प्रविशति ।
3.14.e: He enters this sap of good deeds. And what men in this world sacrifice, what good [deeds] they do, that of them rises upward [as] food-eating; it enters yonder moon, the world of men.

3.14.s: tasyedam mānuṣanikāśanam aṇḍam udare 'ntas sambhavati tasyordhvam annādyam utsīdati stanāv abhi sa yad ājāyate 'thāsmai mātā stanam annādyam prayacchati |
3.14.d: तस्येदम् मानुषनिकाशनम् अण्डम् उदरे ऽन्तस् सम्भवति तस्योर्ध्वम् अन्नाद्यम् उत्सीदति स्तनाव् अभि स यद् आजायते ऽथास्मै माता स्तनम् अन्नाद्यम् प्रयच्छति ।
3.14.e: This human-like egg of him comes into being within the belly. Of it the food-eating rises upward toward the two breasts. When he is born, then the mother offers her breast to him for food-eating,

3.14.s: ajāto ha vai tāvat puruṣo yāvan na yajate sa yajñenaiva jāyate sa yathāṇḍam prathamanirbhiṇṇam evam eva |
3.14.d: अजातो ह वै तावत् पुरुषो यावन् न यजते स यज्ञेनैव जायते स यथाण्डम् प्रथमनिर्भिण्णम् एवम् एव ।
3.14.e: Verily unborn is the man in so far as he does not sacrifice. It is through the sacrifice that he is born; just as an egg first burst.

3.14.s: tadā taṃ ha vā evaṃvid udgātā yajamānam om ity etenākṣareṇādityaṃ devalokaṃ gamayati vāg ity asmā uttareṇākṣareṇa candramasam annādyam akṣitim prayacchati |
3.14.d: तदा तं ह वा एवंविद् उद्गाता यजमानम् ओम् इत्य् एतेनाक्षरेणादित्यं देवलोकं गमयति वाग् इत्य् अस्मा उत्तरेणाक्षरेण चन्द्रमसम् अन्नाद्यम् अक्षितिम् प्रयच्छति ।
3.14.e: Then the udgdtar knowing thus causes him, the sacrificer, through this syllable, viz. om, to enter the sun, the world of the gods. By means of the next syllable, viz. vac, he gives him the moon, food-eating, imperishableness.
3.14.m:
Then indeed the udgātṛ who knows thus makes that sacrificer reach the sun, the world of the gods, by this syllable om;
by the subsequent syllable 'vāc' he bestows upon him the moon, food-essence, imperishability.

3.14.s: atha yasyaitad avidvān udgāyati na haivainaṃ devalokaṃ gamayati no enam annādyena samardhayati |
3.14.d: अथ यस्यैतद् अविद्वान् उद्गायति न हैवैनं देवलोकं गमयति नो एनम् अन्नाद्येन समर्धयति ।
3.14.e: But whose udgītha one not knowing thus sings, verily he does not cause him to enter the world of the gods, nor to thrive through food-eating,
3.14.m: Now for whomsoever an unknowing one sings the udgītha, he neither makes him reach the world of the gods nor does he enrich him with food-essence.

3.14.s: sa yathāṇḍaṃ vidigdhaṃ śayītānnādyam alabhamānam evam eva vidigdhaś śete 'nnādyam alabhamānaḥ |
3.14.d: स यथाण्डं विदिग्धं शयीतान्नाद्यम् अलभमानम् एवम् एव विदिग्धश् शेते ऽन्नाद्यम् अलभमानः ।
3.14.e: As an egg would lie besmeared (?), not receiving any food, so he lies besmeared (?), not receiving any food.
3.14.m: Just as an egg smeared [with dirt/filth] would lie without obtaining food-essence, even so he lies smeared, without obtaining food-essence.

3.14.s: tasmād u haivaṃvidam evodgāpayeta evaṃvid ihaivodgātar iti hūtaḥ pratiśṛṇuyāt | tṛtīye 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ tṛtīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
3.14.d: तस्माद् उ हैवंविदम् एवोद्गापयेत एवंविद् इहैवोद्गातर् इति हूतः प्रतिशृणुयात् । तृतीये ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः तृतीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
3.14.e: Therefore lie should cause only one knowing thus to sing the udgītha. Only one knowing thus here being addressed with "O udgdtar'''' should answer.
3.14.m:
Therefore one should have only one who knows thus sing the udgītha.
Called with 'O udgātṛ who knows thus here!', he should respond.
Fifth khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka.
The third anuvāka is concluded.

3.15.s: vāg iti hendro viśvāmitrāyoktham uvāca tad etad viśvāmitrā upāsate vācam eva |
3.15.d: वाग् इति हेन्द्रो विश्वामित्रायोक्थम् उवाच तद् एतद् विश्वामित्रा उपासते वाचम् एव ।
3.15.e: Indra said the uktha for Vi9vamitra [with] vac. That same the descendants of Vi9vamitra worship, just speech.
3.15.m:
'Speech [vāc]'—thus Indra spoke the praise-hymn [uktha] to Viśvāmitra;
that very thing the Viśvāmitras revere as speech alone.

3.15.s: manur ha vasiṣṭhāya brahmatvam uvāca tasmād āhur vāsiṣṭham eva brahmeti |
3.15.d: मनुर् ह वसिष्ठाय ब्रह्मत्वम् उवाच तस्माद् आहुर् वासिष्ठम् एव ब्रह्मेति ।
3.15.e: Manu declared to Vasistha brahman-hooA. Therefore they say: " The brahman belongs to Vasistha."
3.15.m:
Manu taught the office of the brahman priest to Vasiṣṭha;
therefore they say: 'The brahman priest is indeed a descendant of Vasiṣṭha.'

3.15.s: tad u vā āhur evaṃvid eva brahmā ka u evaṃvidaṃ vāsiṣṭham arhatīti |
3.15.d: तद् उ वा आहुर् एवंविद् एव ब्रह्मा क उ एवंविदं वासिष्ठम् अर्हतीति ।
3.15.e: This they also say: " One knowing thus is the hrahman-Śr\est; and who is equal to a Vasistha knowing thus?"
3.15.m:
Moreover, they also say: 'One who knows thus is indeed the brahman priest.
And who is equal to the one who knows thus as a descendant of Vasiṣṭha?'

3.15.s: prajāpatiḥ prājijaniṣata sa tapo 'tapyata sa aikṣata hanta nu pratiṣṭhāṃ janayai tato yāḥ prajās srakṣye tā etad eva pratiṣṭhāsyanti nāpratiṣṭhāś carantīḥ pradaghiṣyanta iti |
3.15.d: प्रजापतिः प्राजिजनिषत स तपो ऽतप्यत स ऐक्षत हन्त नु प्रतिष्ठां जनयै ततो याः प्रजास् स्रक्ष्ये ता एतद् एव प्रतिष्ठास्यन्ति नाप्रतिष्ठाश् चरन्तीः प्रदघिष्यन्त इति ।
3.15.e: Prajapati was desirous to have progeny. He performed penance. He considered: " Come now, I will generate a firm footing. What oifspring I shall generate thereafter, that will thus stand firm; it will not, moving about without firm foundation, fall (?)." He generated this world, [also] the world of atmosphere [and] yonder world. Having generated these three worlds, he toiled upon [them].
3.15.m:
Prajāpati desired to produce offspring.
He performed ascetic heat.
He considered: 'Come, let me generate a firm foundation; then the offspring which I shall emit will establish themselves upon it and, not wandering without a firm foundation, will not perish.'
