3.15.s: sa imaṃ lokam ajanayad antarikṣalokam amuṃ lokam iti tān imāṃs trīṃl lokāñ janayitvābhyaśrāmyat |
3.15.d: स इमं लोकम् अजनयद् अन्तरिक्षलोकम् अमुं लोकम् इति तान् इमांस् त्रींल् लोकाञ् जनयित्वाभ्यश्राम्यत् ।
3.15.m:
He generated this world, the world of the intermediate space, [and] that world.
Having generated these three worlds, he exerted himself.

3.15.s: tān samatapat tebhyas saṃtaptebhyas trīṇi śukrāṇy udāyann agniḥ pṛthivyā vāyur antarikṣād ādityo divaḥ |
3.15.d: तान् समतपत् तेभ्यस् संतप्तेभ्यस् त्रीणि शुक्राण्य् उदायन्न् अग्निः पृथिव्या वायुर् अन्तरिक्षाद् आदित्यो दिवः ।
3.15.e: He heated them together. From them being heated together three bright [bodies] went up: Agni from the earth, Vayu from the atmosphere, the sun from the sky.
3.15.m:
He heated them thoroughly.
From them, when thoroughly heated, three essences went forth: Agni from the earth, Vāyu from the intermediate space, Āditya from heaven.

3.15.s: sa etāni śukrāṇi punar abhy evātapat tebhyas saṃtaptebhyas trīṇy eva śukrāṇy udāyann ṛgveda evāgner yajurvedo vāyos sāmaveda ādityāt |
3.15.d: स एतानि शुक्राणि पुनर् अभ्य् एवातपत् तेभ्यस् संतप्तेभ्यस् त्रीण्य् एव शुक्राण्य् उदायन्न् ऋग्वेद एवाग्नेर् यजुर्वेदो वायोस् सामवेद आदित्यात् ।
3.15.e: He again heated these bright [bodies]. From them being heated together three bright [bodies] went up: the Rigveda from Agni, the Yajurveda from Vayu, the Samaveda from the sun.
3.15.m:
He thoroughly heated these essences again.
From them, when thoroughly heated, three essences went forth: the Ṛgveda from Agni, the Yajurveda from Vāyu, the Sāmaveda from Āditya.

3.15.s: sa etāni śukrāṇi punar abhy evātapat tebhyas saṃtaptebhyas trīṇy eva śukrāṇy udāyan bhūr ity eva rgvedād bhuva iti yajurvedāt svar iti sāmavedāt tad eva |
3.15.d: स एतानि शुक्राणि पुनर् अभ्य् एवातपत् तेभ्यस् संतप्तेभ्यस् त्रीण्य् एव शुक्राण्य् उदायन् भूर् इत्य् एव र्ग्वेदाद् भुव इति यजुर्वेदात् स्वर् इति सामवेदात् तद् एव ।
3.15.e: He again heated these bright [bodies]. From them being heated together three bright [bodies] went up: bhus from the liigveda, bhuvas from the Yajurveda, svar from the Samaveda, just so.
3.15.m:
He thoroughly heated these essences again.
From them, when thoroughly heated, three essences went forth: bhūḥ from the Ṛgveda, bhuvaḥ from the Yajurveda, svaḥ from the Sāmaveda—just that.

3.15.s: tad dha vai trayyai vidyāyai śukram etāvad idaṃ sarvam sa yo vai trayīṃ vidyāṃ viduṣo lokas so 'sya loko bhavati ya evaṃ veda | caturthe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.15.d: तद् ध वै त्रय्यै विद्यायै शुक्रम् एतावद् इदं सर्वम् स यो वै त्रयीं विद्यां विदुषो लोकस् सो ऽस्य लोको भवति य एवं वेद । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
3.15.e: That is the brightness of the threefold knowledge. So great is this all. Verily what the world is of him who knows the threefold knowledge, that becomes the world of him who knows thus.
3.15.m:
That indeed is the essence of the threefold knowledge.
This whole [universe] is just this much.
Whatever world belongs to the one who knows the threefold knowledge, that becomes his world who knows thus.
First subsection in the fourth lesson.

3.16.s: ayaṃ vāva yajño yo 'yam pavate tasya vāk ca manaś ca vartanyau vācā ca hy eṣa etan manasā ca vartate |
3.16.d: अयं वाव यज्ञो यो ऽयम् पवते तस्य वाक् च मनश् च वर्तन्यौ वाचा च ह्य् एष एतन् मनसा च वर्तते ।
3.16.e: This sacrifice verily is he that cleanses here. Speech and mind are the two tracks of it. For thus it rolls along by speech and mind.
3.16.m:
This one who purifies himself (the wind) is indeed the sacrifice.
Its two tracks are speech and mind.
For by speech and by mind this [sacrifice] moves along.

3.16.s: tasya hotādhvaryur udgātety anyatarāṃ vācā vartaniṃ saṃskurvanti tasmāt te vācā kurvanti brahmaiva manasānyatarām tasmāt sa tūṣṇīm āste |
3.16.d: तस्य होताध्वर्युर् उद्गातेत्य् अन्यतरां वाचा वर्तनिं संस्कुर्वन्ति तस्मात् ते वाचा कुर्वन्ति ब्रह्मैव मनसान्यतराम् तस्मात् स तूष्णीम् आस्ते ।
3.16.e: Of it ' hotar ' adhvaryu,' ' udgdtar' arrange the one [track] by speech. Therefore they officiate with speech. The 6raAma>i-priest [arranges] the other by the mind. Therefore he sits in silence,

3.16.s: sa yad dha so 'pi stūyamāne vā śasyamāne vā vāvadyamāna āsītānyatarām evāsyāpi tarhi sa vācā vartaniṃ saṃskuryāt |
3.16.d: स यद् ध सो ऽपि स्तूयमाने वा शस्यमाने वा वावद्यमान आसीतान्यतराम् एवास्यापि तर्हि स वाचा वर्तनिं संस्कुर्यात् ।
3.16.e: If he should sit talking aloud, while the stotra or the pastra are being uttered, then he would arrange with voice the one track of it.
3.16.m: If he too were to sit talking while the praise-song is being chanted or the recitation is being recited, then he too would prepare only one track with speech.

3.16.s: sa yathā puruṣa ekapād yan bhreṣann eti ratho vaikacakro vartamāna evam eva tarhi yajño bhreṣann eti |
3.16.d: स यथा पुरुष एकपाद् यन् भ्रेषन्न् एति रथो वैकचक्रो वर्तमान एवम् एव तर्हि यज्ञो भ्रेषन्न् एति ।
3.16.e: As a one-legged man, going, keeps on tumbling, or a one-wheeled chariot, rolling, even so the sacrifice then keeps on tumbling,
3.16.m: Just as a man walking on one foot goes along stumbling, or a chariot rolling on one wheel [goes along stumbling], even so then the sacrifice goes along stumbling.

3.16.s: etad dha tad vidvān brāhmaṇa uvāca brahmāṇam prātaranuvāka upākṛte vāvadyamānam āsīnam ardhaṃ vā ime tarhi yajñasyāntaragur iti ardhaṃ hi te tarhi yajñasyāntarīyuḥ |
3.16.d: एतद् ध तद् विद्वान् ब्राह्मण उवाच ब्रह्माणम् प्रातरनुवाक उपाकृते वावद्यमानम् आसीनम् अर्धं वा इमे तर्हि यज्ञस्यान्तरगुर् इति अर्धं हि ते तर्हि यज्ञस्यान्तरीयुः ।
3.16.e: A Brahman knowing this said this to a SraAwaw-priest who, when the prdtaranuvdka was began, sat talking aloud: " These here then have excluded half of the sacrifice." For half of the sacrifice they then did exclude.
3.16.m:
Knowing this, a brahmin said to the brahman priest who was sitting talking while the morning recitation was undertaken: 'These [priests] have cut off half of the sacrifice then!'
For then they had cut off half of the sacrifice.

3.16.s: tasmād brahmā prātaranuvāka upākṛte vācaṃyama āsītāparidhānīyāyā ā vaṣaṭkārād itareṣāṃ stutaśastrāṇām evāsaṃsthāyai pavamānānām |
3.16.d: तस्माद् ब्रह्मा प्रातरनुवाक उपाकृते वाचंयम आसीतापरिधानीयाया आ वषट्काराद् इतरेषां स्तुतशस्त्राणाम् एवासंस्थायै पवमानानाम् ।
3.16.e: Therefore the Brahman-priest should sit in silence, when the prdtaranuvdka is begun, till the final verse, till the utterance of vasat of the other stotra and fastra, even till the completion of the libations.
3.16.m: Therefore, when the morning recitation has been undertaken, the brahman priest should sit restraining his speech until the concluding verse, until the vaṣaṭ-call, until the completion of the other chants and recitations, and of the purifying chants.

3.16.s: sa yathā puruṣa ubhayāpād yan bhreṣaṃ na nyeti ratho vobhayācakro vartamāna evam etarhi yajño bhreṣaṃ na nyeti | caturthe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.16.d: स यथा पुरुष उभयापाद् यन् भ्रेषं न न्येति रथो वोभयाचक्रो वर्तमान एवम् एतर्हि यज्ञो भ्रेषं न न्येति । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
3.16.e: As a two-legged man, going, does not take to tumbling, or a two-wheeled chariot, rolling, even so the sacrifice then does not take to tumbling.
3.16.m:
Just as a man walking on both feet does not fall into stumbling, or a chariot rolling on both wheels [does not fall into stumbling], even so now the sacrifice does not fall into stumbling.
Second subsection in the fourth lesson.

3.17.s: sa yadi yajña ṛkto bhreṣann iyād brahmaṇe prabrūtety āhuḥ atha yadi yajuṣṭo brahmaṇe prabrūtety āhuḥ atha yadi sāmato brahmaṇe prabrūtety āhuḥ atha yadi anupasmṛtāt kuta idam ajanīti brahmaṇe prabrūtety evāhuḥ |
3.17.d: स यदि यज्ञ ऋक्तो भ्रेषन्न् इयाद् ब्रह्मणे प्रब्रूतेत्य् आहुः अथ यदि यजुष्टो ब्रह्मणे प्रब्रूतेत्य् आहुः अथ यदि सामतो ब्रह्मणे प्रब्रूतेत्य् आहुः अथ यदि अनुपस्मृतात् कुत इदम् अजनीति ब्रह्मणे प्रब्रूतेत्य् एवाहुः ।
3.17.e: If that sacrifice should go tumbling from the side of the re, they say: "Tell it to the brahman-T^viesV; and if from the yajus, they say: " Tell it to the SraAmaw-priest"; and if from the sāman, they say: " Tell it to the 6raAwia«-priest"; and if from [a cause] not understood—[when they ask]: " Whence hath this arisen?"—they say: "Tell it to the 5mA»iaw-priest."
3.17.m:
If the sacrifice should stumble on account of the ṛc, they say: 'Address the brahman priest!'
Then if on account of the yajus, they say: 'Address the brahman priest!'
Then if on account of the sāman, they say: 'Address the brahman priest!'
Then if from an unknown [cause, asking] 'Whence has this arisen?', they indeed say: 'Address the brahman priest!'

3.17.s: sa brahmā prāṅ udetya sruveṇāgnīdhra ājyaṃ juhuyād bhūr bhuvas svar ity etābhir vyāhṛtibhiḥ |
3.17.d: स ब्रह्मा प्राङ् उदेत्य स्रुवेणाग्नीध्र आज्यं जुहुयाद् भूर् भुवस् स्वर् इत्य् एताभिर् व्याहृतिभिः ।
3.17.e: That SraAwaw-priest going up toward the east should offer the sacrificial butter with a ladle in the dgnidhra, with these exclamations: bhus, bhtivas, svar.
3.17.m: That brahman priest, having stepped forward to the east, should offer melted butter in the Āgnīdhra fire with the dipping spoon, with these mystic utterances: 'bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ.'

3.17.s: etā vai vyāhṛtayas sarvaprāyaścittayaḥ tad yathā lavaṇena suvarṇaṃ saṃdadhyāt suvarṇena rajataṃ rajatena trapu trapuṇā lohāyasaṃ lohāyasena kārṣṇāyasaṃ kārṣṇāyasena dāru dāru ca carma ca śleṣmaṇaivam evaivaṃ vidvāṃs tat sarvam bhiṣajyati |
3.17.d: एता वै व्याहृतयस् सर्वप्रायश्चित्तयः तद् यथा लवणेन सुवर्णं संदध्यात् सुवर्णेन रजतं रजतेन त्रपु त्रपुणा लोहायसं लोहायसेन कार्ष्णायसं कार्ष्णायसेन दारु दारु च चर्म च श्लेष्मणैवम् एवैवं विद्वांस् तत् सर्वम् भिषज्यति ।
3.17.e: For these exclamations expiate everything. As one would mend gold with salt, silver with gold, tin with silver, copper with tin, iron with copper, wood with iron, wood and leather with glue, even so one knowing thus cures everything,
3.17.m:
These mystic utterances are indeed the universal atonements.
Just as one would join gold with salt-flux, silver with gold, tin with silver, lead with tin, iron with lead, wood with iron, and wood and leather with glue, even so one who knows thus heals all that.

3.17.s: tad āhur yad ahauṣīn me grahān me 'grahīd ity adhvaryave dakṣiṇā nayanty aśaṃsīn me vaṣaḍ akar ma iti hotra udagāsīn ma ity udgātre 'tha kiṃ cakruṣe brahmaṇe tūṣṇīm āsīnāya samāvatīr evetarair ṛtvigbhir dakṣiṇā nayantīti |
3.17.d: तद् आहुर् यद् अहौषीन् मे ग्रहान् मे ऽग्रहीद् इत्य् अध्वर्यवे दक्षिणा नयन्त्य् अशंसीन् मे वषड् अकर् म इति होत्र उदगासीन् म इत्य् उद्गात्रे ऽथ किं चक्रुषे ब्रह्मणे तूष्णीम् आसीनाय समावतीर् एवेतरैर् ऋत्विग्भिर् दक्षिणा नयन्तीति ।
3.17.e: This they say: " If with the words: 'He hath offered for me, he hath dipped the dippings for me,' they lead the sacrificial gifts to the adhvaryu; if with the words: 'He hath sung the s^astra for me, he hath uttered the vasatior me,'to the hotar; if with the words: 'He hath sung 178 //. (h'M, the udgītha for me,' to the udgdtar—now then to the brahman having done what, while he sat in silence, do they lead just as large sacrificial gifts as to the other priests?"
3.17.m: Regarding this they say: 'They lead the sacrificial gift to the adhvaryu, [thinking] "He offered for me, he took the cups for me"; to the hotṛ, [thinking] "He recited for me, he uttered the vaṣaṭ-call for me"; to the udgātṛ, [thinking] "He chanted for me." Now, for what action do they lead to the brahman priest, who sits silently, sacrificial gifts equal to those of the other priests?'

3.17.s: sa brūyād ardhabhāg gha vai sa yajñasyārdhaṃ hy eṣa yajñasya vahatīti ardhā ha sma vai purā brahmaṇe dakṣiṇā nayantīti ardhā itarebhya ṛtvigbhyaḥ |
3.17.d: स ब्रूयाद् अर्धभाग् घ वै स यज्ञस्यार्धं ह्य् एष यज्ञस्य वहतीति अर्धा ह स्म वै पुरा ब्रह्मणे दक्षिणा नयन्तीति अर्धा इतरेभ्य ऋत्विग्भ्यः ।
3.17.e: Let him say: " He, indeed, shareth in half of the sacrifice, for he carrieth half of the sacrifice." Indeed they formerly used to lead half of the sacrificial gifts to the JraAwaw-priest, half to the other priests,
3.17.m:
He should say: 'He is indeed entitled to half of the sacrifice, for he carries half of the sacrifice.'
Formerly, indeed, they used to lead half of the sacrificial gifts to the brahman priest,
and half to the other priests.

3.17.s: tasyaiṣa śloko mayīdam manye bhuvanādi sarvam mayi lokā mayi diśaś catasraḥ mayīdam manye nimiṣad yad ejati mayy āpa oṣadhayaś ca sarvā iti |
3.17.d: तस्यैष श्लोको मयीदम् मन्ये भुवनादि सर्वम् मयि लोका मयि दिशश् चतस्रः मयीदम् मन्ये निमिषद् यद् एजति मय्य् आप ओषधयश् च सर्वा इति ।
3.17.e: Of this there is the following ploka: " In me, I think, is this whole creation etc., in me the worlds, in me the four quarters; ill me, I think, is that twinkling thing which stirs, in me the waters and all the herbs."

3.17.s: mayīdam manye bhuvanādi sarvam ity evaṃvidaṃ ha vāvedaṃ sarvam bhuvanam anvāyattam |
3.17.d: मयीदम् मन्ये भुवनादि सर्वम् इत्य् एवंविदं ह वावेदं सर्वम् भुवनम् अन्वायत्तम् ।
3.17.e: 'In me, I think, is the whole creation etc.:' for on one knowing thus this whole creation is dependent. 8. * In me the worlds, in me the four quarters:' for in one knowing thus are the worlds, in one knowing thus the four quarters.
3.17.m: As for 'In me I think is this all, beginning with the world', this whole world is indeed dependent on the one who knows thus.

3.17.s: mayi lokā mayi diśaś catasra ity evaṃvidi ha vāva lokā evaṃvidi diśaś catasraḥ |
3.17.d: मयि लोका मयि दिशश् चतस्र इत्य् एवंविदि ह वाव लोका एवंविदि दिशश् चतस्रः ।
3.17.m: As for 'In me are the worlds, in me the four quarters', in the one who knows thus are indeed the worlds; in the one who knows thus are the four quarters.

3.17.s: mayīdam manye nimiṣad yad ejati mayy āpa oṣadhayaś ca sarvā ity evaṃvidi ha vāvedaṃ sarvam bhuvanam pratiṣṭhitam |
3.17.d: मयीदम् मन्ये निमिषद् यद् एजति मय्य् आप ओषधयश् च सर्वा इत्य् एवंविदि ह वावेदं सर्वम् भुवनम् प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
3.17.e: ' In me that twinkling thing which stirs, in me the waters and all the herbs:' for in one knowing thus this whole creation has its support,
3.17.m: As for 'In me I think is this which blinks and moves; in me are the waters and all the plants', on the one who knows thus this whole world is indeed established.

3.17.s: tasmād u haivaṃvidam eva brahmāṇaṃ kurvīta sa ha vāva brahmā ya evaṃ veda | caturthe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.17.d: तस्माद् उ हैवंविदम् एव ब्रह्माणं कुर्वीत स ह वाव ब्रह्मा य एवं वेद । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
3.17.e: And therefore one should make one knowing thus a brahman-ipnest. He indeed is a brahman-priest who knows thus.
3.17.m:
Therefore one should make only one who knows thus the brahman priest.
He indeed is the brahman priest who knows thus.
Third subsection in the fourth lesson.

3.18.e: Now from here [about] the after-verses of the stomabhdgas.
3.18.m: Now further, then, [are] the accompanying formulas of the share-of-praise-chants.

3.18.s: tad dhaitad eke stomabhāgair evānumantrayante tat tathā na kuryāt |
3.18.d: तद् धैतद् एके स्तोमभागैर् एवानुमन्त्रयन्ते तत् तथा न कुर्यात् ।
3.18.e: Now some recite the after-verses just with the stomabhdgas. One should not do that.
3.18.m:
In this regard, some accompany [the chants] with the shares-of-praise-chants themselves.
One should not do it in that way.

3.18.s: devena savitrā prasūtaḥ prastotar devebhyo vācam iṣyety u haike 'numantrayante savitā vai devānām prasavitā savitrā prasūtā idam anumantrayāmaha iti vadantaḥ tad u tathā na kuryāt |
3.18.d: देवेन सवित्रा प्रसूतः प्रस्तोतर् देवेभ्यो वाचम् इष्येत्य् उ हैके ऽनुमन्त्रयन्ते सविता वै देवानाम् प्रसविता सवित्रा प्रसूता इदम् अनुमन्त्रयामह इति वदन्तः तद् उ तथा न कुर्यात् ।
3.18.e: And some recite the after-verses [with this]: " Impelled by god Savitar, O prastotar, send [thy] speech to the gods," saying: " Savitar, verily, is the impeller of the gods; we recite this after-verse impelled by Savitar." One should not do that either.
3.18.m:
Some accompany with: 'Impelled by the god Savitṛ, O prastotṛ, send forth speech to the gods!', saying: 'Savitṛ is indeed the impeller among the gods; impelled by Savitṛ, we accompany this.'
One should not do it in that way either.

3.18.s: bhūr bhuvas svar ity u haike 'numantrayanta eṣā vai trayī vidyā trayyaivedaṃ vidyayānumantrayāmaha iti vadantaḥ tad u tathā no eva kuryāt |
3.18.d: भूर् भुवस् स्वर् इत्य् उ हैके ऽनुमन्त्रयन्त एषा वै त्रयी विद्या त्रय्यैवेदं विद्ययानुमन्त्रयामह इति वदन्तः तद् उ तथा नो एव कुर्यात् ।
3.18.e: And some recite the after-verse [with] bhUs, bhuvas, svar, saying: " Verily, this is the threefold knowledge; we now recite this after-verse with the threefold knowledge." One should not do that either,
3.18.m:
And some accompany with: 'bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ', saying: 'This is indeed the threefold knowledge; with the threefold knowledge we accompany this.'
One should by no means do it in that way either.

3.18.e: One should recite the after-verse [saying] only om.

3.18.s: athaiṣa vasiṣṭhasyaikastomabhāgānumantraḥ tena haitena vasiṣṭhaḥ prajātikāmo 'numantrayāṃ cakre devena savitrā prasūtaḥ prastotar devebhyo vācam iṣya bhūr bhuvas svar om iti tato vai sa bahuḥ prajayā paśubhiḥ prājāyata |
3.18.d: अथैष वसिष्ठस्यैकस्तोमभागानुमन्त्रः तेन हैतेन वसिष्ठः प्रजातिकामो ऽनुमन्त्रयां चक्रे देवेन सवित्रा प्रसूतः प्रस्तोतर् देवेभ्यो वाचम् इष्य भूर् भुवस् स्वर् ओम् इति ततो वै स बहुः प्रजया पशुभिः प्राजायत ।
3.18.e: Now this is Vasistha's onlj'^ stomabhdga-aiter-verse. With this same Vasistha, desirous of offspring, recited the after-verses: " Impelled by god Savitar, O prastotar, send [thy] speech to the gods; bhUs, bhuvas, svar, om,." Thereby he was greatly propagated through progeny [and] cattle.
3.18.m:
Now, this is Vasiṣṭha's accompanying formula of the single share-of-the-praise-chant.
Desiring offspring, Vasiṣṭha accompanied with this: 'Impelled by the god Savitṛ, O prastotṛ, send forth speech to the gods: bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ, om!'
Thence indeed he was abundantly propagated with offspring and cattle.

3.18.s: sa eva tena vasiṣṭhasyaikastomabhāgānumantreṇānumantrayeta bahur eva prajayā paśubhiḥ prajāyate iyaṃ tv eva sthitir om ity evānumantrayeta | caturthe 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.18.d: स एव तेन वसिष्ठस्यैकस्तोमभागानुमन्त्रेणानुमन्त्रयेत बहुर् एव प्रजया पशुभिः प्रजायते इयं त्व् एव स्थितिर् ओम् इत्य् एवानुमन्त्रयेत । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
3.18.e: Let him recite the afterverse with this one s*om«Ma^a-after-verse of Vasistha; he is greatly propagated through progeny [and] cattle. But this is the rule: let him recite the after-verse with om only.
3.18.m:
If he should accompany with that single accompanying formula of the share-of-the-praise-chant belonging to Vasiṣṭha, he is abundantly propagated with offspring and cattle.
However, this settled rule is: one should accompany with 'om' alone.
Fourth subsection in the fourth lesson.

3.19.s: athaiṣa vācā vajram udgṛhṇāti yad āha somaḥ pavata iti vopāvartadhvam iti vā vācaiva tad vāco vajraṃ vigṛhyate vācas satyenātimucyate tasmād om ity evānumantrayeta |
3.19.d: अथैष वाचा वज्रम् उद्गृह्णाति यद् आह सोमः पवत इति वोपावर्तध्वम् इति वा वाचैव तद् वाचो वज्रं विगृह्यते वाचस् सत्येनातिमुच्यते तस्माद् ओम् इत्य् एवानुमन्त्रयेत ।
3.19.e: Now with speech he takes up a thunderbolt. In that he says either " Soma cleanses itself " or " Turn ye hither," thereby with speech that thunderbolt of speech is taken apart (?), by the truth of speech he is released. Therefore he should recite the after-verse [saying] om only. 2, Verily the gods •with this threefold [knowledge] rich in sap ascended upwards to the heavenly world. They, being afraid lest men should come after [them], pressed the threefold knowledge (Veda).
3.19.m:
Now here, he lifts up the thunderbolt with speech.
When he says, 'The soma purifies itself', or 'Turn toward [us]', that thunderbolt of speech is grasped by speech itself; it is released through the truth of speech.
Therefore one should accompany with 'om' alone.

3.19.s: devā vā anayā trayyā sarasayordhvās svargaṃ lokam udakrāman te mamuṣyāṇām anvāgamād bibhyatas trayaṃ vedam apīḷayan |
3.19.d: देवा वा अनया त्रय्या सरसयोर्ध्वास् स्वर्गं लोकम् उदक्रामन् ते ममुष्याणाम् अन्वागमाद् बिभ्यतस् त्रयं वेदम् अपीऌअयन् ।
3.19.m:
The gods, full of sap, mounted upward to the heavenly world by this threefold [knowledge].
Fearing the following after of human beings, they compressed the threefold veda.

3.19.s: tasya pīḷayanta ekam evākṣaraṃ nāśaknuvan pīḷayitum om iti yad etat |
3.19.d: तस्य पीऌअयन्त एकम् एवाक्षरं नाशक्नुवन् पीऌअयितुम् ओम् इति यद् एतत् ।
3.19.e: Pressing it, they could not press one syllable of it; that was om.
3.19.m: As they pressed it, there was just one syllable they could not crush: this one, namely om.

3.19.s: eṣa u ha vāva sarasaḥ sarasā ha vā evaṃvidas trayī vidyā bhavati |
3.19.d: एष उ ह वाव सरसः सरसा ह वा एवंविदस् त्रयी विद्या भवति ।
3.19.e: Verily this is full of sap; full of sap becomes the threefold knowledge of one who knows thus. .■>. Verily what victory one wins, what thrift one thrives with the threefold knowledge full of sap, he wins that victory, he thrives that thrift, who knows thus.
3.19.m: And that indeed possesses the essence. Possessing the essence, truly, becomes the threefold knowledge of one who knows thus.

3.19.s: sa yāṃ ha vai trayyā vidyayā sarasayā jitiṃ jagati yām ṛddhim ṛdhnoti jayati tāṃ jitim ṛdhnoti tām ṛddhiṃ ya evaṃ veda |
3.19.d: स यां ह वै त्रय्या विद्यया सरसया जितिं जगति याम् ऋद्धिम् ऋध्नोति जयति तां जितिम् ऋध्नोति ताम् ऋद्धिं य एवं वेद ।
3.19.m: Whatever victory one wins by means of the threefold knowledge possessing the essence, whatever prosperity one attains, that victory he wins, that prosperity he attains, who knows thus.

3.19.s: etad dha vā akṣaraṃ trayyai vidyāyai pratiṣṭhā om iti vai hotā pratiṣṭhita om ity adhvaryur om ity udgātā |
3.19.d: एतद् ध वा अक्षरं त्रय्यै विद्यायै प्रतिष्ठा ओम् इति वै होता प्रतिष्ठित ओम् इत्य् अध्वर्युर् ओम् इत्य् उद्गाता ।
3.19.e: Verily this same syllable is the firm stand of the threefold knowledge. [Saying] om the hotar stands firm, [saying] om the adhvaryu, [saying] om the udgdtar.
3.19.m: This syllable indeed is the support of the threefold knowledge. With om the hotṛ is supported, with om the adhvaryu, with om the udgātṛ.

3.19.s: etad dha vā akṣaraṃ vedānāṃ triviṣṭapam etasmin vā akṣara ṛtvijo yajamānam ādhāya svarge loke samudūhanti tasmād om ity evānumantrayeta | caturthe 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ caturtho 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
3.19.d: एतद् ध वा अक्षरं वेदानां त्रिविष्टपम् एतस्मिन् वा अक्षर ऋत्विजो यजमानम् आधाय स्वर्गे लोके समुदूहन्ति तस्माद् ओम् इत्य् एवानुमन्त्रयेत । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः चतुर्थो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
3.19.e: Verily this same syllable is the triple heaven (?) of the Vedas. The priests having placed the sacrificer in this syllable can-y him up together into the heavenly world. Therefore he should recite the afterverse [saying] om only.
3.19.m: This syllable indeed is the summit of the Vedas. Placing the sacrificer in this syllable, the priests carry him up to the heavenly world. Therefore one should recite the responding chant with om alone. / Fifth khaṇḍa in the fourth anuvāka. / The fourth anuvāka is concluded.

3.20.s: guhāsi devo 'sy upavāsy upa taṃ vāyasva yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ |
3.20.d: गुहासि देवो ऽस्य् उपवास्य् उप तं वायस्व यो ऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मः ।
3.20.e: "Thou art in secret, thou art a god, thou art onblowing; blow on him who hates us and whom we hate.
3.20.m: "You are a hiding place, you are a god; you blow near; blow away him who hates us and whom we hate.

3.20.s: mahināsi bahulāsi bṛhaty asi rohiṇy asy apannāsi |
3.20.d: महिनासि बहुलासि बृहत्य् असि रोहिण्य् अस्य् अपन्नासि ।
3.20.e: Thou art great, thou art abundant, thou art extended (brhatt), thou art ruddy, thou art not fallen,
3.20.m: You are great, you are abundant, you are vast, you are ascending, you are not fallen.

3.20.s: sambhūr devo 'si sam aham bhūyāsam ābhūtir asy ābhūyāsam bhūtir asi bhūyāsam |
3.20.d: सम्भूर् देवो ऽसि सम् अहम् भूयासम् आभूतिर् अस्य् आभूयासम् भूतिर् असि भूयासम् ।
3.20.e: Thou art a god coming into existence; may I come into existence. Thou art existence; may I exist. Thou art becoming; may I become.
3.20.m: You are the deity of whole becoming; may I become whole. You are coming into being; may I come into being. You are flourishing; may I flourish.

3.20.s: yās te prajā upadiṣṭā nāhaṃ tava tāḥ paryemi upa te tā diśāmi |
3.20.d: यास् ते प्रजा उपदिष्टा नाहं तव ताः पर्येमि उप ते ता दिशामि ।
3.20.e: What offspring of thee is declared, that [offspring] of thee I do not comprehend (?). That [offspring] of thee I declare.
3.20.m: Whatever creatures of yours have been assigned, I do not bypass them of yours; I assign them to you.

3.20.s: nāma me śarīram me pratiṣṭhā me tan me tvayi tan me mopahṛthā itīmām pṛthivīm avocat |
3.20.d: नाम मे शरीरम् मे प्रतिष्ठा मे तन् मे त्वयि तन् मे मोपहृथा इतीमाम् पृथिवीम् अवोचत् ।
3.20.e: My name, my body, my foundation: that of me is in thee. Do not take that of me unto thee," thus he said to this earth.
3.20.m: My name, my body, my support—that of mine is in you; do not take that away from me," so he addressed this earth.

3.20.s: tam iyam āgatam pṛthivī pratinandaty ayaṃ te bhagavo lokaḥ saha nāv ayaṃ loka iti |
3.20.d: तम् इयम् आगतम् पृथिवी प्रतिनन्दत्य् अयं ते भगवो लोकः सह नाव् अयं लोक इति ।
3.20.e: Him having come this earth joyfully receives [saying]: " Thine, 0 reverend sir, is this world. This world is ours in common."
3.20.m: This earth welcomes him as he arrives: "This, venerable sir, is your world; this world belongs to us both together."

3.20.s: yad vāva me tvayīty āha tad vāva me punar dehīti |
3.20.d: यद् वाव मे त्वयीत्य् आह तद् वाव मे पुनर् देहीति ।
3.20.e: " Verily what of me is in thee," he says, "give that back to me."
3.20.m: "Whatever of mine is in you," he says, "give that very thing back to me."

3.20.s: kiṃ nu te mayīti nāma me śarīram me pratiṣṭhā me tan me tvayi tan me punar dehīti tad asmā iyam pṛthivī punar dadāti |
3.20.d: किं नु ते मयीति नाम मे शरीरम् मे प्रतिष्ठा मे तन् मे त्वयि तन् मे पुनर् देहीति तद् अस्मा इयम् पृथिवी पुनर् ददाति ।
3.20.e: " What now of thee is there in me?" " My name, my body, my foundation. That of me is in thee; give that back to me." That this earth gives back to him.
3.20.m: "What then of yours is in me?" "My name, my body, my support—that of mine is in you; give that back to me." This earth gives that back to him.

3.20.s: tām āha pra mā vāheti kim abhīti agnim iti tam agnim abhipravahati |
3.20.d: ताम् आह प्र मा वाहेति किम् अभीति अग्निम् इति तम् अग्निम् अभिप्रवहति ।
3.20.e: He says to her: " Carry me forth." " To what?" " To Agni." She carries him forth to Agni.
3.20.m: He says to her: "Carry me forward!" "Towards what?" "Towards Agni." She carries him forward to Agni.

3.20.s: so 'gnim āhābhijid asy abhijayyāsam lokajid asi lokaṃ jayyāsam attir asy annam adyāsam annādo bhavati yas tvaivaṃ veda |
3.20.d: सो ऽग्निम् आहाभिजिद् अस्य् अभिजय्यासम् लोकजिद् असि लोकं जय्यासम् अत्तिर् अस्य् अन्नम् अद्यासम् अन्नादो भवति यस् त्वैवं वेद ।
3.20.e: He says to Agni: "Victorious art thou, may 1 be victorious; world-conquering art thou, may I conquer the world; eating art thou, may I eat food; food-eating becomes he who knoweth thee thus. ii. = s. 12. = 4.
3.20.m: He says to Agni: "You are the winner of victory, may I win victory. You are the winner of the world, may I win the world. You are the eater, may I eat food." An eater of food he becomes who knows thus.

3.20.s: sambhūr devo 'si sam aham bhūyāsam ābhūtir asy ābhūyāsam bhūtir asi bhūyāsam |
3.20.d: सम्भूर् देवो ऽसि सम् अहम् भूयासम् आभूतिर् अस्य् आभूयासम् भूतिर् असि भूयासम् ।
3.20.m: "You are the deity of whole becoming; may I become whole. You are coming into being; may I come into being. You are flourishing; may I flourish.

3.20.s: yās te prajā upadiṣṭā nāhaṃ tava tāḥ paryemi upa te tā diśāmi |
3.20.d: यास् ते प्रजा उपदिष्टा नाहं तव ताः पर्येमि उप ते ता दिशामि ।
3.20.m: Whatever creatures of yours have been assigned, I do not bypass them of yours; I assign them to you.

3.20.s: tapo me tejo me 'nnam me vāṅ me tan me tvayi tan me mopahṛthā ity agnim avocat |
3.20.d: तपो मे तेजो मे ऽन्नम् मे वाङ् मे तन् मे त्वयि तन् मे मोपहृथा इत्य् अग्निम् अवोचत् ।
3.20.e: " My penance, my splendor, my food, my speech, that of me is in thee. That of me do not take unto thee," he says to Agni.
3.20.m: My heat, my brilliance, my food, my speech—that of mine is in you; do not take that away from me," so he addressed Agni.

3.20.s: taṃ tathaivāgatam agniḥ pratinandaty ayaṃ te bhagavo lokas saha nāv ayaṃ loka iti |
3.20.d: तं तथैवागतम् अग्निः प्रतिनन्दत्य् अयं ते भगवो लोकस् सह नाव् अयं लोक इति ।
3.20.e: Him having come thus Agni joyfully receives [saying]: "Thine, O reverend sir, is this world. This world is ours in common." 15. = 7.
3.20.m: Agni welcomes him in the very same way as he arrives: "This, venerable sir, is your world; this world belongs to us both together."

3.20.s: yad vāva me tvayīty āha tad vāva me punar dehīti |
3.20.d: यद् वाव मे त्वयीत्य् आह तद् वाव मे पुनर् देहीति ।
3.20.m: "Whatever of mine is in you," he says, "give that very thing back to me."

3.20.s: kiṃ nu te mayīti tapo me tejo me 'nnam me vāṅ me tan me tvayi tan me punar dehīti asmā agnir punar dadāti |
3.20.d: किं नु ते मयीति तपो मे तेजो मे ऽन्नम् मे वाङ् मे तन् मे त्वयि तन् मे पुनर् देहीति अस्मा अग्निर् पुनर् ददाति ।
3.20.e: " What now of thee is there in me?" "My penance, my splendor, my food, my speech. That of me is in thee; give that back to me." That Agni gives back to him.
3.20.m: "What then of yours is in me?" "My heat, my brilliance, my food, my speech—that of mine is in you; give that back to me." Agni gives that back to him.

3.20.s: tam āha pra mā vaheti | pañcame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.20.d: तम् आह प्र मा वहेति । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
3.20.e: He says to him: "Carry me forth."
3.20.m: He says to him: "Carry me forward!" / First khaṇḍa in the fifth anuvāka.

3.21.s: kim abhīti vāyum iti taṃ vāyum abhipravahati |
3.21.d: किम् अभीति वायुम् इति तं वायुम् अभिप्रवहति ।
3.21.e: "To what?" "To Vayu." He carries him forth to Vayu.
3.21.m: "Towards what?" "Towards Vāyu." He carries him forward to Vāyu.

3.21.s: sa vāyum āha yat purastād vāsīndro rājā bhūto vāsi yad dakṣiṇato vāsīśāno bhūto vāsi yat paścād vāsi varuṇo rājā bhūto vāsi yad uttarato vāsi somo rājā bhūto vāsi yad upariṣṭād avavāsi prajāpatir bhūto 'vavāsi |
3.21.d: स वायुम् आह यत् पुरस्ताद् वासीन्द्रो राजा भूतो वासि यद् दक्षिणतो वासीशानो भूतो वासि यत् पश्चाद् वासि वरुणो राजा भूतो वासि यद् उत्तरतो वासि सोमो राजा भूतो वासि यद् उपरिष्टाद् अववासि प्रजापतिर् भूतो ऽववासि ।
3.21.e: He says to Vayu: "In that thou blowest from the front, thou blowest as king Indra. In that thou blowest from the right, thou blowest as the Lord. In that thou blowest from behind, thou blowest as king Varuna. In that thou blowest from the left, thou blowest as king Soma. In that thou blowest down from above, thou blowest down as Prajapati.
3.21.m: He says to Vāyu: "When you blow from the east, you blow having become King Indra. When you blow from the south, you blow having become Īśāna. When you blow from the west, you blow having become King Varuṇa. When you blow from the north, you blow having become King Soma. When you blow down from above, you blow down having become Prajāpati.

3.21.d: व्रात्यो ऽस्य् एकव्रात्यो ऽनवसृष्टो देवानाम् बिलम् अप्यधाः ।
3.21.e: Thou art the Vratya, the only Vratya, not released of the gods (?). Thou hast closed the opening.
3.21.m: You are a Vrātya, the sole Vrātya; unrestrained, you have stopped up the cavity of the gods.

3.21.s: tava prajās tavauṣadhayas tavāpo vicalitam anuvicalanti |
3.21.d: तव प्रजास् तवौषधयस् तवापो विचलितम् अनुविचलन्ति ।
3.21.e: The progeny, the herbs, the waters follow after thy departing, s. = 20. s. 8. = 20. 4.
3.21.m: Your creatures, your plants, your waters move along after [your] movement.

3.21.s: sambhūr devo 'si sam aham bhūyāsam ābhūtir asy ābhūyāsam bhūtir asi bhūyāsam |
3.21.d: सम्भूर् देवो ऽसि सम् अहम् भूयासम् आभूतिर् अस्य् आभूयासम् भूतिर् असि भूयासम् ।
3.21.m: You are the deity of whole becoming; may I become whole. You are coming into being; may I come into being. You are flourishing; may I flourish.

3.21.s: yās te prajā upadiṣṭā nāhaṃ tava tāḥ paryemi upa te tā diśāmi |
3.21.d: यास् ते प्रजा उपदिष्टा नाहं तव ताः पर्येमि उप ते ता दिशामि ।
3.21.m: Whatever creatures of yours have been assigned, I do not bypass them of yours; I assign them to you.

3.21.s: prāṇāpānau me śrutam me tan me tvayi tan me mopahṛthā iti vāyum avocat |
3.21.d: प्राणापानौ मे श्रुतम् मे तन् मे त्वयि तन् मे मोपहृथा इति वायुम् अवोचत् ।
3.21.e: My breath and exhalation, my learning, that of me is in thee. That of me do not take unto thyself," he said to Vayu.
3.21.m: My out-breath and in-breath, my hearing—that of mine is in you; do not take that away from me," so he addressed Vāyu.

3.21.s: taṃ tathaivāgataṃ vāyuḥ pratinandaty ayaṃ te bhagavo lokaḥ saha nāv ayaṃ loka iti |
3.21.d: तं तथैवागतं वायुः प्रतिनन्दत्य् अयं ते भगवो लोकः सह नाव् अयं लोक इति ।
3.21.e: Him having come thus Vayu joyfully receives [saying]: " Thine is this world, reverend sir. This world is ours in common." 9. = 20. 7.
3.21.m: Vāyu welcomes him in the very same way as he arrives: "This, venerable sir, is your world; this world belongs to us both together."

3.21.s: yad vāva me tvayīty āha tad vāva me punar dehīti |
3.21.d: यद् वाव मे त्वयीत्य् आह तद् वाव मे पुनर् देहीति ।
3.21.m: "Whatever of mine is in you," he says, "give that very thing back to me."

3.21.s: kiṃ nu te mayīti prāṇāpānau me śrutam me tan me tvayi tan me punar dehīti tad asmai vāyuḥ punar dadāti |
3.21.d: किं नु ते मयीति प्राणापानौ मे श्रुतम् मे तन् मे त्वयि तन् मे पुनर् देहीति तद् अस्मै वायुः पुनर् ददाति ।
3.21.e: " What now of thee is there in me?" " My breath and exhalation, my learning. That of me is in thee. Give that back to me." That Vayu gives back to him.
3.21.m: "What then of yours is in me?" "My out-breath and in-breath, my hearing—that of mine is in you; give that back to me." Vāyu gives that back to him.

3.21.s: tam āha pra mā vaheti kim abhīti antarikṣalokam iti tam antarikṣalokam abhipravahati |
3.21.d: तम् आह प्र मा वहेति किम् अभीति अन्तरिक्षलोकम् इति तम् अन्तरिक्षलोकम् अभिप्रवहति ।
3.21.e: He says to him: " Carry me forth." " To what?" " To the world of the atmosphere." He carries him to the world of the atmosphere.
3.21.m: He says to him: "Carry me forward!" "Towards what?" "Towards the world of the intermediate space." He carries him forward to the world of the intermediate space.

3.21.s: taṃ tathaivāgatam antarikṣalokaḥ pratinandaty ayaṃ te bhagavo lokaḥ saha nāv ayaṃ loka iti |
3.21.d: तं तथैवागतम् अन्तरिक्षलोकः प्रतिनन्दत्य् अयं ते भगवो लोकः सह नाव् अयं लोक इति ।
3.21.e: Ilim having come thus the world of the atmosphere joyfully receives [saying]: " Thine is this world, reverend sir. This world belongs to both of us in common." i». = 20. 7.
3.21.m: The world of the intermediate space welcomes him in the very same way as he arrives: "This, venerable sir, is your world; this world belongs to us both together."

3.21.s: yad vāva me tvayīty āha tad vāva me punar dehīti |
3.21.d: यद् वाव मे त्वयीत्य् आह तद् वाव मे पुनर् देहीति ।
3.21.e: " What now of thee is there in me?" " This space of mine. That of me is in thee. Give that back to me." That space the world of the atmosphere gives back to him.
3.21.m: "Whatever of mine is in you," he says, "give that very thing back to me."

3.21.s: kiṃ nu te mayīti ayam ma ākāśaḥ sa me tvayi tan me punar dehīti tam asmā ākāśam antarikṣalokaḥ punar dadāti |
3.21.d: किं नु ते मयीति अयम् म आकाशः स मे त्वयि तन् मे पुनर् देहीति तम् अस्मा आकाशम् अन्तरिक्षलोकः पुनर् ददाति ।
3.21.e: He says to it: " Carry me forth."
3.21.m: "What then of yours is in me?" "This space of mine, that is in you; give that back to me." The world of the intermediate space gives that space back to him.

3.21.s: tam āha pra mā vaheti | pañcame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
3.21.d: तम् आह प्र मा वहेति । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
3.21.m: He says to it: "Carry me forward!" / Second khaṇḍa in the fifth anuvāka.

3.22.s: kim abhīti diśa iti taṃ diśo 'bhipravahati |
3.22.d: किम् अभीति दिश इति तं दिशो ऽभिप्रवहति ।
3.22.e: "To what?" "To the quarters." It carries him forth to the quarters,
3.22.m: "Towards what?" "Towards the directions." It carries him forward to the directions.

3.22.s: taṃ tathaivāgataṃ diśaḥ pratinandanty ayaṃ te bhagavo lokaḥ saha no 'yaṃ loka iti |
3.22.d: तं तथैवागतं दिशः प्रतिनन्दन्त्य् अयं ते भगवो लोकः सह नो ऽयं लोक इति ।
3.22.e: Him having come thus the quarters joyfully receive [saying]: "Thine is this world, reverend sir. This world is ours in common." s. = 20. 7.* 4. "What now of thee is there in us?" " Hearing." That hearing the quarters give back to him.
3.22.m: The directions welcome him in the very same way as he arrives: "This, venerable sir, is your world; this world belongs to us together."

3.22.s: yad vāva me yuṣmāsv ity āha tad vāva me punar datteti |
3.22.d: यद् वाव मे युष्मास्व् इत्य् आह तद् वाव मे पुनर् दत्तेति ।
3.22.e: He says to them: " Carry me forth." " To what?" " To the world of day and night." They carry him to the world of day and night,
3.22.m: "Whatever of mine is in you," he says, "give that very thing back to me."

3.22.s: kiṃ nu te 'smāsv iti śrotram iti tad asmai śrotraṃ diśaḥ punar dadati |
3.22.d: किं नु ते ऽस्मास्व् इति श्रोत्रम् इति तद् अस्मै श्रोत्रं दिशः पुनर् ददति ।
3.22.m: "What then of yours is in us?" "The sense of hearing." The directions give that sense of hearing back to him.

3.22.s: tā āha pra mā vahateti kim abhīti ahorātrayor lokam iti tam ahorātrayor lokam abhipravahanti |
3.22.d: ता आह प्र मा वहतेति किम् अभीति अहोरात्रयोर् लोकम् इति तम् अहोरात्रयोर् लोकम् अभिप्रवहन्ति ।
3.22.m: He says to them: "Carry me forward!" "Towards what?" "Towards the world of day and night." They carry him forward to the world of day and night.

3.22.s: taṃ tathaivāgatam ahorātre pratinandato 'yaṃ te bhagavo lokaḥ saha no 'yaṃ loka iti |
3.22.d: तं तथैवागतम् अहोरात्रे प्रतिनन्दतो ऽयं ते भगवो लोकः सह नो ऽयं लोक इति ।
